Because Cancel can't negate his invulnerability, it must be a PHYSICAL mutation, his body mimicking the properties of a specific metal (a superior variant of Frank's power), likely an Orange Elixir, and a very strong one. But that alone doesn't explain how he moves in stopped time or resists most powers, so Ryan concludes the metal itself has unique, anomalous properties. Livia notes both she and her father can wield two powers with no side-effects, a secret Ryan wants for a Psycho cure and which Dynamis wanted for an army (she refused them).

facts.value: Invulnerability is a physical mutation, not energy-based
Body likely mimics a metal (strong Orange), like Frank's power
The metal has anomalous properties (moves in stopped time)
He and Livia wield two powers without side-effects
Dynamis wanted that secret for an army; Livia refused

wikiObservations.name: Livia Augusti
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: meets 'President' Ryan at Deadland Motel and, after Luigi confirms his time-traveler tale is true, hands over Len's uncorrupted brain-map FREELY, no fetch quest or blackmail, honoring her past self's debt ('I'm the one with a debt, and I'm clearing it off the books'). She fully commits to partnership toward a 'perfect ending,' offering to help investigate why she and her father wield two powers without side-effects (for a cure, though she refused Dynamis the same for an army). Her limits: she can only give Ryan a week or two before her family retakes Rust Town; she wants Augustus retired, not dead ('he's still my father'); and she's in denial over Felix's truth, planning to use this doomed loop to try to win him back. She warns Ryan that Augusti members are dying in mysterious assassinations (the Shroud).

facts.value: Gives Ryan Len's clean brain-map freely, honoring a debt
Commits to partnership toward a 'perfect ending'
Will help probe the two-powers secret for a cure
Wants Augustus retired, not dead; in denial over Felix
Warns of mysterious Augusti assassinations (Shroud)

wikiObservations.name: Luigi the Hockey Victim
wikiObservations.summary: An Augusti truth-teller whose power forces others to speak truth and detects lies. Livia has him verify Ryan's confession; Ryan, whose favorite pastime is beating Luigi with a hockey stick across loops, spitefully rants the whole truth at him (time travel, Darkling, the doomed loop, 'you don't matter'). The revelation triggers an existential crisis (Livia notes her power gave him a 1-in-3 chance of suicide). To contain the leak she pays him 20 million euros to leave New Rome immediately and never speak of it, even to Augustus, on pain of consequences. He flees the city.

facts.value: Augusti truth-teller: compels truth, detects lies
Verifies Ryan's confession for Livia
Ryan's recurring hockey-stick victim across loops
Suffers an existential crisis from the revelation
Paid 20M euros and exiled to keep the secret

wikiObservations.name: Psyshock
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: killed for good. 'President' Ryan delivers the drugged brainjacker to Livia as a peace gift; Cancel negates his power so his death sticks, and Mortimer shoots him twice in the head in the parking lot, freeing his thralls (who wake with no memory of their enslavement). His final cruelty: on his way out he deliberately scrambled Len's brain, leaving her an unresponsive vegetable even though Ryan beat him, so she can't recover without Alchemo's help.

facts.value: Delivered drugged to Livia as a peace gift
Killed by Mortimer after Cancel negates his power
His death frees and restores his surviving thralls
Scrambled Len's brain on the way out, leaving her a vegetable
Forces Ryan to rely on Alchemo to restore Len

wikiObservations.name: The Shroud
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: without Ryan to talk him out of it, the invisible Carnival assassin ('Mr. See-Through') has begun a lone assassination spree, killing Augusti members with bombs and hits, which is why Livia's people are dying mysteriously. He saw Ryan among the Meta-Gang and assumed he turned Psycho, so his harbor hideout nearly blows up in Ryan's face when Ryan tries to visit. This means the Carnival may now target Ryan too, and the Shroud is likely to bomb Jamie Cutter, Lanka, and Ki-jung's apartment again as he did in a prior loop.

facts.value: Invisible Carnival assassin ('Mr. See-Through')
Begins a lone spree killing Augusti with bombs/hits
Thinks Ryan turned Psycho after seeing him with the Meta-Gang
Nearly blows up Ryan at his harbor hideout
Likely to bomb Cutter/Lanka/Ki-jung's apartment again

wikiObservations.name: Mosquito
wikiObservations.summary: A Meta-Gang Psycho, a giant humanoid mosquito ('bugman') too big for a normal car. He foolishly drank a second Green Elixir (the Hercules super-strength knockoff), wrongly thinking a same-color Elixir would overwrite his first power; instead it stacked, and his super-strength only works once he's gorged on blood, weakening every minute after. After the takeover he serves 'President' Ryan as a wary minion, voicing doubts about war with Dynamis before Ryan cows him back into the 'silent majority.'

facts.value: Giant humanoid mosquito Meta-Gang Psycho
Drank a second Green (Hercules) hoping to overwrite the first
Super-strength only after gorging on blood, then fades
Serves President Ryan as a nervous minion
Cowed out of dissenting on the Dynamis war

wikiObservations.name: Alchemo
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: a brass-and-steel cyborg Genius whose head is a brain-in-a-jar dome and whose fingers are syringes; an amoral mad scientist specialized in brain/neuro tech, kept ethical only by his daughter the Doll. He arrives in a 1986 Fleetwood Bounder RV loaded with his workshop. He can't repair Dynamis's booby-trapped transfer machine (the sabotage is in essential parts) but can reverse-engineer and build his own that works, if he gets a Genius workshop and matter replicator, which the bunker's mainframe (a 'Universal Brain,' a device he always wanted to build) could provide. He treats Acid Rain's brain tumors/mutant neurons with cancer treatment and mood stabilizers (a temporary fix) and agrees to help Mongrel and cure Mechron-plague tumors, only because the Doll nagged him and it saves his own neurocomputers. He confirms Len won't wake on her own.

facts.value: Brass cyborg: brain-in-a-jar head, syringe fingers
Amoral neuro-genius, ethical only via the Doll
Can't fix Dynamis's machine but can build a working copy
Needs the bunker's Universal Brain / matter replicator
Treats Acid Rain's tumors; confirms Len won't wake alone

ties.rel: estranged former partner; owes a favor
will build machine to restore her

wikiObservations.name: The Doll
wikiObservations.summary: Tea: Alchemo's android daughter and Ryan's ex, a lifelike redhead gynoid dressed as a country-girl, now covered in synthetic skin. She slaps Ryan for two years of silence but can't hold a grudge, softening when he apologizes. From her view she and Ryan had a brief fling; from his (across erased loops) they were together for years, visited France, etc., a one-sided shared past that, with Alchemo's betrayal, drove Ryan to leave. She's the moral conscience ('Jiminy Cricket') who nags her amoral father into helping others (curing tumors from Mechron's plagues). She's gentle toward the comatose Len and grasps Ryan came to New Rome to find her.

facts.value: Alchemo's lifelike redhead android daughter; Ryan's ex
Slaps Ryan for two years of silence, then forgives
Shares a one-sided years-long erased past with Ryan
The moral conscience who makes Alchemo help others
Tender toward the comatose Len

wikiObservations.name: Toasty
wikiObservations.summary: Ryan's first sentient robot, an intelligent toaster on four little wheels with a vocalizer mimicking the Terminator's voice. Ryan built him during a 'robot-building phase' (before the Bahamut plushie), born of his anxiety about moving to France and waking to un-toastable bread. Unlike the others, Toasty bears Ryan no reproach and warmly missed him. He's crude and playful (jokes about 'toasting chicks'), lives on Alchemo's farm, and begs Ryan to upload his personality into Mechron's scorpion mech ('a giant robot is just a toaster with too much power'). Tea installed his wheels when he tired of watching TV.

facts.value: Ryan's first sentient robot: an intelligent toaster on wheels
Terminator-voiced vocalizer; crude and playful
Born of Ryan's fear of un-toastable French bread
Bears Ryan no grudge, unlike the others
Wants to be uploaded into Mechron's scorpion mech

ties.rel: lives with; wheels installed by Tea

wikiObservations.name: Hector Manada
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: the Dynamis CEO (whom Ryan likens to a Colombian cartel boss, 'Mr. Escobar') refuses to renew the knockoff-Elixir deal now that Ryan's Meta-Gang killed Psyshock. Revelation: the old alliance didn't collapse from the failed brain project, Psyshock had been secretly, insidiously taking over Dynamis by brainwashing staff and executives one by one, and his death exposed that treachery. Manada resists Ryan's blackmail (recordings, and Ryan's hint the knockoffs are 'Psycho-in-a-can' linked to Bloodstream/Lab Sixty-Six), calling his bluff. He offers one deal: Ryan keeps the knockoffs, releases the technicians, returns the tech, and leaves town in 48 hours, or he unleashes Il Migliore (Enrique and Wyvern are already pushing for it).

facts.value: Dynamis CEO; refuses to renew the knockoff deal
Psyshock had been secretly taking over Dynamis staff
His death exposed the Meta-Gang's true intentions
Calls Ryan's Bloodstream/Lab 66 blackmail bluff
Gives Ryan 48 hours to leave or faces Il Migliore

wikiObservations.name: Acid Rain
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: the captured Augusti-hunting Meta-Gang teleporter, strapped to an operating table in Ryan's infirmary, raving and building tolerance to sedation. Alchemo's scan reveals her head is full of tumors and mutant neurons from her Psycho condition, yet she still functions. She obsessively raves about 'the gate' and going 'all the way back', blaming Ryan for keeping 'them' away from her. Alchemo treats her with brain-cancer treatment and mood stabilizers, a temporary fix that stabilizes her mind while her condition keeps mutating. Ryan keeps her for questioning.

facts.value: Captured teleporter, restrained in Ryan's infirmary
Head full of tumors and mutant neurons; still functions
Building tolerance to sedation
Obsessively raves about 'the gate' and going 'back'
Temporarily stabilized by Alchemo's cancer treatment

wikiObservations.name: Universal Brain
wikiObservations.summary: The bunker's central control system, a biomechanical blue brain (a 'U.B.,' Universal Brain), which Alchemo identifies as the ultimate biomechanical data-storage device, something he always wanted to build but never had the resources for. It runs the bunker, continues Mechron's Elixir research posthumously, and whoever seizes it can hijack the base's full capabilities (robots, weapons, matter replicator, the Bahamut). Ryan plans a frontal assault on the mainframe to capture it, guided by the Architect's structural analysis; Alchemo agrees to hijack it if given access.

facts.value: The bunker's central biomechanical blue-brain control
'U.B.', the ultimate biomechanical data-storage device
Runs the base and continues Mechron's Elixir research
Seizing it grants control of the bunker's full arsenal
Ryan plans a mainframe assault; Alchemo can hijack it

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: Refined, the emotional payoff: Alchemo's rebuilt machine overwrites Len's brain with Livia's clean backup map and repairs the overuse damage. She wakes with full recognition, the elusive look Ryan waited centuries for, and rejoices 'Riri, it worked! The transfer worked!' She is herself again, remembering. Seeing Ryan collapse into tears under the lifted weight of his centuries of loneliness, she hugs him as she did in childhood and repeats the words he once gave her: 'You're not alone. You're not alone.' For the first time in his endless looping he is truly not alone.

facts.value: Restored via Alchemo's machine and Livia's clean map
Wakes with full recognition: 'Riri, it worked!'
Herself again, memories and love intact
Comforts a sobbing Ryan, mirroring their childhood
Tells him 'You're not alone,' his own past words to her

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: Refined, catharsis: after Len wakes restored and recognizes him, Ryan, who has carried centuries of buried loneliness, pain, and denial across Monaco and countless loops, finally breaks. He collapses to his knees and sobs uncontrollably, the crushing weight of time lifting, his 'shining armor' falling away to reveal the raw sadness beneath. Len holds him and tells him he's not alone, and for the first time since he began looping he believes it. Earlier he tells Little Sarah he and Len were teenage lovers. This run is his first true 'one-shot': its enabling flukes (Psyshock time-travel, Sarin's aid, Darkling) can never repeat.

facts.value: Breaks down sobbing when Len wakes and knows him
Centuries of buried loneliness finally surface
His knightly 'armor' falls away to raw grief
Believes 'you're not alone' for the first time
This unrepeatable run is his first true one-shot

ties.rel: tells of his past with Len

wikiObservations.name: The Bunker Hivemind
wikiObservations.summary: The mainframe's automated defense: swarms of cyclopean androids (single laser eyes), wall-mounted miniguns, eye-shaped submachine-gun drones, and gatling turrets, all pieces of a single learning hivemind rather than individual units. They coordinate flawlessly, avoid friendly fire, and adapt within minutes, countering Gemini's shadow-power with light manipulation and switching from dogpiling Frank (who absorbs metal) to laser volleys. They identify and prioritize key targets (Alchemo, then Ryan). The final guardian is a telekinetic Genome boss: a crimson-Elixir vat on six spider legs with a speck-sized Red portal, a true telekinetic that flattens the Reptilian.

facts.value: Cyclopean androids, drones, and turrets as one hivemind
Learns and counters powers within minutes
Coordinates without friendly fire; prioritizes key targets
Guarded by a telekinetic vat-boss on spider legs
Runs on Mechron's automated defense system

wikiObservations.name: Gemini
wikiObservations.summary: A Meta-Gang Psycho who appears as an ethereal woman of shining light, but whose true self is her tentacled shadow, an illusion masking the real killer. Her shadow can damage enemies by striking their shadows, inflicting the same wounds on their bodies. Deployed on Ryan's mainframe assault, she is countered by the learning hivemind, which brightens the lights and grabs her shadow with robot shadows; eight machines pin and dismember her shadow, and her light-body flickers out. Killed in the raid.

facts.value: Ethereal light-woman is illusion; tentacled shadow is real
Damages enemies by striking their shadows
Recruited into Ryan's Meta-Gang assault force
Countered and pinned by the hivemind's light/shadow trick
Dismembered and killed in the mainframe raid

wikiObservations.name: Wardrobe's Presidential Costume
wikiObservations.summary: A war-fashioned suit made by Wardrobe and delivered to Ryan in a black briefcase (the 'Nuclear Football'), pure black and red, unlike his earlier playful outfits. Cashmere red shirt and black Lagerfeld-style suit, leather boots with skull socks, velvet gloves, flowing jacket, a red-and-silver mask baring only the eyes, and a bowler hat. Ryan dons it ceremonially to establish 'stylish dominance' over his minions before the raid. Durable enough to survive his acrobatics without rupturing; a laser hole in its bowler hat infuriates him.

facts.value: War-suit by Wardrobe, delivered as the 'Nuclear Football'
Pure black and red; mask bares only the eyes
Worn to assert dominance before the mainframe raid
Durable, survives combat acrobatics
Its bowler hat is holed by a laser

wikiObservations.name: Alchemo
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: in the mainframe raid Alchemo is the mission-critical non-combatant, escorted through the hivemind gauntlet. Reaching the command room, he intertwines with the alien biomechanical brain exactly as Psyshock once did, nailing it with his syringe-fingers so blue lightning races through his exposed brain, and hijacks the Universal Brain, changing admin privileges to register the group as 'staff.' He gains access to Mechron's full database (Psychos, power-enhancement, Elixir mechanics) and is giddy: 'We're going to change the world, meatbag!' He then uses the bunker's replicator to build a working copy of the transfer machine, restores Len with Livia's map, and repairs her brain damage, calling it repayment of his favor.

facts.value: Escorted non-combatant through the raid
Interfaces with the Universal Brain via syringe-fingers
Registers the group as 'staff'; unlocks Mechron's database
Builds a working transfer machine from the replicator
Restores Len and repairs her brain, repaying his favor

wikiObservations.name: The Reptilian
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: a cowardly, dim Meta-Gang mook with enhanced senses (can feel ground vibrations) whom Ryan repeatedly cows with choking gestures to 'rediscover his patriotism.' In the mainframe raid he survives the first rooms by staying near Darkling, but when Ryan orders him to hold the line against the telekinetic vat-boss, the true-telekinetic machine lifts and slams him into the ceiling with crushing force, flattening him like a mosquito under a flyswatter. Killed in the raid.

facts.value: Cowardly mook with vibration-sensing senses
Cowed by Ryan's choking gestures
Survives early rooms by hiding near Darkling
Flattened against the ceiling by the telekinetic boss
Killed in the mainframe raid

wikiObservations.name: Acid Rain
wikiObservations.summary: Refined and humanized: Alchemo's treatment cures her madness, revealing her real self, Helen, a meek, guilt-ridden young woman horrified by the murderer she was. She reveals her power's mechanic: teleporting takes her through the Purple World, a corridor where everything goes violet and she sees a watching pyramid (the Violet Ultimate One) and hears voices; she perceives a 'pathway' inside Ryan that he keeps closed. Her tragic backstory: she lost her family to a mistake and sought a Violet Elixir to go back in time; when she found one meant for a friend, Adam caught her and force-fed it to her, shattering her into a Psycho. Ryan gently tells her he can't save her family but swears to help her. Her treatment is only temporary.

facts.value: Cured; real name Helen, now meek and remorseful
Teleports through the Purple World, seeing the watching pyramid
Perceives a closed 'pathway' inside Ryan
Sought a Violet Elixir to undo losing her family
Adam force-fed her the Elixir, making her a Psycho

wikiObservations.name: Mongrel
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: a Meta-Gang Psycho whose true power is stockpiling multiple Elixirs (inert by itself). Cured by Alchemo, he can now speak (his brain hurts as grey matter fills the tumor-voids) and recounts his fall: he found a White Elixir in Old Rome's ruins but couldn't activate his power, assumed it faulty, and drank a knockoff believing himself powerless, turning Psycho. He was a trash-scavenging animal when Adam found him. Grateful and reformed, he swears off Elixirs forever and offers to help Ryan find a permanent cure. His treatment, like Helen's, is temporary; Genome metabolism builds tolerance.

facts.value: Power: stockpiles multiple Elixirs (inert alone)
Cured by Alchemo; can now speak, brain aching
Drank a knockoff believing himself powerless, turned Psycho
Found by Adam scavenging trash
Swears off Elixirs; offers to help find a cure

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: recovered and clear-headed on Alchemo's superior antidepressants, Len sets up a Genius workshop in the bunker to maintain the brain-copying machine. She defines its key limit: it sends only one brain-map back per loop, requiring an unbroken rebuild-and-resend chain (one break and she forgets everything) unless memories are stored externally, which needs Livia. She warms to cooperating with Livia, who honored their bargain. When Ryan finally confesses he loves her and wants to settle down and have children, she gently declines romance ('I don't feel I'm ready... perhaps never') but insists he stay in her life, reframing them not as best friends but as family. She remains wary of the Meta-Gang Psychos.

facts.value: Recovered on Alchemo's antidepressants; runs a bunker workshop
Machine sends one brain-map per loop; needs an unbroken chain
Warms to cooperating with Livia for memory storage
Gently rejects Ryan's love but calls him family
Still distrusts the reformed Meta-Gang members

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: for the first time in centuries Ryan wakes genuinely happy and at peace, radiating uncharacteristic kindness (praising Frank, forgiving Acid Rain, sparing cruelty). Secure with his 'White House' and base, he plans to take New Rome before Manada's ultimatum expires, expecting a clash with Il Migliore and maybe the Carnival. He believes some Psychos are victims worth curing, not just monsters. He finally confesses his love to Len and asks to build a life with her; when she declines romance but offers family, he accepts it with hard-won dignity, having had centuries to process the feelings. All he ever truly wanted was to be remembered, and that wish is now fulfilled.

facts.value: Wakes at peace and uncharacteristically kind
Plans to take New Rome before Manada's ultimatum
Believes reformed Psychos deserve a cure
Confesses love to Len; accepts her 'family' answer
Content: his wish to be remembered is fulfilled

wikiObservations.name: The Brain-Copying Machine
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: Len's rebuilt transfer machine, the device that ended Ryan's centuries of loneliness by looping a companion with him. Its hard constraints define the endgame: it can send only one brain-map back in time per loop, so preserving memories requires an unbroken chain of rebuild-and-resend (a single break wipes the traveler's memories), unless an external memory store is used, which requires Livia (Blue Genome backup). Len lacks the tech to rebuild the scanner at her own base; it needs Vulcan's or the bunker's resources. Psyshock corrupted the earlier prototype, so a fresh one must be built each time.

facts.value: Sends only one brain-map back per loop
Needs an unbroken rebuild-and-resend chain to keep memories
External memory storage requires Livia
Requires Vulcan-grade or bunker tech to build
Prototype was corrupted by Psyshock

wikiObservations.name: Toasty
wikiObservations.summary: Refined: Ryan's sentient toaster robot continues his comic-relief antics, awkwardly flirting with the newly-cured Helen ('do you want me to toast your bread?... I've got butter'). He is eager for Ryan to install him into the big battle mech in the garage so he can finally 'show arms' and fight Wyvern, planned for the coming assault. His flirting is atrocious, as expected of a toaster.

facts.value: Sentient toaster robot; comic relief
Awkwardly flirts with cured Helen
Wants to be installed into the garage battle mech
Eager to fight Wyvern once armed

wikiObservations.name: Monaco
wikiObservations.summary: CH79 flashback (Ryan's early 'Perfect Run' to free Monaco): the pocket dimension's rules mapped precisely. The teleport effect triggers on crossing Monaco's legal frontier (airspace included, but NOT territorial waters, per old Franco-Monégasque treaty gaps) and fires either on approaching the Monte-Carlo, staying 2+ hours, or next falling asleep after having entered. It never releases a victim once entered. Animals teleport straight to the maze kitchens (not the marble entry hall). The effect does NOT apply to machines past the 2-hour limit. Damage self-repairs: doors reseal the instant they leave sight; a smuggled nuke's blast is undone by fresh rooms within 24 hours. The real Monte-Carlo is only the anchor on Earth; the true maze is a separate reality Jean-Stéphanie may have BECOME. Ryan proved even nuking the whole microstate (a French nuke on his drone) couldn't dispel the effect; it took him ~5 years of loops mastering particle physics to breach it.

facts.value: Teleport triggers on crossing frontier (air yes, waters no), 2hr stay, or next sleep
Animals go to the kitchens; machines are exempt past 2hr
Self-repairs: doors reseal off-sight; nuke damage undone in 24hr
Real Monte-Carlo is only the Earth anchor; true maze is a separate reality
Nuking the microstate did not dispel the effect

ties.rel: maze may be his very being

wikiObservations.name: Simon
wikiObservations.summary: CH79 flashback shows the run where Ryan actually SAVES Simon rather than losing him: Ryan reaches Room 44 with the French Foreign Legion password ('Français par le sang versé...'), reveals himself as an immortal, and plants a Resonator in Simon's lifelong tunnel to open the escape portal. After Ryan single-handedly massacres the entire clown army, Simon has refused to evacuate until Ryan (as 'part of everyone') leaves too. Here Simon SURVIVES, chooses to stay behind and fence off Monaco as its self-appointed border guard for the rest of his short life, and gives Ryan a parting gift: Nietzsche's 'Thus Spoke Zarathustra', pointing him to the concept of eternal recurrence he knows Ryan will 'like.' This is the origin of Ryan's guiding philosophy.

facts.value: Saved via Legion password and a Resonator in his tunnel
Refuses to leave until Ryan does ('you're part of everyone')
Survives; stays to fence off Monaco as border guard
Gifts Ryan Nietzsche's 'Thus Spoke Zarathustra' (eternal recurrence)

wikiObservations.name: Jean-Stéphanie
wikiObservations.summary: CH79 flashback: as Ryan breaches the maze, the loudspeaker 'voice' (Jean-Stéphanie or the maze itself) turns from obsequious to openly passive-aggressive and vengeful, announcing the Monte-Carlo will 'permanently close due to the Andorran invasion' and unleashing every clown, then wave after wave of circus minibosses (acrobats/ninjas, firecrackers, magicians, strongmen, ringmasters) against Ryan. Confirms Ryan's theory that the controller is a Yellow or Violet Psycho tied to the yellow/violet teleport flash, and that only a powerful Yellow or Violet could permanently destroy the maze.

facts.value: Voice turns passive-aggressive and vengeful when the maze is breached
Throws waves of circus minibosses (ninjas, magicians, ringmasters) at Ryan
Suspected Yellow/Violet Psycho tied to the yellow-violet teleport flash

wikiObservations.name: Quicksave
wikiObservations.summary: CH79 flashback reveals the ORIGIN of Ryan's 'Quicksave' superhero alias: when Simon asks who he is during the Monaco jailbreak, Ryan blurts out 'I'm Quicksave, the boulder who rolls' (a Sisyphus reference he immediately regrets sounding cooler in his head). He wears a custom metal mask with two rounded eye-glasses and night-vision, and crowns it with a stolen clown's rounded hat as a souvenir.

facts.value: Name coined on the spot during the Monaco jailbreak
Tagline 'the boulder who rolls' is a Sisyphus reference
Debuts a metal night-vision mask topped with a stolen clown hat

wikiObservations.name: Martine
wikiObservations.summary: CH79 flashback: among the ~40 Monaco captives Ryan frees, Martine is the warm blonde community leader whose death (April 28th, on a shrimp supply run) was the deadline forcing Ryan's rescue timing. After the jailbreak she leads the survivors west to rebuild, unaware she once lived a century of loops alongside Ryan; she parts with sad warmth, sensing they'll never meet again, and tells him he'll always be welcome. She embodies the bittersweet core of a Perfect Run: Ryan saves people who will never truly know him.

facts.value: Warm blonde community leader among the Monaco captives
Her looming April 28th death set Ryan's rescue deadline
Leads survivors west after the jailbreak; parts with Ryan warmly

ties.rel: saved by, never truly knows him

wikiObservations.name: The Resonators
wikiObservations.summary: A matched pair of nuclear-powered, steel-plated cube devices ~40cm across, each with a hand-sized particle-collider 'mouth' on one face and a control panel on the other. Built by Ryan over ~5 years of loops with a Genius's help, using scavenged parts of CERN's unfinished Hadron collider. They create a 'convergence' mimicking Ryan's own two-places-at-once power: particles stream from one cube to the other, forcing a path through dimensions. Ryan used them to breach Monaco's pocket dimension, opening a portal in Simon's tunnel (Monaco 'turned purple' as the barrier broke). They include a nuclear self-destruct sequence, which Ryan triggered to bury the maze behind the escaping captives. Ryan muses they could one day build an interdimensional radio.

facts.value: Paired nuclear cube colliders ~40cm, built from CERN Hadron parts
Force an inter-dimensional 'convergence' mimicking Ryan's power
Breached Monaco's pocket dimension via Simon's tunnel
Have a nuclear self-destruct sequence

wikiObservations.name: The Croupiers
wikiObservations.summary: CH79 flashback details the clown-croupiers as Monaco's staff-army in full: metal-masked in permanent grins, they only turn lethal during 'closed hours' and when the maze is threatened, then swarm in the hundreds armed with silver cutlery, golf clubs, sushi knives and nightsticks. Above the rank-and-file sit circus-themed minibosses summoned in escalating waves, acrobat/ninja swordsmen throwing shurikens, firecracker-throwers, magicians, strongmen, and ringmasters. They worship Jean-Stéphanie, chant anti-Andorran war slogans, and regenerate endlessly, but Ryan (as Quicksave) slaughters the entire garrison single-handed until the survivors drop their grins and flee screaming.

facts.value: Metal-masked grinning staff-army, lethal in 'closed hours'
Swarm in hundreds with cutlery, clubs, knives, nightsticks
Circus minibosses: ninjas, firecrackers, magicians, strongmen, ringmasters
Regenerate endlessly; routed by Quicksave in the jailbreak

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH79 flashback illuminates Ryan's defining early arc, his self-set 'Perfect Run' to free Monaco. Key power revelation: because he exists simultaneously in a place beyond spacetime and on Earth, 'I am an exit', the pocket dimension can push back the convergence of his two selves but never fully sever it, which is how a mortal escape becomes possible. He realizes the bittersweet truth of a Perfect Run here: he lived over a century of loops beside these people, knows them better than they know themselves, yet remains a stranger they meet only once, 'This was the perfect ending, for everyone. Everyone but Ryan.' He debuts the Quicksave persona, adopts Simon's Sisyphus/Camus outlook, and receives Nietzsche's eternal recurrence as its capstone. He freezes time to absorb the entire century of memories into himself before the save point advances, then drives into the sunset, his Perfect Run complete.

facts.value: 'I am an exit': his two-places-at-once nature lets him breach the maze
Lives centuries beside people who meet him only once, the Perfect Run's ache
Adopts Camus (Simon) + Nietzsche's eternal recurrence as his philosophy
Freezes time to absorb a century of memories before the save point advances

wikiObservations.name: Livia Augusti
wikiObservations.summary: CH80 deepens Livia: on the Rust Town pier she confides in Ryan as the one person her foresight can't 'watch', so their moments feel genuine. She reveals her power shows up to six switchable futures reacting to her emotions/desires, sees ~a month ahead (unreliable further out, she couldn't foresee her father's cancer in time), and that processing all those realities at accelerated rate makes her feel like an outside observer of her own life, she knows everyone but never truly lived with them (the same loneliness as Ryan). She confirms Felix will never return to her by free will, so 'there was nothing between us'. She agrees to Ryan's plan: preserve memories via her time-leap (she won't overwrite her own mind with Dynamis tech, so Len's past self must be the one convinced), co-develop the Psycho cure (on condition she's involved at every step), and gleefully joins the Star Studios raid as the supervillain Ryan dubs 'Queen Crimson'. She asks Ryan to destroy Ischia's Bliss Factory on his way out and foresees Leo Hargraves and Dynamis attacking Rust Town.

facts.value: Sees up to 6 switchable futures ~a month out; feels like an outside observer of her own life
Confirms Felix will never return by free will
Agrees to memory-preservation, Psycho cure (if involved throughout), and the raid
Foresees Leo Hargraves and Dynamis attacking Rust Town

wikiObservations.name: Queen Crimson
wikiObservations.summary: The supervillain alias Ryan coins for Livia Augusti when she insists on joining the Star Studios raid: a name he deems perfectly styled for her inexplicable time-leap power (she pitched 'Timestamp / Timezone / Time-Out / O'Clock' and he vetoed them all). To hide her identity from her father she'll wear a mask and use only her time-leap ability (her family alone knows its details). It debuts as her disguise for Ryan's planned takeover of Dynamis's Star Studios.

facts.value: Alias Ryan coins for Livia for the Star Studios raid
She keeps her face masked and uses only her time-leap ability
Ryan rejected her pitches (Timestamp, Time-Out, O'Clock)

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH80 shows Ryan's softened, matured worldview. He accepts Len as a friend rather than lover ('all I wished for was someone to remember me'), and declines Livia's suggestion to recreate his lost Jasmine across loops, fearing he'd obsess over his idea of her rather than the person (as he once did with Len). He commits to making the Psycho cure part of his final loop, 'I gave them hope; I don't want to disappoint it', extending mercy to Acid Rain, Mongrel, Frank, and Sarin as victims of their own powers, while still wanting Bloodstream dead. He plans to take Dynamis by going 'full supervillain': seize Star Studios, livestream Hector Manada's crimes, and recruit Vulcan's tech (bought with cooperation, not coercion) to boost his power and carry more minds across time.

facts.value: Accepts friendship over romance with Len; refuses to recreate Jasmine across loops
Vows to fold the Psycho cure into his final loop
Plans a 'full supervillain' Star Studios takeover to expose Hector Manada

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: CH80: to get closure, Len insists on the Lab Sixty-Six knockoff test despite Ryan's fears. Her theory: Dynamis didn't just capture her father, they 'packaged him, turned him into a product' -- inhuman and unforgivable even if it isn't truly him. When a droplet of her blood hits the Dynamis knockoff Elixir it SCREAMS, turns bloody red, and bloats into a twisted parody of Bloodstream's face reaching for its 'lost daughter'. Len relives her four-year-old trauma in raw terror, screaming and clawing her own cheeks bloody until Alchemo's flamethrowers incinerate the slime; Ryan holds her as she sobs. She still cannot answer what she'll do if her father is really alive in the lab.

facts.value: Insists on the knockoff test for closure despite the risk
Frames Dynamis 'packaging' her father as inhuman
Relives her trauma when the knockoff reforms into Bloodstream
Can't yet decide what to do if her father lives

wikiObservations.name: Bloodstream
wikiObservations.summary: CH80 reveals Bloodstream's fate: Dynamis has kept Len's father in storage in Lab Sixty-Six for ~4 years and uses him as the raw material to mass-produce their knockoff Elixirs. A drop of Len's (his daughter's) blood makes a knockoff scream, turn red, bloat like Darkling devouring Adam, and form Bloodstream's screaming face, confirming he is the source. Whether anything curable remains after four years of Dr. Tyrano's exploitation is unknown; Ryan wants him dead and buried regardless.

facts.value: Held in Lab Sixty-Six ~4 years as knockoff-Elixir raw material
Reacts to Len's blood by reforming his screaming face
Ryan wants him dead regardless of any cure

wikiObservations.name: The Knockoff Elixir
wikiObservations.summary: Dynamis's mass-produced counterfeit power Elixirs, achieving the same effect as Mechron's knockoffs by a different method. The 'Hercules' variant (green liquid, templated on Wyvern) is shown to be made from Bloodstream: exposed to Len's blood it screams and reforms into his face. Implication that horrifies Ryan: unknown numbers of New Romans have unknowingly drunk Elixirs made from a packaged human being, the scale of Hector Manada's crimes.

facts.value: Dynamis counterfeit Elixirs; 'Hercules' variant templated on Wyvern
Made from Bloodstream; reacts to Len-blood by reforming his face
Many New Romans may have unknowingly consumed them

wikiObservations.name: Leo Hargraves
wikiObservations.summary: CH80: Livia's foresight increasingly places Leo Hargraves ('Sunshine') in Rust Town intending to attack Ryan, odds rising with time -- which would only happen if he learned of the bunker. Ryan links this to the glass-manipulator Mr. See-Through's ('Safelite') recent activity, suspecting Shroud pieced together the bunker's existence via former Psyshock thralls or Ryan's own presence among the Meta-Gang.

facts.value: Foreseen coming to Rust Town to attack Ryan (only if he learns of the bunker)
Linked to Mr. See-Through/Shroud investigating Rust Town

wikiObservations.name: Mr. See-Through
wikiObservations.summary: A glass-manipulating Shroud/Safelite operative ('Mr. See-Through') making increasingly frequent forays into Rust Town, though the Land's interference keeps his visits short. Ryan suspects he has been investigating the bunker -- possibly interrogating former Psyshock thralls -- and that his intel is why Leo Hargraves may soon strike Rust Town.

facts.value: Glass-manipulating Shroud/Safelite operative
The Land's interference limits his time in Rust Town
Suspected of uncovering the bunker

ties.rel: feeds intel that may bring him

wikiObservations.name: Alchemo
wikiObservations.summary: CH80: Alchemo runs the bunker's cure/enhancement lab, confirming Mosquito's nutrient-rich synthesized blood boosts his strength for ~an hour. Ready with ceiling flamethrowers as a failsafe, Alchemo incinerates the Bloodstream knockoff the instant it threatens Len, and chides Ryan for dragging the gentle Doll (Tea) into the raid.

facts.value: Runs bunker cure/enhancement research
Confirms synthesized blood boosts Mosquito's strength ~1 hour
Torches the Bloodstream knockoff to protect Len

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH81: Ryan executes his 'Mr. President' villain plan, storming Dynamis's Star Studios with the Meta-Gang, seizing the live news set, and broadcasting to New Rome. He livestreams his edited confrontation with Hector Manada plus the Bloodstream-knockoff footage (revealing ~10% of New Rome unknowingly carries a Bloodstream clone), threatens the city with a mini A-bomb (the 'North Korea special'), performs a stop-motion figurine parody of Manada/Augustus/Adam/Psyshock, and demands a deliberately absurd 'one million dollars' ransom. The stunt is designed to make Dynamis tear itself apart rather than target Rust Town. Sarin keeps re-uploading the exposé faster than Dynamis can censor it.

facts.value: Hijacks Star Studios' live news set as 'Mr. President'
Airs the Bloodstream-knockoff exposé; ~10% of New Rome affected
Threatens the city with a mini A-bomb; demands $1 million ransom

wikiObservations.name: Livia Augusti
wikiObservations.summary: CH81: Livia's first field outing as 'Queen Crimson', in a black lounge suit with red shirt/tie and a Daft-Punk-style helmet (an androgynous, stylish look Tea adores). Shy and inexperienced with fieldwork, she stays in the background of the news-set takeover, gasps at the knockoff footage, and warms to the gang's gallows humor, giggling at Ryan's antics. Ryan lends her the Fisty Brothers gauntlets. Her foresight underpins Ryan's confidence that the raid unfolds exactly as planned.

facts.value: Debuts as 'Queen Crimson' in a Daft-Punk-style helmet
Shy and inexperienced with field work; stays background
Lent the Fisty Brothers gauntlets

wikiObservations.name: Mosquito
wikiObservations.summary: CH81: over-fed on Alchemo's high-nutrient synthesized blood, Mosquito nearly doubles in size for the raid, his under-exoskeleton flesh turning from crimson to green and his muscles swelling grotesquely, prompting Ryan to nickname him 'Beefcake'. He serves as aerial guard over Star Studios, watching for flying reinforcements.

facts.value: Doubled in size on synthesized blood; Ryan nicknames him 'Beefcake'
Flesh turns green, muscles grotesquely swollen
Acts as aerial lookout during the raid

wikiObservations.name: The Knockoff Elixir
wikiObservations.summary: CH81 quantifies the horror: Ryan estimates Knockoff Elixirs (made from Bloodstream) are in roughly 10% of New Rome's population, since both Dynamis and Augustus used them heavily to bolster forces, meaning one in ten people could turn into a Bloodstream clone. Ryan broadcasts the exposé live to force Dynamis into crisis.

facts.value: ~10% of New Rome has consumed a Knockoff Elixir
Used heavily by both Dynamis and Augustus
Any consumer could become a Bloodstream clone

wikiObservations.name: Star Studios
wikiObservations.summary: CH81: Dynamis's film-and-broadcast complex, controlling the Dynanet and airwaves, is raided by the Meta-Gang. Lightly guarded (Dynamis never expected an attack), the crew crashes the checkpoint, seizes the circular News Studio set (half its walls a 3D screen, staffed by underpaid workers), and commandeers the live morning broadcast. Ryan takes over the anchor desk to deliver his ransom message and knockoff exposé.

facts.value: Dynamis's broadcast complex controlling Dynanet and airwaves
Lightly guarded; Meta-Gang crashes the checkpoint
Its live News Studio is hijacked for Ryan\u2019s broadcast

wikiObservations.name: Wardrobe
wikiObservations.summary: CH82: Ryan finally meets his 'archenemy' Wardrobe in person during the Star Studios raid. She is the costume-Genome who unknowingly designed his 'Mr. President' ensemble (skull socks and all), and Ryan reveals she 'created' her own nemesis. Craving a flashy lifelong rivalry, she gleefully accepts his pitch to be his scheduled archenemy forever and build a billion-euro hero/villain merchandising franchise. Her power still lets her instantly re-costume: she cosplays an FBI negotiator, then Arsene Lupin to steal Ryan's A-bomb from Sarin's hand, then a nurse to treat the wounded. Its limit: she can only steal/hold one bomb at a time, which Ryan exploits by juggling three.

facts.value: Unknowingly designed Ryan's 'Mr. President' costume; now his willing archenemy
Instant re-costume: FBI negotiator, Arsene Lupin, nurse
Can only steal/hold one bomb at a time (Ryan juggles three)

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH82: Ryan walks out of the Star Studios raid untouched by out-bluffing every hero. He recruits Wardrobe as his archenemy, out-juggles her costume-theft power with three A-bombs (mass-produced via Mechron's matter replicator), dodges Atom Cat's kill-touch on legs alone, and forces Wyvern to stand down by threatening 'Dr. Strangelove'. He hands Wyvern a syringe of Len's blood as proof of the Bloodstream-knockoff crime, betting she'll turn on Dynamis. He spares Felix (per his promise to Livia) and leaves the wounded Shroud for Dynamis to avoid provoking Leo. He escapes with the ransom pending, only to find a horror waiting at the Rust Town checkpoint.

facts.value: Juggles three A-bombs to defeat Wardrobe's one-item steal limit
Gives Wyvern Len's blood as proof against Dynamis
Spares Felix per his promise to Livia

wikiObservations.name: Mr. See-Through
wikiObservations.summary: CH82: the invisible glass-manipulating Shroud operative joins the assault on the Star Studios raiders but Livia (as Queen Crimson), warned by her foresight of alternate selves dying to 'glass shards to the neck', punches him with the Fisty Brothers, slamming him into the truck and revealing his bloodied body. Dying of a punctured lung, he rasps a crucial confession: the Shroud hunted down all of Bloodstream's clones but 'failed... we just delayed' Bloodstream's return, they only postponed it, not stopped it. Ryan leaves him for Dynamis rather than provoke Leo Hargraves by capturing him.

facts.value: Downed by Livia's Fisty punch (she foresaw his glass-shard kill)
Confesses the Shroud only 'delayed', not stopped, Bloodstream's return
Left wounded for Dynamis to avoid provoking Leo

wikiObservations.name: Wyvern
wikiObservations.summary: CH82: Dynamis's shining hero Wyvern ('Dragon Mom') fights to stop the raid, dueling the overfed Mosquito in dragon form (she eventually smashes him back to normal size) and threatening Ryan with lethal force. Ryan neutralizes her with his triple-A-bomb bluff, which Dynamis's Geniuses confirm genuine over her earpiece, forcing her to stand down. He gives her a syringe of Len's blood, betting she never knew Dynamis makes Elixirs from a living man and would never have signed on if she had, planting the seed of her defection.

facts.value: Duels Mosquito in dragon form; beats him back to normal size
Forced to stand down by Ryan's confirmed triple-bomb bluff
Handed Len's blood as proof against Dynamis

wikiObservations.name: Mosquito
wikiObservations.summary: CH82: the 'Beefcake'-enhanced Mosquito holds his own against Wyvern in the skies over Star Studios (cracking nearby windows with a single punch), a reversal from an early loop where she squashed him easily. She eventually overpowers him, smashing him through the warehouse roof; he deflates back to normal size, badly wounded, and Frank carries him to the truck.

facts.value: Enhanced 'Beefcake' form trades blows with dragon-form Wyvern
Eventually overpowered, smashed through the roof, deflates
Carried wounded to the truck by Frank

wikiObservations.name: The Killer Rabbit Plushie
wikiObservations.summary: CH82 cliffhanger: the plushie that breached containment and escaped the Junkyard reappears with lethal effect. At the Rust Town checkpoint the raiders find ~24 Private Security guards hung from an archway by their own intestines, '885' daubed in blood beneath them and 'HAPPY BIRTHDAY!' spelled out one letter per corpse, its signature loving-yet-monstrous flourish. It pollutes Livia's foresight (as another such creature did with Eugene-Henry), which is why she 'couldn't see it' coming. Its pointed ears rise behind Ryan in the truck's rear-view mirror, the reason Ryan declares this run already doomed.

facts.value: Escaped plushie massacres ~24 guards, hanging them by their intestines
Signs its kills 'HAPPY BIRTHDAY! 885' in blood
Pollutes Livia's foresight so she can't predict it; appears in Ryan's truck

ties.rel: its creator, now hunted by it

wikiObservations.name: Atom Cat
wikiObservations.summary: CH82: Felix ('Atom Cat', mocked as 'Atom Kitten/Kitty') fights among the heroes defending Star Studios, repeatedly lunging to land his kill-touch on Ryan's bare skin, but Ryan dodges and trips him with legs alone, humiliating him. Ryan sics Eugene-Henry on his face (the cat claws him bloody) but, per his promise to Livia, ensures Felix is not seriously harmed. Livia, disguised as Queen Crimson, tenses at her ex-boyfriend and avoids his gaze in apparent shame.

facts.value: Kill-touch hero; repeatedly fails to land a blow on Ryan
Humiliated (tripped, clawed by Eugene-Henry) but spared per Ryan's promise
Livia's ex; she avoids his gaze during the fight

wikiObservations.name: Livia Augusti
wikiObservations.summary: CH82: Livia proves herself in the field. Her foresight flags Wyvern's attack, the Il Migliore/Private Security siege, and her own alternate deaths by glass shards, letting her punch the invisible Shroud with the Fisty Brothers at the decisive moment. She uses her time-leap to skip past a killing burst of glass at Ryan. Exhilarated ('I couldn't tell how it would turn out at any point!'), she rediscovers her love of surprises, until the checkpoint massacre (which her foresight couldn't show) horrifies her, since the Killer Rabbit Plushie blinds her power.

facts.value: Downs the invisible Shroud with a foreseen Fisty punch
Time-leaps Ryan past a lethal glass burst
Exhilarated by the chaos; then horrified by the plushie massacre she couldn't foresee

wikiObservations.name: Vulcan
wikiObservations.summary: CH83: Vulcan (Jasmine's alternate loop-self) flies past Dynamis's blockade, which she designed, to honor her deal with Ryan, delighted that he humiliated 'that bitch Wyvern'. Ryan, still in love and aching over the promise his own Jasmine made him ('don't replace me with another Jasmine'), keeps things playful but won't rekindle romance. She agrees to build his magnum opus using the bunker's Mechron tech and matter replicator: a power-boosting cashmere-poncho armor incorporating Len's signal tech, meant to let Ryan carry multiple people back through time. The armor still needs Len's help, and Len won't leave her room.

facts.value: Bypasses her own Dynamis blockade to join Ryan per their deal
Agrees to build a power-boosting cashmere armor with Len's signal tech
Ryan keeps his promise to Jasmine and won't rekindle romance

wikiObservations.name: Wyvern
wikiObservations.summary: CH83: at Dynamis's damage-control press conference, Wyvern goes off-script and publicly confirms the Knockoff Elixir horror is real ('I have checked'), then resigns as Il Migliore's leader on principle, refusing to stay with an organization capable of it (she'll still cooperate against the Meta-Gang). Her defection detonates Dynamis's PR; Enrique Manada stays silent (as if he'd long wanted to say it) and Felix walks out of Dynamis entirely. Ryan's exposure gambit ('all according to keikaku') pays off.

facts.value: Publicly confirms the Knockoff Elixir crime live on air
Resigns as Il Migliore leader on principle
Her defection shatters Dynamis's PR; Felix quits too

wikiObservations.name: The Psycho Cure
wikiObservations.summary: CH83: Alchemo's bio-scans crack the Psycho puzzle. Helen's two Elixirs each rewrote ~50% of her DNA and conflict daily (51/49% flux) causing tumors; Livia's blue Elixir dominates while ~2.5% violet coexists WITHOUT overwriting. Alchemo's theory: Livia's genome (Neanderthal-inherited DNA, chimerism, or a rare quirk) fools her Elixirs into believing they bonded to two different people sharing one body, so they share rather than fight. The cure would reproduce Mongrel's Elixir-control power via gene therapy to force conflicting Elixirs into that same equilibrium (or strip the extra one to make a stable monocolor Genome). Building it needs Mongrel, Livia's data, the bunker, and Dr. Tyrano (the only gene-therapy Genius); Alchemo's AI alone would take months.

facts.value: Livia's stable dual-power = Elixirs think they bonded to two people
Cure mimics Mongrel's Elixir-control + gene therapy to force equilibrium
Needs Dr. Tyrano, who rarely leaves Dynamis HQ and is protected by Fallout

wikiObservations.name: Elixirs
wikiObservations.summary: CH83: deeper lore. Elixirs are alien lifeforms that don't even use DNA; per Darkling they were 'taught' (probably by the Alchemist) to bond with humans, so the bonding is not natural to them. They know the words but not the music: they connect lower lifeforms to the Ultimate Ones to let them ascend, but their grasp of human biology is only superficial. This explains why they only bond with Homo Sapiens (all attempts with animals, even 99%-shared chimpanzees, failed) and why a genome close enough to two templates (Neanderthal-tinged) can fool them into a dual bond.

facts.value: Alien lifeforms that don't use DNA, taught to bond with humans
Only bond with Homo Sapiens; animal bonding always fails
Meant to connect lifeforms to the Ultimate Ones for ascension

ties.rel: their misbinding is the cure's basis

wikiObservations.name: Fallout
wikiObservations.summary: CH83: named as the guarantor that keeps Dr. Tyrano untouchable. Augustus never had Tyrano assassinated because 'then Fallout gets involved' and Livia (who has foreseen it) implies the outcome is catastrophic. A Dynamis-aligned power tied to protecting the Knockoff operation's cornerstone.

facts.value: Deterrent protecting Dr. Tyrano; retaliates if he is killed
Livia foresees his involvement ending very badly

wikiObservations.name: Livia Augusti
wikiObservations.summary: CH83: lets Alchemo draw her blood for the cure research despite fearing the data could cause an arms race (a no-side-effect power cure could mint warlords like her father). Her bio-scan reveals ~97.5% blue / 2.5% violet Elixir coexisting without conflict, the stable template for the Psycho Cure. She warns kidnapping Tyrano triggers Fallout, foresees Sarin listening at the door ('you can come in, this does not have to end in violence'), and must return to a meeting Augustus called about how to deal with Ryan.

facts.value: Bio-scan: ~97.5% blue, 2.5% violet Elixir, stable and non-conflicting
Consents to blood draw despite arms-race fears
Predicts Sarin eavesdropping; defuses it before violence

wikiObservations.name: Sarin
wikiObservations.summary: CH83: eavesdrops on Ryan and Livia's cure/endgame discussion and turns on Ryan, leveling her vibrating gauntlet at him ('Better luck next time, eh? Not gonna work for me.'). Livia foresaw it and coaxes her out of hiding, hoping to avoid violence. A betrayal beat that closes the chapter.

facts.value: Turns on Ryan after overhearing the cure/endgame talk
Vibrating gauntlet, fingers charged with power

ties.rel: foreseen and coaxed out by her

wikiObservations.name: Sarin
wikiObservations.summary: CH84: mutinies against Ryan, refusing to let him time-travel until he cures her, but her rebellion collapses into the chapter's most tragic backstory. Her real grief: when she first gained power the wind dispersed her; it took SIX MONTHS to pull herself together and find a container she wouldn't rust through, spent 'years' sealed in a cloth prison feeling nothing, terrified of any blade. Ryan refuses to absolve her for standing by Adam through his atrocities ('you're entirely lucid'). She fires a warning blast, then collapses sobbing: 'My name is not Sarin... I want my life back.' Ryan swears she'll get a happy ending but must wait her turn; Alchemo takes her to attempt a memory backup.

facts.value: First manifested as dispersing wind; took 6 months to reform, years sealed in a cloth suit
Mutinies to force a cure, then breaks down; rejects the name 'Sarin'
Ryan won't absolve her complicity with Adam ('you're entirely lucid')

ties.rel: attempts to back up her memories

wikiObservations.name: Alchemo
wikiObservations.summary: CH84: revealed to have read the Doll's memory-map (harvesting memories like Psyshock) to check for sabotage, which is how the group learned Ryan planned to abandon them. Ryan indicts him for the OTHER Alchemo who once went mad and tried to extract Ryan's brain to stop him reloading (Tea had to finish Ryan off mid-procedure). This Alchemo refuses the equivalence: 'That was another me... I am not the person he was.' He confesses he's a cynical old man who built a robot daughter because he drove everyone away, and offers to copy the Doll's, Sarin's, and others' minds so the loop-bonds can survive. A genuine redemption beat.

facts.value: Can harvest and read others' memories, like Psyshock
Read the Doll's memory-map, exposing Ryan's plan to leave
Rejects being judged by his other self's worst act; offers to back up minds

ties.rel: offers to copy minds with it

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH84: reaches a major turning point in his eternal-loop psychology. Confronted by Sarin's mutiny, Alchemo's plea, and Livia, he agrees for the first time to bring loop-companions FORWARD via memory backups rather than leaving everyone behind as he did in Monaco, Spain, France, Italy. He's terrified of bonds he can't take back, but recalls that trusting Jasmine taught him change must begin with himself. He won't take everyone (too many already know, risking another Adam/Psyshock capture) but lets Livia record vetted people's brainmaps. Livia names his true fear: 'You're not afraid of death, but you're afraid of other people.' He counters Sartre's 'hell is other people' with her 'hell is loneliness.'

facts.value: First agrees to carry loop-companions forward via memory backups
Won't take everyone; only Livia-recorded vetted brainmaps, to limit exposure
Afraid of connections he can't take back, not of death

ties.rel: the means to carry bonds forward
Jasmine, the trust that taught him to change

wikiObservations.name: Livia Augusti
wikiObservations.summary: CH84: the diplomat and moral center. She defuses Sarin's mutiny (having foreseen Sarin shooting her and Alchemo dead in other branches), then persuades Ryan to keep his loop-bonds by recording vetted brainmaps before the coming point of no return. She reads Ryan's soul precisely ('you're afraid of other people') and answers Sartre with 'hell is loneliness,' something only the two of them understand. She shares her own wound: childhood Sicily drives with her parents she can never return to, mirroring Len's paralysis. Ryan tells her she too can make new happy memories; she echoes his old words back: 'You are not alone, Ryan. Not anymore.'

facts.value: Foresaw Sarin killing her and Alchemo; defused it instead
Persuades Ryan to back up vetted minds before the point of no return
'Hell is loneliness'; shares her Sicily memory of lost family happiness

ties.rel: talks him into keeping his bonds

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: CH84: found catatonic in Shortie's room, knees to chest, water rifle within reach as if Bloodstream might barge in like in her childhood. She has never moved on. Ryan tells her it's almost time to open Darkling's gate home and then raid Lab Sixty-Six to face what remains of Bloodstream. She dreads it and doubts her father can be cured or is even still alive (maybe just a harvested corpse for Knockoffs), but grabbing her water rifle she resolves to go: 'Let's go.' She stops hiding to face the raid.

facts.value: Catatonic with childhood Bloodstream trauma; water rifle always in reach
Resolves to raid Lab 66 to face what remains of Bloodstream

wikiObservations.name: The Brain-Copying Machine
wikiObservations.summary: CH84: pressed into service to preserve loop-companions. Livia can store as many brainmaps as needed; Alchemo takes Sarin to attempt copying even her (a challenge, since she 'has air for a head' with no physical brain, though she still forms memories). Ryan agrees to let Livia record only vetted people before the coming point of no return, making it the tool that lets his loop-bonds survive a reload for the first time.

facts.value: Livia records vetted brainmaps to carry companions across a reload
Sarin has no physical brain (air-headed), so copying her is uncertain

wikiObservations.name: The Doll
wikiObservations.summary: CH84: her love for Ryan is the lever that turns Alchemo toward redemption. Alchemo reveals he built her as a robot daughter because he'd driven everyone else away, and that her wish to help others made him try to do better. He fears that if Ryan leaves forever, the Doll will never find closure, only a gaping hole, so he offers to copy her memories for Ryan to carry.

facts.value: Built by Alchemo as a daughter after he drove everyone away
Her love for Ryan drives Alchemo's redemption and memory-backup offer

wikiObservations.name: The Saturn Armor
wikiObservations.summary: CH85: the magnum-opus power armor Vulcan (Jasmine) finally builds, fulfilling a promise she and Ryan made loops ago to make a suit that could destroy Dynamis's HQ. A lightweight purple exoskeleton refined across many loops: servo-enhanced strength, hidden switchblades, gauntlet laser turrets, and 'the Chernobyl' nuclear-powered chest blaster. Its reinforced backpack holds a miniaturized Chronoradio (artificial brain included) meant to transfer a mind across time, though it still can only carry ONE person. Its rabbit-eared helmet antennae streamline Ryan's connection to the Violet Flux dimension and feed him data on how his power works. Vulcan names it Saturn (over Ryan's 'Rabbinator'/'White Rabbit'); it needs Mechron's matter replicator to rebuild.

facts.value: Switchblades, gauntlet lasers, 'the Chernobyl' nuclear chest blaster
Miniature Chronoradio backpack transfers one mind across time
Rabbit-ear antennae streamline Violet Flux connection, feed power data

ties.rel: needs his matter replicator to build

wikiObservations.name: Darkling
wikiObservations.summary: CH85: goes home. Via the bunker's particle collider (the same room Mechron's AI once summoned it in) Ryan opens the gate to the Black World and Darkling crosses over, reverting from slime to its true impossible form (a prismatic sphere of recursive eyes and impossible geometries) and leaving a pile of corroded human bones behind. It reveals it has been studied 'far longer than you can imagine' (years/decades trapped across Ryan's loops) and tempts Ryan to ascend and abandon Earth. When Ryan refuses, Darkling is not angry ('Black is paradox, freedom from all laws, the ability to say no') and promises to wait for him at the end: 'When you are satisfied... I will wait for you here.'

facts.value: Returns home to the Black World through Ryan's gate
Reverts to true form: prismatic sphere, recursive eyes, impossible geometry
Will wait for Ryan at world's end when he chooses to end it all

ties.rel: friend who opens its gate home

wikiObservations.name: The Black World
wikiObservations.summary: CH85: the color dimension Darkling/the Black Elixir comes from, the source of the Black Flux, reached through Ryan's gate. A realm darker than any abyss that exists BEYOND time, space, and reason, where Ryan glimpses living equations, an ouroboros devouring itself without losing mass, and stillborn realities. Its nature is paradox: 'nothing is forbidden,' 'freedom from all laws, the ability to say no to everything, even to itself.' It tempts visitors to ascend and shed their flesh; entering it, Ryan's own hands flicker in and out of existence. It could recreate the dead Ryan erased, but only as agonized paradoxes, so his Elixir warns him to let the dead rest.

facts.value: Beyond time/space/reason; the realm of paradox and pure freedom
Dissolves physical form; ascension means never returning
Can recreate the erased dead, but only as suffering paradoxes

ties.rel: its Flux is the Black Elixir's source
the god that dwells in it

wikiObservations.name: The Black Ultimate One
wikiObservations.summary: CH85: the divine entity dwelling at the heart of the Black World, a black hole so vast it makes the Milky Way's central one look like a speck, whose mere attention could erase Ryan unless it consciously holds back. Like the Violet Ultimate One, it beckons humans toward its dimension (this drew Geist, Bacchus, and Mechron to obsess over higher dimensions). It heard Ryan's wish and communicated by borrowing the voices of his dead (Jasmine, Simon, Felix) 'the way a human might mimic an ant's language,' offering to free his spirit from flesh and causality. Ryan refuses its ascension.

facts.value: A black hole dwarfing the Milky Way's; could erase Ryan by mere attention
Spoke through the voices of Ryan's dead to lure him to ascend

ties.rel: tries to draw him into ascension

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH85: his most profound crossroads. After sending Darkling home, Ryan crosses into the Black World and is tempted by the Black Ultimate One to ascend, shed his flesh, and escape immortality's curse forever, lured by the voices of Jasmine, Simon, and Felix, the promise of reuniting with everyone he ever erased. He almost stays, but chooses the living (Len, Livia, Felix, Sarin, all who trust him) over the dead, refusing to recreate the erased as suffering paradoxes. He returns changed, now radiating BLACK particles alongside violet. He confirms he cannot break the loop himself: his power is the wish he made at bonding and his Elixir cannot undo it.

facts.value: Refuses to ascend into the Black World; chooses the living over the dead
Returns radiating Black particles alongside Violet Flux
His time-loop is the unbreakable wish he made when his Elixir bonded to him

wikiObservations.name: Elixir Mechanics
wikiObservations.summary: CH85: the origin and mechanics of Ryan's power are finally revealed by the power itself. In the Black World his save-point manifests as the violet phantom that always chases him, and speaks: it is his Elixir, his 'other half,' the Violet-Flux power slumbering in him. When they bonded it looked into him and granted his deepest wish (to return to the past to change the present), which is why it revives him even from old age, believing this makes him happy. It CANNOT undo or re-parameter that wish, so it cannot stop the loop; only Ryan choosing to stop can end it. In normal time the phantom cannot speak (that needed the Black World's interference); catching it forms a new save point.

facts.value: Ryan's save-point IS his Elixir, his violet-Flux other half
Grants his wish to return to the past, made at bonding; cannot be undone
Phantom catching Ryan forms a save point; it can only speak via the Black World

ties.rel: is his bonded Elixir and power
the dimension its Violet Flux is drawn from

wikiObservations.name: Black Flux
wikiObservations.summary: CH86: the new energy Ryan brought back from the Black World, detected by the Saturn Armor only when the suit is on and time is frozen. It is a paradox substance: its recorded readings keep CHANGING after being recorded (binary to trinary, numbers to symbols), actively refusing categorization and 'passively altering reality' when insisted upon. Alchemo's scans still read Ryan as an ordinary monocolor Violet Genome with no anomaly, so the Black Flux works on a level beyond physical reality (like the DNA-less ghosts Geist and Ghoul). Vulcan suspects Ryan gained a secondary power linked to the Black World, but he can't yet use it ('UNLIMITED POWAH' does nothing) and doesn't know what it does.

facts.value: Readings self-alter after recording; refuses categorization, warps reality
Brought from the Black World; only appears with the Saturn Armor in frozen time
Possible dormant second power Ryan can't yet activate or understand

ties.rel: the only thing that detects it

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH86: launches the Lab Sixty-Six raid. He puzzles over his new Black Flux (a possible unusable second power), then formally forgives Alchemo, granting him a second chance (send his brainmap to Livia) with a hard 'no third chance' warning, embodying his new resolve to extend a hand rather than stay alone. He confesses to Len this will be his TWELFTH time destroying the world, swearing there won't be a thirteenth, and they pinky-swear 'together till the end.' The plan: Mosquito flies Ryan and Len up while minions and Toasty's robots storm the tower; grab Dr. Tyrano, torch Lab 66, flee before Dynamis mobilizes. Complication: Fallout is recalled, ~1-2 hours out.

facts.value: Forgives Alchemo, grants a final second chance
This is his 12th time destroying the world; swears no 13th
Aerial insertion, grab Tyrano, torch Lab 66, flee before Fallout arrives

ties.rel: forgives and gives a second chance

wikiObservations.name: The Killer Rabbit Plushie
wikiObservations.summary: CH86: its rampage escalates into open war on Mount Augustus, which Ryan dubs the plushipocalypse/Leporimachia. A self-replicating tide of white fur overwhelms the entire hill toward Augustus's villa, replicating faster than even Augustus can kill it (forcing Dynamis to mobilize everyone). Ryan reads its motive as unfinished business: it vanished after Augustus slew Acid Rain in a prior loop, and now it wants to hunt bigger game, 'to make a god bleed.' Its plushies also besiege New Rome (missing children, daycare attacks). Whoever wins the hill, the city is doomed.

facts.value: Self-replicating swarm wars on Mount Augustus faster than Augustus can cull
Wants to 'make a god bleed'; unfinished business with Augustus
Ryan calls it the plushipocalypse / Leporimachia

ties.rel: prior loop hunt drives its grudge

wikiObservations.name: Sarin
wikiObservations.summary: CH86: fully redeemed from mutineer to Ryan's most fervent believer. When the demoralized gang wants to flee (Mongrel, Mosquito, Acid Rain all wavering), Sarin delivers a rousing, unexpectedly charismatic speech casting Ryan as an unbeatable cheating gambler who ran circles around Adam, Dynamis, Augustus, and the Carnival: 'This guy brings a nuclear bomb to a gunfight and wins his wars with a goddamn alien... Would you bet against a cheater? I say we burn [the house]!' Frank's applause turns the tide and rallies everyone. She reminds Ryan of his cure-promise ('I'll haunt you').

facts.value: Turns from mutineer to Ryan's loyal rallying voice
Her speech re-motivates the demoralized gang for the raid

wikiObservations.name: Vulcan
wikiObservations.summary: CH86: parts ways with Ryan before the raid on Augustus's orders (she won't disobey her father-figure warlord for Ryan's sake: 'that mofo is more lethal than Ebola'). She sees through his lie about the killer-plushie ('I'm a Genius, but I'm also a genius, so don't f--- with me') and tells him to skip town so they don't end up enemies. She scrambles Dynamis's comms on the way out and, crucially, warns Ryan her radars detected a radiation spike west: Fallout has been recalled, ~1-2 hours out. She warns Len not to hang around Ryan ('he's going to live fast and die young').

facts.value: Departs on Augustus's orders; scrambles Dynamis comms
Detects Fallout's radiation inbound, ~1-2 hours out
Sees through Ryan's plushie lie; tells him to skip town

ties.rel: parts as a friend, warns him off

wikiObservations.name: Fallout
wikiObservations.summary: CH86: recalled by Dynamis (with Hector's star fading) to defend against Ryan's raid, turning the mission into a race against a ticking clock. Vulcan's radars pick up his radiation signature approaching from the west, ~1-2 hours out. A radiation-based powerhouse fast enough that his arrival would make the Lab 66 raid extraordinarily more dangerous, prompting Ryan to joke about 'making a new Chernobyl.'

facts.value: Recalled to stop Ryan's raid; ~1-2 hours out per Vulcan's radar
Radiation-based, detectable at long range

ties.rel: the threat racing to intercept his raid

wikiObservations.name: Fallout
wikiObservations.summary: CH87: arrives far faster than the ~1-2 hour estimate, drilling down through the floors above and crashing into Lab Sixty-Six just as Ryan reaches the final door. Named Alphonse 'Fallout' Manada, he tosses away Mosquito's charbroiled corpse (having killed him on the roof), his hands shining with deadly radiation that trips the Saturn Armor's alarm. 'You're going all-in, huh? Well, I'm calling your bet, muties... Time to die.' A Manada powerhouse and the raid's greatest threat, now blocking Ryan's crew inside the lab.

facts.value: Alphonse 'Fallout' Manada, radiation-based powerhouse
Kills Mosquito on the roof; drills into Lab 66 to confront Ryan
Comes much faster than the 1-2 hour estimate

wikiObservations.name: Wardrobe
wikiObservations.summary: CH87: guards Lab 66 but only makes a token effort (no apocalypse or Augustus suit) because Dynamis holds her girlfriend Nora Moore hostage over the money-laundering Ryan exposed; Enrique confirmed Ryan meant no harm, so she'd have quit like Felix otherwise. She and Ryan have a glorious costume duel (Poseidon, ninja, fencer) that Ryan wins only by cheating with a time-stop, blade to her throat. He proposes marriage ('together we can rule the galaxy'); she tearfully refuses (already taken, 'no harems'), they agree to stay 'good archnemeses,' and he taps her pressure points to lay her down gently. Ryan promises to free Nora on the way out.

facts.value: Only token-defends; Dynamis holds Nora Moore hostage
Costume duel with Ryan; he wins by cheating a time-stop
Rejects Ryan's marriage proposal but stays willing archnemesis

ties.rel: her hostage girlfriend, Ryan will free
confirmed Ryan's good faith to her

wikiObservations.name: The Panda
wikiObservations.summary: CH87: Dynamis desperately recruits Ryan's most powerful rogue to guard Lab 66, a colossal kung-fu manbear from Zhongguo whose head reaches the ceiling, fur white as bone and soul black. Grandiose and heroic in speech ('We meet at last, villain!'; 'The Panda is the only one who can stop you, even if he must ally with a lesser evil'), but visibly terrified underneath, unable to hide his fear. He leaps to fight Ryan 'in Justice's name' but Len simply traps him in a pressurized water bubble, where the great swimmer flails helplessly.

facts.value: Giant kung-fu manbear, Ryan's most powerful rogue, recruited to guard Lab 66
Grandiose but frightened; neutralized instantly by Len's water bubble

wikiObservations.name: Reload
wikiObservations.summary: CH87: the Il Migliore hero guards Lab 66 alongside the Panda and Wardrobe, wielding a laser blade and hungry for payback (still believing Ryan a deranged Psycho warlord who nuke-threatened New Rome, refusing to credit the Knockoff exposé). He charges recklessly and Len traps him in a water bubble, where his death-and-rebirth power cycles him through repeated drownings. Wardrobe later grabs his dropped laser blade for her fencing duel. He is unironically named the same as Ryan's save-point mechanic, but is a distinct person.

facts.value: Charges Ryan; trapped in a drowning-rebirth cycle by Len's bubble
Refuses to believe the Knockoff exposé; sees Ryan as a warlord

ties.rel: she takes his dropped laser blade

wikiObservations.name: Incognito
wikiObservations.summary: CH87: a Psycho infiltrator Ryan deployed earlier in the loop to breach Dynamis HQ. His Blue power forces others to perceive him as anyone he chooses (though not enough to fool all security systems). Combined with Ryan's hacking and Tea/Alchemo's remote assistance, Incognito slipped inside and reached the building's main servers, letting the crew reprogram every keycard to open any floor during the raid.

facts.value: Blue: makes others perceive him as any person he picks
Infiltrated Dynamis servers to reprogram keycard access for the raid

wikiObservations.name: Lab Sixty-Six
wikiObservations.summary: CH87: finally breached. An immaculate sterile white room ~50m by 20m, a claustrophobic automated medical assembly line staffed only by robots and drones (no human guards, likely due to Elixir contamination risk). Colored Knockoff Elixir bottles emerge from a metal hole, get stamped with Dynamis's logo by robotic arms, and are crated for delivery. It runs on its own secure computer system, so Ryan's reprogrammed keycards fail on the inner bioscanner door, behind which Dr. Tyrano presumably works. Fallout drills in before they can breach that final door.

facts.value: Sterile automated Knockoff assembly line, robots only, no human guards
Own secure computer system; keycards fail on the inner bioscanner door

wikiObservations.name: Mosquito
wikiObservations.summary: CH87: carries Len into Dynamis HQ and fights bravely in the assault, tackling Devilry with Acid Rain's teleport assist. But he is killed on the roof by Fallout, who tosses away his charbroiled corpse into Lab 66, the raid's first major casualty. His mind was backed up earlier via Livia's brainmaps, so his death need not be permanent across the loop.

facts.value: Airlifts Len into HQ; helps down Devilry
Killed and charbroiled by Fallout on the roof

wikiObservations.name: The Architect
wikiObservations.summary: CH88: Dynamis's designer of Lab Sixty-Six, mentioned as having engineered the facility to survive even the building's total collapse. She is not the same person as Chronoradio/Nora; here she is credited only as the structural genius behind the lab's fortress-grade construction (though it proved vulnerable to internal structural damage from Fallout's rockets).

facts.value: Designed Lab Sixty-Six to survive the building's collapse
Did not account for internal structural damage

wikiObservations.name: Alphonse Manada
wikiObservations.summary: CH88 (as Fallout / 'Atom Smasher'): the raid's true boss fight. His minigun/rockets/particle shields nearly overwhelm Ryan's crew; a chest-blaster shot only staggers him. When Ryan traps him in Mechron nanomachine goo, Fallout overrides his own safeties, shedding armor and humanity to become a blackened flaming skeleton of pure Red Flux, a self-sustaining nuclear core as durable as Leo Hargraves, melting the ground he stands on. He kills Mongrel (bisected by a stray beam) and, with Frank and Sarin, is buried alive when the factory ceiling collapses. Notably, Ryan's Black Flux devours Fallout's Red Flux like a black hole eating light.

facts.value: Blackened flaming skeleton of Red Flux, a living nuclear core, Hargraves-durable
Bisects Mongrel with a stray particle beam
His Red Flux is devoured by Ryan's Black Flux

ties.rel: his Red Flux is consumed by it

wikiObservations.name: Bloodstream
wikiObservations.summary: CH88: the horror at the heart of Lab Sixty-Six. Len's father survives as a house-sized shoggoth, a dark-red protoplasmic blob with temporary eyes, suspended in a mechanical aquarium and wired into the whole Knockoff system. His mutated blood is the raw source: pumped into modified clones of Knockoff templates (Wyvern, Devilry, Windsweep, an embryonic Panda) housed in glass pods as living organ processors, then processed into Knockoff Elixirs. Len recognizes him instantly and rushes to the glass; his eyes find his daughter. Blood calls to blood.

facts.value: House-sized red shoggoth in a mechanical aquarium, source of all Knockoffs
Len's father, reunited with her at last

ties.rel: his blood is the raw material

wikiObservations.name: Sarin
wikiObservations.summary: CH88: her sacrifice. Fighting Fallout with shockwaves despite her leaking, holed suit, she orders Ryan to grab the cure data and flee while she and Frank keep the nuclear Genome busy, judging the loop already lost now that Mongrel is dead. Ryan refuses to abandon her ('I'm not Adam'), and in that moment she finally gives him her real name: Bianca. She charges Fallout like a suicide bomber and is buried alive with him and Frank when the ceiling collapses. Ryan vows to save her next loop.

facts.value: Bianca (revealed to Ryan at last)
Sacrifices herself against Fallout; buried alive as the ceiling collapses

ties.rel: gives him her real name; he vows to save her next loop
charges him in a suicide attack

wikiObservations.name: Dr. Tyrano
wikiObservations.summary: CH88: works unbothered through the boss fight, more worried about lab damage than the invaders. Ryan captures him at water-rifle-point to open the inner bioscanner door. His true endgame is revealed: he is refining Knockoffs not just to change a host's species but its entire biological class, mammal to reptile, so he can 'consensually' turn any human into a dinosaur ('a fundamental mammalian right'). He is a scaled mad-scientist furry, and even Ryan half-sympathizes.
