facts.value: A Knockoff that turns humans into dinosaurs, consensually
Captured by Ryan to open the door to Bloodstream's chamber

wikiObservations.name: Mongrel
wikiObservations.summary: CH88: fights hard in the Lab 66 battle (aerokinetic blasts, fireballs, flanking Fallout) despite taking chest wounds, but is cut clean in half at lightspeed by a stray particle beam when Fallout's nanomachine prison cracks. His death is the emotional pivot that makes Sarin declare the loop lost. His Elixir/possibilities are eyed even in death (mind-backups mean it need not be permanent across loops).

facts.value: Bisected by a stray Fallout particle beam
His death convinces Sarin the loop is lost

wikiObservations.name: Frank the Mad
wikiObservations.summary: CH88: climbs the elevator shaft into the lab (absorbing machinery on contact) and tackles the nuclear Fallout head-on like a football player, powering through radiation as a patriotic American badass ('A Soviet Mexican! I knew it was all connected!'). But his metal hands soften against Fallout's heat; Alphonse punches a hole in his chest, and Frank is buried alive with Sarin when the ceiling collapses.

facts.value: Absorbs machinery on contact; tackles Fallout to buy Ryan time
Chest melted through, buried alive as the factory collapses

ties.rel: his bodyguard, buys him escape time

wikiObservations.name: Freddie Sabino
wikiObservations.summary: CH89 (flashback origin): the human behind Bloodstream. Born 1980 in Otranto, Italy, to a fisherman and housewife; married young, dropped out of college, became an Otranto municipal policeman (his only job). Abandoned by his wife before Last Easter, left to raise daughter Len (Lenora) and son Cesare alone. On Last Easter's eve he stole two Elixirs mistaken for drugs from his station and fled the apocalypse, becoming the Psycho Bloodstream by 2009. A loving but broken father whose delusions (he 'dreams of a Green Hell,' believes the Elixirs are Satan's poison) drive escalating abuse; he keeps his children isolated and dependent.

facts.value: b. 1980 Otranto; ex-municipal policeman; stole 2 Elixirs on Last Easter
Widower-by-abandonment; father of Len and the dead Cesare

wikiObservations.name: Mr. Wave
wikiObservations.summary: CH89: a Carnival member, 'the oddest of the group,' a creature of living wavelengths who speaks of himself in the third person and rarely takes things seriously. His firm moral line in the Bloodstream operation: no harming the children, even if they were Genomes.

facts.value: A being of living wavelengths
Refuses to harm children

wikiObservations.name: Stitch
wikiObservations.summary: CH89: the Carnival's plague-doctor medic and biological analyst. He examines Bloodstream's samples and delivers the chapter's terrifying reveal: the target's 'limits' (only human hosts, only ~10 clones) are purely psychological, not biological. Bloodstream can infect anything with a circulatory system; his self-hatred is the only cap on unlimited potential. Stitch also sterilizes areas after Leo incinerates each clone.

facts.value: Carnival medic / biologist; sterilizes incinerated clone sites
Bloodstream's limits are psychological, not biological

wikiObservations.name: The Laika
wikiObservations.summary: CH89: the ten-meter scavenged submarine Len built (named for the Soviet space dog) in the Porto Venere boathouse to carry the 'family' to America in ~12 days. Fully automated (no manual controls), it auto-redirects to the nearest shore on any problem, and once its autopilot+timer is engaged it cannot be disabled. In the origin loop, Len flees in it alone at Ryan's insistence while he goes to die with Bloodstream.

facts.value: 10m automated scavenged sub; ~12-day crossing; autopilot can't be disabled once set

wikiObservations.name: Porto Venere
wikiObservations.summary: CH89: the small abandoned coastal town near Genoa on the Tyrrhenian Sea where Ryan (as Cesare), Len, and Bloodstream hid in the origin loop, in a former boat club whose boathouse held the Laika. Isolated enough to stay hidden from the Carnival, close enough to Genoa for supply runs.

facts.value: Origin-loop hideout of Bloodstream's 'family'

wikiObservations.name: The Violet Elixir
wikiObservations.summary: CH89 (origin): the Violet Elixir Ryan (as Cesare) secretly kept in a syringe throughout the origin loop, hidden because Bloodstream could only sense Elixirs inside a Genome's blood (so he'd know the instant Ryan used it). At the chapter's climax, out of desperation as the Carnival attacks, Ryan injects it into his own arm for the very first time and 'the world turned purple' as he runs. This is the birth of his Violet time-manipulation power and, ultimately, his save-point loop.

facts.value: The Elixir Ryan first injects in the origin loop, granting Violet time-power
Undetectable to Bloodstream until injected into a Genome's blood

ties.rel: the bonding that sets his loop

wikiObservations.name: Bloodstream
wikiObservations.summary: CH89 (Carnival dossier + origin): Green/Blue Psycho whose powers mutated into a unique synergy. His Green power is total control of his own blood (weapons, tentacles, restructuring); his Blue power turned him into pure information carried in every blood cell, so he reforms as long as one cell survives (only disintegration kills him). If his blood enters another's circulatory system he overwrites their DNA, mind, and memories, converting them into a clone of himself, hence a four-digit body count and a loose clone hive-mind. Crucially, his human-only, ~10-clone 'limits' are purely psychological: if his daughter Len dies, he loses all restraint and becomes the 'Bloodstream plague,' an extinction event that could infect Earth's entire biosphere within months. Prophesied by Pythia.

facts.value: Green(blood control)/Blue(pure info); each cell hosts his mind, reforms from one
His blood in your bloodstream overwrites you into a copy of him
If Len dies he becomes an extinction-level plague; limits are psychological

ties.rel: her death is his doomsday trigger

wikiObservations.name: Cesare
wikiObservations.summary: CH89 (origin loop): the identity Ryan lived under before he had any power. Len's real brother Cesare died (confirmed only around 2012), and the delusional Bloodstream refuses to accept it, forcing Ryan to be 'Cesare.' In the origin loop Ryan-as-Cesare is Bloodstream's captive stepson: he endures the Psycho's rambling love-and-abuse ('your sister is sick'), pities then re-hates him, and secretly plots his death. He deliberately leads the Carnival to the hideout, then injects his Violet Elixir to try to save Len. This is the seed of every future loop.

facts.value: Ryan's pre-power identity, forced on him by Bloodstream's denial of Cesare's death
Baits the Carnival to the hideout to get Bloodstream killed

ties.rel: the identity he was forced into

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: CH89 (origin loop): teenage Lenora Sabino, the 'Genius' who scavenge-built the submarine Laika to carry the family to America. In love with Ryan (their clumsy first night together), but she refuses again and again to abandon her father, clinging to the kind man he once was ('as long as he's alive, there's a chance he can heal'). When the Carnival attacks, Ryan forces her onto the Laika alone and goes back to die; she sets the irreversible autopilot and begs him to return. Her survival is literally the fate of the world: her death triggers Bloodstream's extinction plague.

facts.value: Built the Laika; refuses to abandon her father
Her death is Bloodstream's doomsday trigger

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH89 (origin loop, as 'Cesare'): the pre-power Ryan. A captive stepson of the delusional Bloodstream, secretly in love with Len, worn down by the Psycho's abuse and the constant fear he'll one day feed on his own daughter. Unable to convince Len to abandon her father, Ryan takes the desperate gambit: he deliberately leads the Carnival to their Porto Venere hideout, forces Len onto the Laika, and returns to die alongside Bloodstream. As the battle rages he injects his hidden Violet Elixir for the first time ('the world turned purple, and Ryan ran'), the moment that begins his time-looping existence.

facts.value: First injects his Violet Elixir here, birthing his time-loop power
Baits the Carnival to kill Bloodstream; sends Len away on the Laika

ties.rel: injects it for the first time

wikiObservations.name: The Carnival
wikiObservations.summary: CH89: a resilient, cell-structured band of pro-bono wandering-hero Genomes led by Leo Hargraves, gathering only for debriefs or major ops. Members seen: Leo (the Living Sun), Mr. Wave, Stitch (medic), Mathias Martel (info-gatherer), Ace, the Cossack, and the seer Pythia. They hunt Bloodstream in the origin loop, planning to incinerate every clone (Leo) and sterilize the sites (Stitch) while evacuating the children, only to learn from Stitch that Bloodstream's true power is unlimited and that Len's death would end the world.

facts.value: Cell-based, highly resilient; unites only for big operations
Hunts Bloodstream; goal: destroy every clone, protect the children

ties.rel: their target in the origin loop

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH90 (origin, 'The First Run'): Ryan discovers his power in real time, a 10-second time-stop with a 10-second cooldown. On his first attempt he steps out of the smoke and shouts at the Carnival to stop; the distraction lets Bloodstream infect and kill Ace, and Bloodstream, no longer recognizing 'Cesare,' crushes Ryan's skull, his first death. He wakes rewound to a checkpoint: his power also creates a save-point. This run he stays hidden and lets Bloodstream die in Leo's fireball, but can't outrun the blast (light beats his 10-second window) and dies again, waking in the Carnival infirmary. Len and the Laika are gone; he loops the explosion endlessly, never catching her, and is left alone, the numb, grieving seed of the man he becomes.

facts.value: 10s time-stop, 10s cooldown; death creates a reload checkpoint
Loses Len forever; traps in the unwinnable Porto Venere explosion loop

ties.rel: loses her on the Laika, never catches up

wikiObservations.name: Elixir Mechanics
wikiObservations.summary: CH90: Ryan's Violet power is revealed in full at its origin. A ~10-second time-stop (10s cooldown), and crucially, dying rewinds him to a checkpoint set by his power ('like video games'), proven when Bloodstream kills him and he wakes back on the walkway. In this first loop the checkpoint lands at the worst moment, just before Leo's fireball, so no matter what he tries he keeps dying to the blast and can never reach the departed Len. The loop is not a one-time thing, it is his permanent condition from here on.

facts.value: Death rewinds Ryan to his power's checkpoint; not one-time, permanent
Locked just before the Porto Venere fireball, an unwinnable window

wikiObservations.name: Mr. Wave
wikiObservations.summary: CH90: shines in the Bloodstream fight. A creature of living wavelengths who moves at lightspeed in laser form, but only in a straight line and must revert to human form to turn (his worst fear: being ejected into space unable to turn back). He shreds Bloodstream repeatedly to stop him regenerating, and repeatedly shields the powerless Ryan with his own body from Leo's fireball, waking him in the Carnival infirmary each loop and gently helping him ('the adventurer's gate' window exit). Blames himself for Ryan's wounds. His comic third-person bravado hides genuine heroism.

facts.value: Lightspeed laser, straight-line only; must revert to human form to turn
Repeatedly shields Ryan from the fireball; tends him in the infirmary

wikiObservations.name: Ace
wikiObservations.summary: CH90: the Carnival's freckled teleporter, on standby to evacuate the wounded to Stitch's infirmary. In Ryan's first attempt his distraction gets her killed, Bloodstream's blood volley hits her throat and converts her mid-scream into a copy of himself. On the reload where Ryan stays hidden, Mr. Wave downs Bloodstream in time and Ace escapes unharmed with the Cossack. Her death-or-survival is the clearest lesson of Ryan's first reload.

facts.value: Teleporter; opens portals to Stitch's infirmary
Killed by Bloodstream in the failed run, saved in the reload

ties.rel: killed then spared depending on Ryan's choice

wikiObservations.name: Enrique Manada
wikiObservations.summary: CH90 (origin epilogue): 'Blackthorn.' Hector's more principled son, brother of Alphonse. He quietly directs Dynamis to support the Carnival's Bloodstream hunt (movement reports via Dynamis agents, blood-sample analysis via Dr. Tyrano) 'on principle', a better world has fewer Psychos. He dreams of an Italy reborn under the rule of law rather than Genome strength, and hopes Dynamis and the Carnival can one day unite against Augustus. He insists Bloodstream's samples be destroyed, overruling his father's and Alphonse's wish to keep the world-changing power.

facts.value: Blackthorn; the principled Manada son
Backs the Carnival's hunt; orders Bloodstream's samples destroyed

wikiObservations.name: Alphonse Manada
wikiObservations.summary: CH90 (origin epilogue, as Fallout): already the glowing skeleton in a black hazmat suit. He personally incinerates Dynamis's copy of Bloodstream's blood samples, but resents it, he and even Hector saw the god-tier potential of a power that rewrites genetic code in an instant. He tells Enrique he disposed of the samples ('Yes,' after a telling pause) and signs off with his creed 'All for the dream.' The seed of Dynamis's later Knockoff program: they knew exactly what Bloodstream's blood could do.

facts.value: Incinerates Dynamis's Bloodstream samples, resentfully
Dynamis knew the blood's genetic-rewrite power (later Knockoffs)

wikiObservations.name: Bloodstream
wikiObservations.summary: CH90: seen in full combat at Porto Venere's Marina. He fights the Carnival trio (Leo, the Cossack, Mr. Wave) as a red blur that leaps like a flea, crystallizes blood into spikes/axes, stretches tentacle limbs, and reforms in seconds from any hit, only Leo's fireball or total incineration can end him. His shrieking, childlike delusion ('why does everyone harass me?!') breaks when Ryan's Elixir seems to shatter the 'Cesare' illusion: he no longer recognizes Ryan, demands 'where is my son?!' and crushes his skull. His last clone finally dies in Leo's fireball; Dynamis and the Carnival incinerate every sample after.

facts.value: Blood spikes/axes, tentacle limbs, flea-like leaps, seconds-fast regen
Last clone incinerated by Leo's fireball at Porto Venere

ties.rel: no longer recognizes Ryan as his son

wikiObservations.name: Bloodstream
wikiObservations.summary: CH91: Dynamis has held him since 2016 (cloned from warehouse-raid samples), chemically neutered and reduced to <50% human DNA, a non-sentient 'company asset' (Tyrano's Monster Girl Project folder hints at worse). But Len's proximity re-triggers the dormant infection her father implanted in her blood; when her converted tendrils touch the aquarium, Bloodstream detonates free and mutates far past his old self: house-sized ooze with fanged maws, TV-screen eyes, Green Flux geysers spawning alien moss, generating mass from nowhere. He devours Len and Tyrano, and every Knockoff across New Rome reverts at once, an unlimited-range extinction plague. He can now use the powers of Genomes he infects (he takes Acid Rain's raindrop-swap). This is the doomsday the Carnival always feared.

facts.value: Held by Dynamis since 2016, neutered, <50% human DNA, non-sentient
Freed via infected Len; becomes rangeless world-virus, uses infected Genomes' powers

ties.rel: her infection frees and merges with him
all revert to him at once

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: CH91: her tragic end this loop. Bloodstream long ago implanted a foreign agent in her blood (which is why Knockoffs react violently to her, and why Tyrano wanted to study her). Confronted with the truth that her father is <50% human and unsavable, she goes silent and, standing before the aquarium, shoots the glass, her proximity having already let the infection take her over (black blood behind her visor). Her converted body merges with Bloodstream, freeing and empowering him; the monster devours his own daughter. Her death is literally the trigger the Carnival prophesied.

facts.value: Bloodstream implanted a foreign agent in her blood years ago
Infected and absorbed into Bloodstream, freeing the world-plague

ties.rel: infected by and merged into him

wikiObservations.name: Dr. Tyrano
wikiObservations.summary: CH91: reveals the Knockoff cure exists, an injection-based neutralizing agent that repairs a host's genetic code to its pre-consumption state (a stronger variant floods the aquarium on breach), effective on Bloodstream-based Knockoffs but not true Alchemist Elixirs. He insists mass-reversion risk is 'nonexistent' (fatally wrong). Ryan 'nationalizes' him and the cure, planning to take him to a Mechron base (Area 51) to make safe Knockoffs and keep his promise to Bianca. Tyrano cheerfully agrees to be 'abducted' for a Mechron lab, but drowns in Bloodstream's flood before escape; Ryan keeps his encrypted-email codes and the vaccine data for the next loop.

facts.value: Injectable agent repairs Knockoff genetic code; useless once Bloodstream goes rangeless
Nationalized by Ryan, then drowned in the Bloodstream flood

wikiObservations.name: Enrique Manada
wikiObservations.summary: CH91: 'Blackthorn' finally breaks with his father, arriving at Lab 66 with Fallout and a security troop, vine-and-moss armor, no firearm, disgusted by the aquarium. He admits 'none of this would have happened if you and father didn't lie to me,' says Wyvern was right and their father will be 'out of the picture,' one way or another. He tries and fails to save Tyrano with his vines; Alphonse shields them both from the blood flood. His long-held veto against studying Len (raising Ryan's respect for him) is now moot.

facts.value: Breaks with Hector; sides with Wyvern's stance against the Knockoffs
Vine/moss armor (Blackthorn); unarmed

ties.rel: arrives with him, is shielded by him

wikiObservations.name: Augustus
wikiObservations.summary: CH91: descends on the burning New Rome having won the Lepiromachia (holding a destroyed rabbit-plushie's charred half). He shrugs off Ryan's time-stop entirely (neither he nor his lightning slow), vaporizes Mr. See-Through with crimson lightning, and cares only for killing Leo Hargraves ('a world where your sun has set') over the world ending. But when Ryan's Saturn armor absorbs a bolt and he punches Augustus, black-and-violet particles swirling, the tyrant recoils: 'I felt that', the first blow that ever reached him, a flash of fear beneath the god-mask. Augustus counters harder than anyone Ryan's fought, breaching his armor, then duels Leo (whose burning core is his one weakness).

facts.value: Won the plushie-gods' war; killed the rabbit deity
Ryan's Black-particle punch is the first thing to ever hurt him ('I felt that')

wikiObservations.name: Mr. See-Through
wikiObservations.summary: CH91: the glass-armor vigilante (Shroud/Safelite operative) surveys the Bloodstream apocalypse alongside Leo Hargraves, urging Leo to unleash his full supernova to buy the rest of the world time even at the cost of millions in New Rome. Before they can act, Augustus descends and vaporizes him with a crimson lightning bolt through the chest, his organs cooked inside his own glass armor. His death underlines that even the loop's antagonists are helpless before the plague and Augustus.

facts.value: Urged Leo's supernova to contain the plague
Vaporized by Augustus's crimson lightning

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH91: this raid-loop ends in total disaster, but it's the one where his endgame crystallizes. He nationalizes Tyrano and the Knockoff cure, downloads the vaccine data and Tyrano's encrypted-email codes for the next loop, and watches Bloodstream's world-plague consume Len, New Rome, and the planet. Fleeing to Livia in Sorrento for the memory transfer, he confronts Augustus and, for the first time ever, hurts him with a Black-particle punch ('I felt that'), realizing the Black Ultimate One's wish granted him a paradox: a power that can kill immortals. He completes Livia's brainmap transfer as Augustus closes in and resets, uncertain his power is even the same now that the Black World courses through him.

facts.value: Knockoff vaccine data + Tyrano's email codes for the next run
His Black power is a paradox that can hurt/kill immortals like Augustus

ties.rel: completes her memory transfer before resetting

wikiObservations.name: The Black Ultimate One
wikiObservations.summary: CH91: its granted wish is finally understood. When Ryan's punch actually hurt the invulnerable Augustus ('I felt that'), he realizes what the Black Ultimate One gave him: a paradox, a power that can kill immortals. Combined with the Black World's energy now coursing through his veins, this reset is a dive into the unknown, his looping power may not even work the same way anymore.

facts.value: A paradox: the power to hurt and kill the immortal (proven on Augustus)

ties.rel: the immortal Ryan's paradox can hurt

wikiObservations.name: Livia
wikiObservations.summary: CH91: waits for Ryan on a Sorrento rooftop ringed by hundreds of Vulcan-built turrets vaporizing every Bloodstream clone, her precognition showing the blood-rain apocalypse. Despite Ryan's warning she gently touches his acid/Augustus wounds. She receives the loop's data and the brainmap memory transfer via the Saturn armor's Chronoradio helmet, vowing that next loop Ryan 'won't carry this cross alone' and that they'll find a painless transfer so he needn't die for their mistakes. Her surviving memory is the anchor that makes the next run different from every loop before.

facts.value: Receives the memory transfer; her mind carries across the reset
Next loop Ryan won't loop alone; find a painless transfer

wikiObservations.name: Henriette
wikiObservations.summary: CH92: a filthy stray street dog (a mastiff-greyhound mongrel, flea-ridden, foul-smelling) Ryan adopts on his way to Renesco's bar, buying her loyalty with a ham. A cat person by preference, he uses her as a weapon against the skeletal Ghoul, siccing her to gnaw his bones (she proudly retrieves his femur). A recurring bit of Ryan's dark comedy; he keeps her in his Plymouth Fury with food on hand.

facts.value: Mastiff-greyhound mongrel stray, adopted with a ham
Ryan's comic anti-Ghoul weapon; chews his bones

wikiObservations.name: Night Terror
wikiObservations.summary: CH92: real name Richard Pinkman, a gaunt, pallid, sunlight-shunning hitman-telepath whose power (nightmares made real, functioning only in darkness) once tormented Ryan across loops. Ryan finally delivers his overdue 'package': a single punch that knocks him out cold, revenge for the childhood traumas Night Terror made real (and the therapy bills). Lives in a condemned-window bungalow near Jamie's house.

facts.value: Richard Pinkman
KO'd by Ryan in a one-punch revenge visit

ties.rel: knocked out by him in revenge

wikiObservations.name: Livia
wikiObservations.summary: CH92: the first ally to fully carry her memories across a reset, and it delights her, she greets Ryan with a theatrical fake-betrayal 'villain speech' (claiming Cancel waits outside) purely because she always wanted to, then apologizes. Now Ryan's true co-strategist: she runs precognitive simulations (the Bloodstream pandemic's odds spike if Alphonse takes over Dynamis), sketches a May calendar of the three calamities, and plans the perfect run, Ryan joins Augustus's mob as a double-agent, rebuilds the mind-transfer machine via Vulcan, and returns Narcinia to make peace with the Carnival. She insists the resets be made painless and that Ryan stop martyring himself: 'a perfect ending for everyone includes you too.'

facts.value: First to remember across a reset; Ryan's permanent co-strategist
Simulations date the calamities; maps the perfect-run sequence

ties.rel: will introduce Ryan to rebuild the machine

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH92 (new loop, 'Best Laid Plans'): Ryan opens with cathartic revenge rounds, ramming Ghoul again, feeding his bones to his new stray dog Henriette, and one-punching Night Terror (Richard Pinkman). Then he and the now-memory-carrying Livia plan the endgame around three overlapping calamities: the Meta-Gang seizing Mechron's satellite (~May 12-18), Augustus's war with the incoming Carnival (~May 28), and Bloodstream. His plan: play Carnival double-agent, rebuild the mind-transfer machine via Vulcan, have Stitch/Tyrano turn the Knockoff vaccine into a 'vaccine plague' to erase Bloodstream, and neutralize Len's implanted sample. He admits it's taken dozens of resets and isn't the final loop yet.

facts.value: Solve satellite + Carnival war + Bloodstream in one sequenced run
Carnival double-agent, Vulcan's tech, a Knockoff 'vaccine plague'

ties.rel: co-plans the perfect run with her
wants him to weaponize the Knockoff vaccine

wikiObservations.name: Eugene-Henry
wikiObservations.summary: CH93: Ryan's aristocratic pet cat, an aloof, noble-mannered feline who treats the newly-adopted stray dog Henriette like a peasant, ignoring her nuzzling entirely. Part of the menagerie Ryan keeps at the Rust Town orphanage and in his Plymouth Fury (alongside Henriette and the sulking plushie).

facts.value: Ryan's noble-mannered pet cat; snubs the dog Henriette

wikiObservations.name: Julie Costa
wikiObservations.summary: CH93: mother of Narcinia (the Costa daughter). Ryan promises Shroud he will destroy the Bliss Factory and return 'Julie Costa's daughter' to the Carnival, framing Narcinia's rescue from Augustus's exploitation as returning her to the Costa family. Referenced as the wronged parent behind Narcinia's captivity.

facts.value: Narcinia's mother; the wronged 'Costa' parent

wikiObservations.name: Pythia
wikiObservations.summary: CH93: real name Alice Martel, the Carnival's seer and Mathias Martel's (Shroud's) mother. Her precognition drove the Carnival's whole strategy: she ranked the world's threats, placing Bloodstream at the very top, foreseeing he would cause an extinction event if Len (Bloodstream's daughter) died. Revealed to be still alive, gravely wounded fighting Mechron but recovering in Denmark with her husband. After she fell ill, Mathias tried to fill her role but cannot see the future, which is why he values Quicksave's foreknowledge.

facts.value: Alice Martel
Alive; wounded vs Mechron, recovering in Denmark
Ranked Bloodstream top threat; extinction if Len dies

ties.rel: foresaw him as the extinction-level threat

wikiObservations.name: Mathias Martel
wikiObservations.summary: CH93: as Shroud, Ryan's first recruit for the perfect-run alliance. Ryan tells him almost everything (minus, at first, the time travel), gives him a sample of Len's blood to prove the Knockoffs are made from Bloodstream, and wins him over. Mathias reveals his mother is the seer Pythia (Alice Martel), which is why the Carnival's plans were so effective, and that Augustus is fated to eventually attack Dynamis and conquer Europe by force to leave Livia queen of the ashes. Too sharp to fool, he deduces Ryan is not just a time-freezer but a true chronokinetic who loops time; Ryan takes a leap of faith and all-but-confirms it. Mathias commits fully.

facts.value: First recruited Avenger; deduces Ryan is a chronokinetic looper
Son of the seer Pythia; warns of Augustus's coming all-out war

ties.rel: recruited ally who learns his time-loop secret

wikiObservations.name: The Killer Rabbit Plushie
wikiObservations.summary: CH93: darkly comic aftermath of the Leporimachia, having been beaten so thoroughly by Augustus, the eldritch murder-plushie has lost its will to kill. Now permanently switchable-on yet inert: it sits sulking, its shadow shrunk by half, the alien whispers silent, refusing to enter cute mode, fire lasers, or kill even when a preteen (Little Sarah) is present. Ryan realizes it could always step outside his 'pentagram' and was only ever pretending to be bound. Augustus effectively gave the demon depression; it now just glares south at Mount Augustus.

facts.value: Post-Leporimachia: inert, will-to-kill broken by Augustus
Was never truly bound; could always activate itself

ties.rel: broke its will in the Leporimachia

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: CH93: amnesiac Len, atop the orphanage roof, hears Ryan's full tale (time travel, downloadable memories, her father alive as Bloodstream, her own death). She believes her oldest friend despite the insanity, and asks how she died: Ryan explains the blood sleeper-agent turned her into her father, and warns her feelings for him may not be her own while the infection remains. She wavers on the memory transfer, fearing it will change her, but has not refused. Backstory filled in: after the origin she was carried by the Laika to the Canary Islands, wandered years finding she couldn't fix a broken world, and admits she waited for Ryan and her father to the last second before letting the sub take her. Ryan vows not to abandon her.

facts.value: Laika carried her to the Canary Islands; wandered years
Fears the memory transfer will change her; undecided

ties.rel: he seeks her consent for the memory transfer
her infection may be shaping her feelings for him

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH93 'Defenders of the Realm': Ryan builds his alliance for the perfect run. He counsels amnesiac Len and seeks her consent for the memory transfer, then recruits Shroud/Mathias (proving the Knockoff-Bloodstream link with Len's blood, and taking a leap of faith to all-but-confirm his chronokinetic looping), and finally cold-calls the Panda (Timmy). He plans to sic Sunshine on Mechron's other bases (hoping to self-detonate the Bahamut satellite), turn Enrique/Blackthorn against Hector and Fallout, and reserve Augustus for himself, admitting he only has a 'maybe' for defeating the emperor. Learns Augustus is fated to wage an all-out war to leave Livia queen of the ashes.

facts.value: Shroud/Mathias and the Panda into his 'Avengers'
Sunshine hunts Mechron bases; flip Enrique; Augustus is Ryan's own

wikiObservations.name: The Killer Rabbit Plushie
wikiObservations.summary: CH94: the plushie's post-Leporimachia depression turns suicidal, it hangs itself with a rope in the orphanage kitchen and stages a bathtub-and-jumper-cable scene, terrifying the orphans. Ryan reads it as the monster (which never understood death) now trying to understand it by experiencing it, mirroring his own centuries-ago suicidal phase. It eyes Ryan's A-bomb with interest. Ryan also grasps in horror that it was never contained: it could always activate itself and had been silently watching him for centuries.

facts.value: Suicidal, stages hangings; eyes Ryan's A-bomb

ties.rel: haunts its maker; covets his bomb

wikiObservations.name: Fortuna
wikiObservations.summary: CH94: Ryan's 'living cheat code' for the Mechron raid, her Yellow luck-Elixir (a guardian-angel power bending events her way) is his answer to breaking Mechron's mainframe without endless loops. Vain and oblivious, she joins Livia's mission out of pure loyalty ('if a friend needs help, you give it no questions asked') without even asking why, dons a useless golden domino mask, and gushes about her boyfriend, revealed (to Ryan's delight) to be a mortified Mathias Martel/Shroud, whom her Elixir seems to be steering toward her. Her one true threat on the Meta roster is the Land, who has killed her before.

facts.value: The 'cheat code' whose luck-Elixir cracks Mechron's systems
Boyfriend is a reluctant Mathias Martel; her Elixir steers it

ties.rel: the one Meta foe who has killed her

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH94 'Cheat Code' (May 10th): on the revised loop Ryan preempts Psyshock's orphanage raid, freezing time to bubble Mosquito and Mongrel with Len's water rifle and huffing Psyshock full of Bliss in under a minute. He assembles his 'Avengers' (Len, Panda, Shroud) and forges a temporary alliance with Livia's team (Livia, Fortuna, Cancel) to destroy the Meta-Gang's Mechron weapons cache. His plan: use Fortuna's luck-Elixir as a 'living cheat code' to crack Mechron's mainframe instead of grinding loops, jail Psychos in Len's crush-depth underwater asylum rather than killing them, and time Cancel's execution of Psyshock to coincide with the Junkyard assault for maximum chaos.

facts.value: One-minute takedown of Psyshock, Mosquito, Mongrel
Fortuna's luck as a 'cheat code' vs Mechron's mainframe

ties.rel: recruits her luck-Elixir as his cheat code

wikiObservations.name: Livia
wikiObservations.summary: CH94: co-architect of the anti-Mechron operation, arriving as Queen Crimson with Fortuna and Cancel. She brokers the fragile alliance with the Carnival's Shroud (whose secret identity and relationship with her 'best friend' she calmly reveals she knows), insists her father Augustus stays ignorant, and frames the goal as destroying the Mechron cache because her visions show the tech harms whoever holds it. She has timed the whole strike from Ryan's intel but admits she still can't see Ryan himself: 'Surprise me, Quicksave.'

facts.value: Times the strike; brokers the Carnival alliance behind Augustus's back

wikiObservations.name: The Panda
wikiObservations.summary: CH94: Timmy joins Quicksave's Avengers, arriving on his 'fearsome bicycle' too eager to fight. Shroud, expecting to dismiss him, instead judges heroism by heart over skill and welcomes him. The Panda is invigorated by the honor of serving the Carnival but recoils at Cancel's casual talk of killing, and Ryan reassures his 'young Pandawan' they'll bring foes in 'by the book.' Names his transformation 'the most powerful creature on Earth.'

facts.value: Joins the Avengers; balks at lethal methods

ties.rel: welcomed into the Carnival by him

wikiObservations.name: Psyshock
wikiObservations.summary: CH94: leads the Meta-Gang's orphanage raid (with Mosquito and Mongrel) on May 10th, taunting 'Little Cesare' and 'Little Len' about her dead father. Ryan, saving his cruelty for this one enemy, curbstomps him in half a minute, huffing his tentacled true form full of Bliss until he collapses drooling. Captured and handed to Cancel to be executed on Livia's signal, timed to coincide with the Junkyard assault.

facts.value: Bliss-huffed unconscious in the orphanage raid; slated for execution

wikiObservations.name: Pale Guy
wikiObservations.summary: CH95: a minor Meta-Gang Psycho at the Junkyard bunker, glimpsed trapped in one of Len's water spheres during the raid (alongside Fuckface) as she assaults the base from its sea access. A background gang member, not a major combatant.

facts.value: Minor Meta-Gang Psycho, bubbled by Len in the raid

wikiObservations.name: Fuckface
wikiObservations.summary: CH95: a minor Meta-Gang Psycho at the Junkyard bunker, seen captured in one of Len's water spheres during the raid (alongside Pale Guy). A background gang member with a crude name, not a major combatant.

facts.value: Minor Meta-Gang Psycho, bubbled by Len in the raid

wikiObservations.name: Acid Rain
wikiObservations.summary: CH95: real name Helen. A Meta-Gang teleporter-assassin who conjures corrosive toxic clouds/raindrops and fights with knives, guarding the Junkyard bunker's tunnel. She flanks and nearly guts Ryan (whom she can't touch during Livia's skip since he phases out), holes his bowler hat with acid, and is finally caught when Livia, predicting her teleport with her Blue foresight, waits and bubbles her in a water sphere that follows her even as she rolls down a trash pile.

facts.value: Helen
Water-bubbled after Livia predicts her teleport

wikiObservations.name: Livia
wikiObservations.summary: CH95 'Double Date': in the field for the Junkyard raid, Livia proves a devastating partner. Her Blue foresight lets her hard-counter Acid Rain (predicting each teleport) and aim borrowed weapons; her secondary Violet 'skip forward' power freezes everyone into sleepwalking predestined actions while she acts freely (Ryan alone is uninteractable in it, so Acid Rain's knife phased through him). She and Ryan fight in flawless synergy against drones and Psychos, flirting mid-battle ('Only if you conquer France for our honeymoon'), and float the idea of a vacation loop together. She warns the Land (a Yellow/Orange with area-dominion) hard-counters Fortuna's luck.

facts.value: Blue foresight + Violet skip-forward; Ryan is uninteractable within it
Flawless combat synergy with Ryan; mutual flirting

ties.rel: battle partner and growing romantic interest

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH95: leads the Junkyard raid, masking their approach with Ghoul's severed foot (so the Land mistakes the car for her returning tenant), then blitzing the base with Livia, the Panda, Shroud, Fortuna and Len. Cancel's execution of Psyshock frees the thralls and sows chaos; the crew defeats the Reptilian, Acid Rain and the drones and breaches the blast door, trapped inside with Adam, Sarin and Frank waiting. Emotionally, Ryan settles that he and Len are now family (brother-sister), not romance, and for the first time in ages wonders what he wants from his life now that friends can remember him, sensing Livia is the key.

facts.value: Ghoul's foot masks the car from the Land's area-sense
Accepts Len as family; senses Livia is his future

ties.rel: intuits she is key to his future

wikiObservations.name: Adam the Ogre
wikiObservations.summary: CH96 'Beast of the East': the Meta-Gang's cannibal leader makes his last stand in the Junkyard bunker, wielding a salvaged Mechron gravity gun (a slow black projectile that shreds metal by pulling matter inward). He brainwashes Frank with a 'CIA is staging a coup, protect democracy' delusion, and his carbon skin shrugs off Ryan's Fisty punch entirely, teaching Ryan he needs the Saturn armor to focus Black Flux. Livia deduces his skin protects only the surface, so head trauma still concussions him; blinded by coil-gun rounds, he tries to Elixir-convert the Panda but the Panda absorbs it and finishes him with a 'Soaring Panda' kick. Len bubbles him and he drowns to death.

facts.value: A salvaged Mechron gravity gun (matter-pulling black shots)
KO'd by the Panda's kick, then drowned in Len's water bubble

ties.rel: killed by his kick after failing to Elixir-convert him

wikiObservations.name: Frank the Mad
wikiObservations.summary: CH96: real name Vladimir Khabarov, a Russian (from Novgorod, not the Arkansas of his delusion) whose false-patriot identity is a coping fiction. Adam pre-brainwashes him into 'protecting democracy' so he attacks Ryan's crew, but Livia, unable to hurt the metal giant physically, dismantles his mind instead: naming him Vladimir, exposing his soviet origins, and finally telling him 'you are the communists,' which shatters him into a catatonic pile of scrap. Sarin collapses the floor to trap him.

facts.value: Vladimir Khabarov, a Russian from Novgorod
Livia breaks his delusion; goes catatonic

wikiObservations.name: Ki-jung
wikiObservations.summary: CH96: mentioned among Ryan's Rust Town street contacts (with Jamie and Lanka) he intends to reconnect with now that his loops can carry friends' memories. Part of the low-level crew Ryan uses to infiltrate Dynamis 'from the bottom.'

facts.value: One of Ryan's Rust Town contacts for the Dynamis infiltration

ties.rel: part of the same street crew

wikiObservations.name: The Panda
wikiObservations.summary: CH96: the raid's MVP. When Adam tries to Elixir-convert him with a Blue Elixir (which normally can't bond to animals), the Panda's human-beneath lets him absorb it and, per Livia's foresight that he and her father could safely take two Elixirs, he gains a SECOND power, moving with focus instead of madness. He flies into a Bruce-Lee-style 'Soaring Panda' kick that caves in Big Fat Adam's skull, killing him. Timmy the disciple becomes a master.

facts.value: Absorbs Adam's Blue Elixir to gain a second power
Kills Adam the Ogre with the 'Soaring Panda' finisher

ties.rel: she foresaw he could safely take the Elixir

wikiObservations.name: Sarin
wikiObservations.summary: CH96: real name Bianca. Adam's Psycho enforcer (shockwave gauntlets, sealed hazmat suit) whom Ryan finally turns to his side: he refuses to fight her, disarms himself, and offers her his cure and a last chance at being human again. Her doubt seeded, she picks Ryan's side mid-battle, collapsing the floor to trap Frank and helping subdue the Meta-Gang, then aids Len in loading the captured Psychos into bathyspheres. Ryan tells the crew she 'will be very important later.'

facts.value: Defects to Ryan; joins subduing the Meta-Gang
Ryan promises a cure to restore her humanity

ties.rel: won over by his offer of a cure

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH96: leads the bunker's final fight, learning his Fisty punch can't focus Black Flux without the Saturn armor. He turns Sarin/Bianca to his side, sets up Adam's death, and wins a near-flawless victory (his only loss the car). The Meta-Gang is jailed underwater pending a cure; Adam drowns. Afterward he plots his next phase, infiltrate Dynamis from the bottom via Jamie/Ki-jung/Lanka, brief Alchemo/Len/Sarin on the memory map, have Vulcan rebuild the Saturn armor, deal with the Carnival, Narcinia and the Bliss Factory. Emotionally freed by having friends who can remember him, he finally makes his move on Livia and asks her out.

facts.value: Needs the Saturn armor to focus his Black Flux
Asks Livia on a date; near-flawless victory

wikiObservations.name: Livia
wikiObservations.summary: CH96: the battle's tactician, foreseeing the winning branch. She reveals Adam's carbon skin only protects the surface (head trauma still works), mentally destroys Frank by exposing his real identity (Vladimir Khabarov), and lets the Panda absorb Adam's Elixir because she predicted he could safely take two. Increasingly warm with Ryan (letting him rescue her repeatedly, 'you may rescue me as many times as you like'), she insists Shroud come clean to Fortuna. When Ryan finally makes his move and asks her out, she, unable to predict him, blushes and gasps in genuine surprise.

facts.value: IDs Adam's weakness, unmasks Frank, greenlights Panda's Elixir
Accepts Ryan's advance; can't foresee him, so it's a real surprise

ties.rel: grows close; he asks her out

wikiObservations.name: Origami
wikiObservations.summary: CH97: a Carnival member on Shroud's team who can turn herself into paper sharp enough to slice throats, and, Shroud boasts, even cut through Sarin's hazmat suit. Mentioned in passing as Shroud spars verbally with Sarin, a point of comparison for the Panda's own new origami skill.

facts.value: Transforms into razor-sharp paper

wikiObservations.name: The Monster Girl Project
wikiObservations.summary: CH97: Dr. Tyrano's secret, deeply disturbing side project, a demented attempt to create a 'monster girl' out of a mink (he 'couldn't do that to a reptile'). Ryan gains access to the file as leverage and is so horrified by the shrieking abomination on the video that he nearly falls off his chair; the first specimen died but Tyrano has a spare. A running gag underscoring Tyrano's amoral genius.

facts.value: Tyrano's grotesque mink-based 'monster girl' experiment

wikiObservations.name: Dr. Tyrano
wikiObservations.summary: CH97: Ryan recruits the saurian Genius by dangling the bunker's create-life lab, multi-power Genomes to study, and a Green Knockoff that could grant his dream of turning humans into dinosaurs. Tyrano is contractually bound to Dynamis for 200 years and can't leave HQ or sabotage the Knockoff supply, so Bloodstream still requires assaulting Lab 66 again. He signs on remotely for the Psycho-cure research (with Stitch), and Ryan extracts access to his files, including the horrifying 'Monster Girl Project.'

facts.value: Bound to Dynamis 200 years; won't sabotage Knockoffs
Joins the Psycho-cure team remotely for a dinosaur Knockoff

wikiObservations.name: The Panda
wikiObservations.summary: CH97: Len's tests reveal the Panda's new Blue power is ACCELERATED LEARNING, he masters origami, learns French by page five of Descartes, and picks up kung-fu in half an hour, adapting human techniques (Bruce Lee's flying kick from The Green Hornet) to his massive bear body, which is how he learned to 'fly.' His martial-arts 'Genius' was really this osmosis power all along. Ryan realizes he could learn almost any human skill, even Genius tech given time to observe it.

facts.value: Blue accelerated-learning: masters any human skill fast
His flying kick came from learning Bruce Lee's move

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: CH97: Len, still adjusting, pulls Ryan aside about Livia. She wistfully floats running away together on the Mechron sub, but Ryan gently refuses, he has too many people to fight for now, and won't abandon them. He reassures her she is family forever, his sister and most important person, regardless of anything with Livia. Persuaded that one must 'let the dead rest' rather than cling to her father's blood tracker, she finally agrees to both the memory transfer (to recover her other self's memories) and having the Carnival remove her infection, choosing to offer Ryan her hand as he offered his.

facts.value: Agrees to the memory transfer and to remove her blood tracker
Makes peace with Ryan's bond with Livia; stays family

ties.rel: reconciles herself to Ryan's relationship with her

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH97 'A Breath of Fresh Air' (day after the raid): Ryan consolidates his gains, recruiting Tyrano remotely, gifting the real A-bomb to Vulcan (and becoming her reluctant assistant), and giving the suicidal plushie a decoy prop bomb (then the gravity cannon). With Shroud he maps the Dynamis endgame: flip Enrique, but Alphonse/Fallout won't surrender Bloodstream's power-give-and-take monopoly, so Ryan will stop him with the bunker's resources and a rebuilt Saturn armor (chest-blaster swapped for the gravity cannon). He plans to destroy the bunker only after it solves the crisis, wins Len's consent to the memory transfer, and heads off for his date with Livia.

facts.value: Recruits Tyrano/Vulcan; plans an upgraded Saturn armor vs Alphonse
Destroy the bunker only after the crisis is solved

ties.rel: her assistant; gives her the A-bomb
targets him as the hardest Dynamis obstacle

wikiObservations.name: The Midnight Road
wikiObservations.summary: CH98: Ryan's name for a 'thin place', a natural space anomaly he takes Livia to on their date, reached by a particle-accelerator device hidden in his Plymouth Fury. A deserted, endlessly looping highway (~30 km before it folds back) under purple auroras that show mirages of alien realms (seas of mercury, floating ice, green lightning), with a duplicate highway visible in the distance where the travelers see themselves. Ryan believes it sits close to the Purple World, a border realm between Earth's reality and the crossroads of all space-time. It follows Earth's own timestream.

facts.value: A thin place / space anomaly; a looping interdimensional highway
Reached via Genius particle-accelerator tech

ties.rel: sits near it, a border realm
he named it and takes Livia there

wikiObservations.name: Thin Places
wikiObservations.summary: CH98: natural space anomalies where space-time folds due to gravitational or electromagnetic forces, likened to caves inside the 'mountain' of Earth's reality. Distinct from the colored dimensions above reality, they lie 'sideways' and follow the same timestream as our own. They require Genius tech to access. Ryan learned of them researching particle physics in Switzerland; the Midnight Road is one, and the deadly Monaco anomaly is implied to be another.

facts.value: Sideways space-time folds; same timestream, Genius-tech access only

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH98 'White Night': Ryan's date with Livia. He drives her to the Midnight Road (a thin place) via his car's particle accelerator, and there, in a rare act of total trust, unburdens his darkest secret: he once spent an ENTIRE full lifetime trapped in the Monaco anomaly, which is why he calls himself immortal, and has never dared start a family because loop-timing would produce a different child each reset. Livia is the only one he's ever told. The evening deepens into genuine intimacy; she brings him into her father's villa at Mount Augustus as an open act of rebellion, and they spend the night together.

facts.value: Lived a full lifetime trapped in the Monaco thin place
Consummates his relationship with Livia

ties.rel: his date and now lover; his sole confidant
takes her there on the date

wikiObservations.name: Livia
wikiObservations.summary: CH98: on her date with Ryan she experiences, for the first time in ~14 years, life without her foresight guiding her (she can't predict Ryan), finding it terrifying but refreshing, 'the unexpected' is his gift to her. She confesses she's seen the fuller lives she could have had with Felix but couldn't make them real ('watching is not living'), and vows to stop her father's coming war. Moved by Ryan's confession, she offers to share his burden. She dislikes sushi (a comic near-miss), and finally brings Ryan into her father's villa and her bed as a deliberate act of rebellion against Augustus.

facts.value: Ryan gives her 'the unexpected'; her power can't foresee him
Sleeps with Ryan in Augustus's villa as open rebellion

ties.rel: defies him openly by choosing Ryan

wikiObservations.name: Augustus
wikiObservations.summary: CH99 'How I Met Your Daughter': catches Ryan the morning after in his villa kitchen (Augustus sleeps standing utterly still like his own Jupiter statue). Enraged, he electrocutes Ryan with low-current lightning, discerning via the electrons in Ryan's brain that Ryan is the source of the time-stops. He cannot be harmed by Ryan (who lacks the Saturn Armor to focus his Black power). When Livia intervenes with her power and threatens to leave forever if he harms Ryan or Felix, the tyrant relents, a rare crack showing the lonely, paranoid old man beneath. He half-accepts Ryan with a triple death-threat (disrespect / break her heart / break up = 'I will kill you'), still refusing to acknowledge him otherwise. Grieves being unable to protect his late wife.

facts.value: Sleeps standing perfectly still, mistaken for a statue
Grudgingly tolerates Ryan under a triple death-threat

ties.rel: his daughter, who defies him to keep Ryan

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH99: wakes the morning after in Livia's bed feeling genuinely loved (she won't release him even asleep), and for the first time dreads a reset because he doesn't want Livia to forget him. Cooking her breakfast, he's caught by Augustus, taunts the tyrant with repeated time-stops, then confirms (defiantly) he slept with Livia and gets electrocuted. He confirms he still needs the Saturn Armor to harm Augustus. Saved by Livia, he weathers Augustus's triple death-threat and gives his real name ('Ryan Quicksave Romano, immortal'). Notes that lovemaking reveals character (Len hesitant, the Doll playful, Jasmine wild, Livia 'just right'). Agrees to be healed by Venus/Narcinia.

facts.value: For the first time fears a reset would make Livia forget him
Still needs the Saturn Armor to harm Augustus

ties.rel: electrocuted by then grudgingly accepted as boyfriend
his lover, who shields him from her father

wikiObservations.name: Livia
wikiObservations.summary: CH99: paints alternate-universe cities in her spare time (a happier-realities hobby). Rushing into the kitchen when her father electrocutes Ryan, she uses her power on Augustus to save him and openly claims Ryan as her boyfriend, revealing to her father that she knows he murdered Narcinia's parents. She refuses to step aside and threatens to leave the Augusti empire forever if he harms Ryan or Felix, a threat that visibly shakes the tyrant into relenting. Insists on taking Ryan to Venus/Narcinia to heal his lightning burns.

facts.value: Threatens to abandon the empire to protect Ryan and Felix
Knows Augustus killed Narcinia's parents

ties.rel: defies her father to keep Ryan
shields and claims him as boyfriend

wikiObservations.name: Andreas Torque
wikiObservations.summary: CH100 'Past Fragment: No Planet for Old Men' (~2005): Cardinal Andreas Torque, one of the youngest Cardinals and Inquisitor-General of the Malleus Maleficarum (the Vatican's secret service), investigates the escalating pre-Genome-age incidents (the Stanford Incident, Sarajevo's iron pillars, spontaneous combustions) and tracks the immortal teleporting geneticist Eva Fabre. He launders mafia money through Janus Augusti for a black budget. When Fabre's hive wipes out his order, they capture him and force Augustus's mind-opening crystal drug plus a Blue Elixir injection into him. His soul ascends into the Blue World and melds with the Ultimate One, an experience of divine rapture; cast back into his broken flesh he is left an addict craving only to return, indifferent as the old world burns. Strongly implied to be a proto-/origin story tied to the Blue-World Genius entity Alchemo.

facts.value: Cardinal + Inquisitor-General of the Malleus Maleficarum
Dosed with crystals + Blue Elixir; melds with the Ultimate One, left an addict of the Blue World
~2005, during the collapse of the old world (Last Easter)

ties.rel: hunted her; she has him experimented on
launders his mafia money; given the crystal drug by him
melds with it in the Blue World

wikiObservations.name: Eva Fabre
wikiObservations.summary: CH100: the human origin of The Alchemist. Once the lead geneticist of France's secret Antarctic bacteriological-weapons base Station Orpheon, where on Dec 12 1992 a purple flash and crash preceded a lethal outbreak that killed 22 of 23 researchers; Fabre's body was never found. By ~2005 she reappears un-aged, able to teleport (be in two places at once), running worldwide human experiments via a shell-company vaccine network ('New H'). She is revealed to be a legion, dozens/hundreds of blue-particle copies of herself with slight variations, an 'organization of one', who collapse into blue particles when killed. She now goes by 'the Alchemist', preaching that mankind must evolve past natural selection into intelligent design ('Our design') to face demons 'above our heads, in space'.

facts.value: The human name/origin of The Alchemist
A hive of blue-particle copies; immortal, teleporting
Ex-lead geneticist of Station Orpheon (Antarctica, 1992)

ties.rel: is the Alchemist's original human identity

wikiObservations.name: Janus Augusti
wikiObservations.summary: CH100 (~2005): elder patriarch of the Augusti mob dynasty, a Neapolitan Camorra boss in a red suit and Augustus's forebear (father of young Livia in this era, so Livia's grandfather-era figure). A godless 'necessary evil' who launders his blood money through Cardinal Torque's Vatican channel and serves as a patron of the Malleus Maleficarum's black budget. Cold, shark-like, expansionist. He gifts Torque a bag of colored crystals ('our new product', a mind-opening drug), tempting the priest's curiosity about contacting higher realms. Dotes on his little daughter Livia (who asked for a pony).

facts.value: Camorra patriarch; launders money via the Vatican
Introduces the colored-crystal mind-opening drug

ties.rel: Augusti-dynasty forebear of the modern patriarch
his money-launderer; gives him the crystal drug

wikiObservations.name: The Ultimate One
wikiObservations.summary: CH100: the divine intelligence at the center of the Blue World, glimpsed by Andreas Torque when the Blue Elixir + crystal drug sent his soul there. A bodiless psionic god of pure information, neither male nor female, ruling from a 'throne of information', all the universe's data focused into a singularity, the being an ascended mind melds into. It feels neither love nor hate, only curiosity: it disassembled Torque's mind to its molecules to understand him, then shared cosmic knowledge back (mathematics, chemistry, true history), an experience of unbearable rapture. The 'God' at the heart of the Akashic Records / Blue World that Blue-power ascension leads toward.

facts.value: Bodiless psionic god of pure information at the Blue World's center
Feels only curiosity; disassembles minds to understand them

wikiObservations.name: The Malleus Maleficarum
wikiObservations.summary: CH100: the Vatican's officially-nonexistent secret service, whose purpose is to keep the Pope aware of all threats to the faith and advance Catholic interests through covert means. Historically fought communism and terrorism; by ~2005 it turned to the unnatural incidents of the pre-Genome age. Funded by a laundered mafia black budget, invested in facial-recognition tech. Led by Inquisitor-General Cardinal Andreas Torque, with senior Inquisitor Ambrosio as his agent. Eva Fabre's hive systematically wiped the order out in days, killing Ambrosio and finally capturing Torque.

facts.value: The Vatican's deniable secret service / inquisition
Annihilated by Eva Fabre's hive in the old world's collapse

wikiObservations.name: The Stanford Incident
wikiObservations.summary: CH100: a pre-Genome-age catastrophe (Nov 14, ~2004) in the dying mining town of Stanford, Nevada (pop. 202). Repairman James Poole, given a New H 'tetanus vaccine' (actually a bottled Elixir) by Eva Fabre's delivery network, burst from the clinic as a faceless six-meter white-skinned beast trailing blue mist that turned bystanders feral, killing or vanishing half the town before escaping into the Mojave. One of the escalating covert human-experiment tragedies (alongside Sarajevo's iron pillars, Utah's invisible reptilian, Tajikistan's burning woman) by which Torque pieced together the Alchemist's worldwide testing program.

facts.value: A Elixir-vaccine test turned James Poole into a rampaging monster
A key clue in Torque's investigation of Eva Fabre

ties.rel: caused by her experiment / delivery network
the case that opens his investigation

wikiObservations.name: The Alchemist
wikiObservations.summary: CH100 origin: revealed to be Eva Fabre, once the lead geneticist of France's secret Antarctic base Station Orpheon, where a purple-flash crash in Dec 1992 preceded a lethal outbreak; she vanished un-aged. By ~2005 she is a legion, dozens/hundreds of teleporting blue-particle copies of herself with slight variations, an 'organization of one' that collapses into blue particles when killed. Under the name 'the Alchemist' she ran a worldwide covert human-experiment program (shell-company 'vaccine' deliveries via the New H front) that seeded the Elixirs, engineered the old world's collapse (Sarajevo's metal men, ICBMs), and preaches mankind must abandon natural selection for 'intelligent design' to survive the demons 'above our heads, in space'.

facts.value: Eva Fabre, ex-lead geneticist of Station Orpheon (Antarctica, 1992)
A legion of teleporting blue-particle self-copies
Forced human evolution ('intelligent design') to face coming cosmic threats

ties.rel: hunted and then experimented on him

wikiObservations.name: Mars
wikiObservations.summary: CH101: real name Luca Veran, a Camorra don and Augustus's follower who runs Triton's Resort. An Italian-George-Clooney charmer with blue eyes, father of Fortuna, Atom Kitty (Felix) and the abducted Narcinia. Warmly welcomes Ryan as Livia's boyfriend and floats a family dinner when Narcinia returns (May 14), but makes casual racist remarks about 'normies'. Ryan privately recalls Mars murdered Narcinia's real parents and abducted her as a baby. Attends the Augusti meeting scheduled for the 15th; pushes (with Venus) to destroy the Manada clan.

facts.value: Luca Veran
Camorra don, runs Triton's Resort; Augustus loyalist
Murdered Narcinia's real parents and abducted her

ties.rel: abducted her as a baby; raised as his daughter

wikiObservations.name: Venus
wikiObservations.summary: CH101: real name Andrea Julani-Veran, Fortuna's mother and a beautiful woman in her forties. Her power is limited to superficial aesthetic surgery, reshaping skin, eye color, hair (and, with sustained contact, potentially lethal reshaping), healing Ryan's lightning burns in a green flash. She runs Triton's Resort's prostitution/Bliss-addiction operation, using her face-reshaping power to sell celebrity/hero lookalikes and to hook clients on Bliss for blackmail. Colder and deadlier than her husband, she resents Ryan for 'usurping' her son Felix's place with Livia and quietly plots against him, pushing to destroy the Manada clan and reclaim Felix.

facts.value: Andrea Julani-Veran
Superficial aesthetic surgery (skin/hair/eyes; lethal only with contact)
Runs the resort's brothel + Bliss-addiction/blackmail racket

wikiObservations.name: Triton's Resort
wikiObservations.summary: CH101: a lavish Augusti-owned resort complex west of New Rome, on a hill between the Colosseum Maximus and Little Lilith (the red-light district). Glass domes, white spires, pleasure gardens, thermal pools and coastal views in Roman style; entrances are segregated by status. Run by Mars (Luca Veran) and Venus (Andrea Julani-Veran), it is publicly a luxury resort but privately the epicenter of New Rome's prostitution trade, using Venus's face-reshaping power to sell celebrity/hero lookalikes and hooking clients on Bliss for blackmail. Bugged throughout except Livia's private lovers' suite.

facts.value: The Augusti; operated by Mars and Venus
Center of New Rome prostitution + Bliss-addiction blackmail

ties.rel: keeps a private lovers' suite there

wikiObservations.name: Station Orpheon
wikiObservations.summary: CH101 (from CH100 lore): France's secret Antarctic bacteriological-weapons base and the likely site of the Alchemist's fortress that Ryan glimpsed in the Purple World, buried in snow and ice. Eva Fabre was its lead geneticist when a purple-flash crash and lethal outbreak wiped out the staff in Dec 1992. Livia connects Ryan's vision to it via a tale Bacchus told her: Bacchus was investigating the Alchemist before Last Easter and she 'twisted' him, leaving him deranged and Bliss-obsessed. Ryan flags finding this base as a Perfect Run objective, suspecting the Violet Ultimate One steered him toward it.

facts.value: France's secret Antarctic bioweapons base; the Alchemist's origin site
Ryan's Purple-World vision of an icebound fortress points here

ties.rel: her Antarctic base / origin (as Eva Fabre)

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH101 'Lover's Breath': officially asks Livia to be his girlfriend; she insists their relationship last 'until we choose to break up', not until a reset, refusing to let his power define its end. He shares his Perfect Run to-do list (Kill Psypsy, Cure the Psycho condition, Prevent the Leporimachia, Reconcile Wyvern & Vulcan, Find the Alchemist's Antarctic base, Bury my daddy issues, Make Livia happy); Livia strikes his other 'fuck/marry' goals and adds 'Be happy too', banning his suicide-reloads and his drugs. He offers Livia an endorphin-blocker Bliss cure and to tear down Triton's Resort for her. He's healed by Venus and resolves to eventually bring down Augustus and the Veran 'Olympians' for Livia's sake.

facts.value: Livia becomes his girlfriend; relationship not bound to resets
Accepts 'Be happy too'; agrees to stop suicide-reloads and drugs

ties.rel: his girlfriend, who reforms his habits and list
heals his burns; he clocks her as a deadlier enemy

wikiObservations.name: Mr. See-Through
wikiObservations.summary: CH102 'Moving On' (as Shroud): his relationship with Fortuna ruptures after he half-confessed on a date, that he came to New Rome to strike the Augusti and only ever 'protected' her from dangers he himself caused, but couldn't bring himself to sleep with her while lying. Fortuna, in denial about her family's crimes, gives him the cold shoulder. Ryan counsels him (with cat therapy) not to break it off, noting her luck-power still engineers romantic situations between them, a sign the relationship isn't dead. Shroud admits he's growing fond of her against his judgment, and secures Alchemo's agreement to try healing his brain-damaged mother (Pythia/Alice Martel).

facts.value: Confessed his anti-Augusti mission to Fortuna, causing estrangement
Gets Alchemo to attempt healing his mother's brain damage

ties.rel: his straining girlfriend, now in denial about her family
agrees to try healing Shroud's mother

wikiObservations.name: Fortuna
wikiObservations.summary: CH102: exhausted and foul-tempered after the Mechron raid (Ryan analyzes her luck-power: it warps this reality's causality in her favor within a <10 m radius, can't negate other Genomes' direct powers, so Mechron used long-range telekinetic machines against her). Estranged from Shroud after he confessed his anti-Augusti mission, she gives him the cold shoulder, defends her family, denies her father Mars's crimes, and transfers her affection to the adopted stray dog Henriette. Ryan believes her denial masks buried doubts about her parents' true nature.

facts.value: Luck warps causality within <10 m; can't stop direct powers or long-range attacks
Estranged from Shroud; in denial about her family; dotes on Henriette

ties.rel: adopts and dotes on the stray dog

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: CH102: her memory transfer is completed by Alchemo using his improved method (memories now coexist rather than overriding), so she recalls both this loop and the last, remembering that her father Bloodstream killed her. Stitch removes the Bloodstream strain from her body. She can only agree to help destroy her father once she's certain he's truly beyond saving, so Ryan delays the Dynamis raid. Learning (via the chronoradio) that Ryan is now dating Livia, she accepts it gracefully: they're 'family now', Livia is good for him, and, inspired by his happiness, she resolves to stop living in the fearful past and look forward. Both agree it's time to move on, together.

facts.value: Now carries both loops via Alchemo's coexisting-memory method
Accepts Ryan+Livia; resolves to move on from the past

ties.rel: accepts her as Ryan's partner; 'family now'

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH102: consolidates the post-raid gains, Mechron's mainframe lets him recreate the Saturn Armor and probe his new Black power. Stitch (with Dr. Tyrano's help) develops an airborne vaccine for the Psycho condition and a viral Bliss cure (endorphin blockers + nerve suppressant) from Ryan's own recipe; the Panda, via accelerated learning, has absorbed multiple doctorates to serve as lab assistant. Ryan counsels Shroud through his Fortuna rift, delays the Dynamis raid until Len is ready, and sets the next plan: after hitting the Bliss Factory, blow the bunker and flee New Rome for Antarctica (Station Orpheon) to find the Psycho cure's source, with a stop near Monaco. He affirms he no longer wants to die and wants lifetimes with Livia and Len.

facts.value: Delay Dynamis raid; head for Antarctica (via Monaco) for the Psycho cure
No longer wants to die; wants lasting lifetimes with loved ones

ties.rel: delays the raid on her father until she's ready
develops the vaccine and Bliss cure with him

wikiObservations.name: Bacchus
wikiObservations.summary: CH103 'Drug Bust': revealed to be Andreas Torque, the former Vatican Cardinal from CH100, now the Augusti Olympian who cooks Bliss at the Ischia superlab and is obsessed with returning to the Blue World's Ultimate One ('Heaven') he tasted via his Elixir. A gaunt, unblinking, corpse-like fanatic who reveres the Alchemist / Eva Fabre as a divine prophet (having tracked and met her once on Last Easter, when she 'enlightened' him). He mentors young Narcinia (whom he calls Ceres, after breaking her mind), endorses Bliss's sterilization as sorting God's 'chosen' from the unworthy, and gives Ryan the Station Orpheon coordinates while insisting the base was found empty after a violet flash. It cannot tell one human from another (hinting the captive Elixirs are still being conditioned) and turns cold when refused. Ryan deduces that Elixirs being MUTE in normal use is likely the Alchemist's deliberate design feature, not a bug - a talking, willful Elixir is far harder to control. The Elixirs share fear of 'them' when alien footsteps approach.

facts.value: A sapient, telepathic, child-like being that wants to possess a human host
Elixir muteness is likely an intentional Alchemist control feature

wikiObservations.name: Augustus
wikiObservations.summary: CH112: his nature is finally explained. The team finds Augustus's body-metal matches a substance on the Orange World hologram - his power gives his flesh the properties of Adamantine, the ur-metal of a realm without time, life, or death (Sunshine calls him 'an Orange'). This resolves every anomaly: why time-stop and Livia's time-skip can still affect the 'invincible' warlord, why Frank the Mad's metal-absorption harmed him, why he neither eats nor breathes yet sleeps and ages, and why Julie Costa's life-touch never registered him as alive. Conceptual powers (Frank, Ryan's Geist-killing Black) remain his only known counters.

facts.value: An 'Orange' - his body has the properties of Adamantine (Orange World ur-metal)

wikiObservations.name: Hegemony Soldiers
wikiObservations.summary: CH113: the surviving alien crew of the crashed ship, biomechanical hybrid warriors (uplifted slave-soldiers of the fallen Hegemony). The one Ryan fights ('E.T.') is a 3m armored horror with reptilian eyes, an acid chest-maw, a seed-firing organic cannon, and access to every Flux color: teleport (Violet), phasing/solidifying (part-Orange), a White cancel-shield, and the ability to shift its whole armor to indestructible Adamantine - a stolen, bottled Flux supply that runs out like fuel. Crucially it CANNOT use Black; Ryan cracks its adamantine visor and lets Black Flux corrupt its seven-color balance, collapsing it into a black hole. Darkling reveals these are vengeful GHOSTS of a war lost decades ago (a 'Japanese holdout'), no invasion or rescue coming; the one Ryan killed was a mere grunt, and if the rest escape they will devastate Earth, able to replicate any power but Black.

facts.value: Wield every Flux color from a finite stolen reserve; can turn armor to Adamantine - but never Black
Ghost-holdouts of a decades-dead empire; the killed one was only a grunt

he killed one with Black Flux and must end the rest

wikiObservations.name: Darkling
wikiObservations.summary: CH113: Ryan's Black Elixir/messenger speaks to him through the black hole that consumed the alien (opened easily because this metal prison's spacetime is thin, built to open doors to the higher realms). Watching from the timeless Black World, it has learned the whole truth and delivers the arc's thesis: the Hegemony fell decades ago, no invasion or rescue is coming, and the ship is just vengeful ghosts fighting a lost war. Eva Fabre treated that history as a blueprint rather than a warning and repeated their mistakes making Genomes. Most importantly, Darkling reveals the Violet Ultimate One never intervenes directly - it 'sent Ryan' via visions so a human could choose to end a human-made disaster. Ryan alone is closest to ascension, can now speak Elixir, and can interface with the ship's control-mind to destroy the ship across all timelines (the Alchemist will fight back).

Ryan can talk to Elixirs / interface with the ship's mind because he is nearest to ascension

names them ghosts of a lost war

wikiObservations.name: The Hegemony
wikiObservations.summary: CH113 (Darkling's confirmation): the Hegemony collapsed DECADES ago, overthrown by its own freed slaves; nothing remains of it in its home universe. The crashed Antarctic ship is all that is left - a 'Japanese holdout' whose surviving hybrid soldiers still fight a war they already lost, no invasion and no rescue coming. Its lingering danger is only local: if those last soldiers escape the pocket dimension they can replicate any Earth power except Black and devastate civilization. Its true significance for the story is as a CAUTIONARY tale Eva Fabre ignored - she read its history as a blueprint for uplifting humanity into a 'master race' and so repeated its mistakes, birthing Genomes, Psychos, and monsters like Mechron, Bloodstream, and Augustus.

facts.value: Fell decades ago; only this holdout ship survives, in Earth's reality

wikiObservations.name: Homo Novus
wikiObservations.summary: CH114: the Alchemist's name for her intended successor species - superpowered humans meant to supplant Homo Sapiens the way sapiens replaced Neanderthals. Elixir genetics (decoded from the ship): Elixirs originate in the White World, reproduce asexually like jellyfish, and adapt to any colored dimension's Flux. A Genome+normie child inherits a duplicated, slightly adapted version of the parent's power; a Genome+Genome child gets ONE Elixir that blends both parents' colors (e.g. Narcinia = Green mother + Yellow father = 'create life by cutting herself'). Children of Genomes are ALWAYS stable Genomes, so by the Alchemist's own projection Homo Sapiens declines within ~200 years. Psychos (bicolored mutants) were a deliberate EXPERIMENT into multi-color Flux synergy - a hoped-for reality-overwriting Genome - not a bug; they are sterile (can't propagate) and target other Genomes.

facts.value: Replace Homo Sapiens with superpowered Homo Novus within ~200 years

A deliberate multi-color synergy experiment (seeking a reality-editing power), sterile by design

wikiObservations.name: The Alchemist
wikiObservations.summary: CH114: confronted in the ship as a squad of quantum-duplicate Eva Fabre clones (like Livia's power, they collapse to Blue Flux when 'killed'). They reveal, without a flicker of remorse, that Psychos were an intentional experiment and that a Psycho cure existed from the start (Psychos being sterile 'features,' not bugs; she keeps other degraded Bloodstream-like Psychos in storage). She calls the apocalypse 'an acceptable loss' and 'a dirty job someone had to do' to forge Homo Novus. Ryan diagnoses her fatal flaw: her Elixir granted her deepest wish - an army of adoring copies - turning the ship into an echo chamber that eroded all self-reflection (her clones finish each other's sentences and none dissent), making her more narcissistic than Augustus. Sunshine formally arrests her for genocide; she is genuinely baffled ('We made you into gods!') and battle erupts.

wikiObservations.name: The Founders of Homo Novus
wikiObservations.summary: CH114: resolved. They share Eva's face, complete each other's sentences, and every one of them is remorseless: to them the world's death was an 'acceptable loss' and mankind their lab rats in the pursuit of Homo Novus. They tracked Ryan since he beat Mechron (Case-BiH-006) and covet his reality-affecting time power for their chronotech research.

wikiObservations.name: The Psycho Cure

The mechanism, decoded from the ship: pairing gene therapy with the correct Flux 'message' teaches an Elixir to recognize the right DNA and patch out the instability, potentially curing even Sarin or Frank. But past a threshold the genetic damage is beyond any Elixir's correction (as with degraded Psychos like Bloodstream, of which the Alchemist keeps others in storage). Learning the cure was withheld turns Sarin from wanting answers to wanting revenge.

facts.value: The Alchemist had the cure all along and withheld it deliberately

her rage at the withheld cure

wikiObservations.name: The Alchemist

She can spawn endless human clones and hack Earth tech (she jams Ryan's suit) but cannot pilot the ship past her own Blue nature, and is stunned Ryan wields Black Flux. Unable to pilot it himself (a Violet), Ryan instead infects the overmind brain with Black Flux, rotting it and tearing open black-hole rifts. wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano

wikiObservations.name: Station Orpheon
wikiObservations.summary: CH115 (destroyed): after Ryan Black-Flux-rots the ship's overmind, the Black Ultimate One's rift devours the entire vessel - the Alchemist, her clones, the Hegemony Soldiers, the Elixir factory, labs, and eons of accumulated alien knowledge (cloning, mind-transfer, unlimited energy, immortality research). Of the Alchemist's lair, nothing remains, and it will be erased from Ryan's timeline entirely once he reloads.

wikiObservations.name: Sarin
wikiObservations.summary: CH116 (CURED / true name Bianca): the refurbished Station Orpheon team uses copied Alchemist data + a Chronoradio-based Flux signal to guide Sarin's Elixirs into cleanly separating her powers. The reveal of the Psycho mechanism: her condition was two competing Elixirs (a Red and an Orange) each believing it served the sole host, unaware humans can 'twin' - Hanlon's razor, incompetence not malice. Told there are 'two Homo Sapiens in one flesh vessel,' the Elixirs 'divorce,' each taking custody of a DNA share. Her gas cloud condenses into flesh: Bianca is a thin, small (~1.5m), ~30-year-old woman with messy green-and-orange hair and gray eyes, memories intact (the molecular sample Ryan saved from the Meta-Gang loop restored her). She weeps, embraces Ryan for keeping his promise, and rejoins his circle - the same Bianca who once sacrificed herself to delay Fallout.

wikiObservations.name: The Psycho Cure
wikiObservations.summary: CH116 (PROVEN): the cure works on Sarin/Bianca. Method: send Chronoradio-based Flux signals (the Panda translated the Elixir 'Flux language' from Alchemist notes) to the host's Elixirs, guiding them to rewrite DNA on Livia's clean Homo-Sapiens/Neanderthal ratio, separating the fused powers. Root cause revealed: a Psycho is two rival Elixirs sharing one body, each thinking it has the sole host and ruining the other's 'ascension' out of ignorance, not malice (Hanlon's razor). A saved pre-Psycho molecular sample lets the Elixirs restore the original body and memories. The team lacks the Alchemist's alien tech, so success wasn't guaranteed - but it worked, ending fifteen years of the Psycho scourge in principle.
