wikiObservations.name: Ascension
wikiObservations.summary: CH116 (defined): the cosmology's central promise, threaded since CH100 (Torque/Bacchus) and CH111-115. True Genomes exist on two levels - the biological body and an immaterial consciousness partly living in Flux form (the bonded Elixir). Over time that ethereal consciousness grows in power, wisdom, and strength until it becomes too great for flesh to contain, and it ascends into a higher form of existence - ultimately toward becoming an Ultimate One. This explains hosts like Mr. Wave, Sunshine, Geist, and Sarin. Ryan is uniquely poised for it: he alone already exists in two places/eras at once, a single consciousness split across the timestream, so his neurons are not the full seat of his mind. Darkling's CH115 moral: ascension is every living thing's right but cannot be FORCED (the Alchemist's fatal error).

facts.value: Immaterial Flux consciousness grows beyond the body, then ascends toward becoming an Ultimate One
It is every being's right but cannot be forced - the Alchemist's error

ties.rel: the immaterial half of a Genome that can ascend

wikiObservations.name: Elixirs
wikiObservations.summary: CH116: heard debating aloud for the first time (loudspeakered from Sarin's vat). They sound like hyperactive children with a poor grasp of human biology - a Red one obsessed with energy/power, an Orange one obsessed with repair/freedom - each convinced it alone serves the host, arguing over her 'ascension.' They cannot read their host's thoughts well (unlike Ryan's own Elixir) and only realized she was a 'twin' when the team transmitted an instruction. They 'divorce' on command, each taking a DNA share, curing the Psycho. Confirmed: an Elixir is the immaterial half of a Genome, sees the host's thoughts/wishes and translates them into Flux, and grows toward ascension; Eva/the Ultimate Ones are their ultimate authority ('The Ultimate Ones won't be happy').

wikiObservations.name: Felix

Ryan can't reload on demand, so he recounts an unrepeatable private memory (Felix tracking rats to a Bliss-overdosed Ki-jung, and Narcinia's parents' 'greater good of the family' line) that only the real Felix ever knew - convincing him it's time-travel, not mind-reading. Ryan reveals this is his ~16th New Rome reload, that in a past loop they were close partners ('Quicksave the Pandas') and Felix's sister Livia died to save him, and that Jamie and Ki-jung died protecting Felix believing he hated them. Grief-stricken, Felix resolves to take the second chance and formally joins Ryan's endgame, accepting a 'boss rush' against his own parents and godfather. Then they sight the coast: New Rome is on fire again.

wikiObservations.name: Mr. Wave

I've seen crazier things than time travel'), reveals he already knew and is proud. Ryan confesses Mr. Wave is his hero - saved him from explosions 20+ times, sat at his bedside every death, once toured Italy's coast at 'lightspeed' to find Len - and that with his parents dead and Bloodstream no model, Ryan tried to become more like him. Mr. Wave, a comedian before becoming a 'living spotlight,' explains his relentless jokes: on the road one in four newbies dies, so he carries the show to keep his grieving teammates going. wikiObservations.summary: CH120 (revealed a VIOLET; final confrontation): after Ryan's team routs the Meta-Gang bunker, Ryan reaches the deep chamber and faces Big Fat Adam alone. Adam emerges grinning, carbon skin black, and reveals he is a fellow VIOLET ('never tasted a fellow Violet before') - meaning he too can manipulate time/space, making him uniquely dangerous. Ryan names him the deadliest of his foes: Augustus is stronger and Fallout more determined, but Adam is shrewder, crueler, and more dangerous, which is why he had to be taken down FIRST. The duel begins on a cliffhanger, Ryan warning 'make that last loop count - you won't get another.'

facts.value: A Violet, like Ryan - can manipulate time/space, hence uniquely dangerous
Shrewder and crueler than Augustus/Fallout; taken down first

ties.rel: its leader, cornered as his bunker falls

wikiObservations.name: The Perfect Run
wikiObservations.summary: CH120 (bunker raid executed flawlessly): the memory-loaded team runs the honed assault. Ryan drives Livia and Fortuna in (Ghoul chained to the hood mid-joyride); Felix and the Panda/Timmy air-drop; Shroud saves Fortuna from collapsing debris. They breach the Junkyard past its guards (Reptilian, Gemini, Acid Rain, Mosquito, Mongrel) non-lethally. Inside, Bianca (secret code confirmed) turns on her old teammates; the recreational-area Psychos are subdued (Ink Machine, Rakshasa, Incognito, Catcher, Penanggalan). Ryan Bliss-overdoses Psyshock and cons Frank the Mad into standing guard via a fake 'Agent Frank/Pearl Harbor' script Livia scripted. Even his Plymouth Fury takes no damage - a first, which Ryan reads as a holy sign the Perfect Run is on. He reaches the deep chamber to face Adam the Ogre, the priority kill.

facts.value: Bunker cleared non-lethally with the memory-team; Psyshock and Frank neutralized
The Plymouth Fury survives undamaged for the first time - 'Perfect Run confirmed'

ties.rel: the boss waiting at the end of the raid
scripted the Frank ruse and fights at Ryan's side

wikiObservations.name: Fuckface
wikiObservations.summary: CH120 (real name revealed: CATCHER): the floating disembodied Asian woman's head Ryan crudely nicknamed 'Fuckface' on his first suicide run is actually named Catcher, as Livia informs him. She fights with crimson Red-Flux energy arms/tentacles that deflect bullets and spits acid, but Ryan freezes time, closes in, and smashes her head against the bar counter, knocking her out. Ryan (a self-styled completionist) resolves to learn the real names of the bunker's minor Psychos he never bothered with before, since they died in his Meta-Gang-run civil war and he never knew them.

facts.value: Catcher (Ryan's 'Fuckface' was his own first-run nickname)
Disembodied head projecting crimson Red-Flux energy arms; spits acid

ties.rel: minor member subdued in the bunker raid

wikiObservations.name: Pale Guy
wikiObservations.summary: CH120 (real name revealed: PENANGGALAN): the sickly white, bald 'Pale Guy' Ryan never named is actually Penanggalan, per Livia. A nimble dodger, he is flanked and cornered by Livia (wielding the Fisty Brothers gauntlets) and Bianca's vibration blasts until a Fisty blow to the chest knocks him into a wall, out of the fight. Like Catcher, one of the minor Meta-Gang Psychos Ryan is now bothering to know by their true names.

facts.value: Penanggalan (Ryan's 'Pale Guy' was a first-run placeholder)
Flanked by Livia and Bianca, knocked out by a Fisty Brothers blow

ties.rel: minor member subdued in the bunker raid

wikiObservations.name: Adam the Ogre
wikiObservations.summary: CH121 (KILLED): the duel reveals his two powers - a Violet time-sense (he FEELS Ryan's freezes like Acid Rain and shields his vitals whenever time stops, though he lacks the reflexes/teleport to fully exploit it) and a POCKET DIMENSION in his gullet/torso (wounds bleed no blood, only suck air; he pulls out grenades, a flail, a crossbow he spits bolts from, even a Blue Elixir syringe). His carbon skin resists most bullets; Ryan blinds both eyes with depleted-uranium rounds but is crossbow-bolted in the belly and leg. Cornered, Ryan throws his triggered A-bomb down Adam's throat mid-taunt ('Filibuster!'); the pocket dimension contains most of the blast, but flames erupt from his mouth, nostrils, and the uranium bullet-holes, cooking his organs and melting his skull. He dies. The Panda's prior-loop fight had taught Ryan Adam was vulnerable to internal damage.

facts.value: Violet time-sense (feels/shields against freezes) + a pocket dimension in his gullet
Killed by his own swallowed A-bomb; flames cooked him through the uranium bullet-holes

ties.rel: killed by him in single combat
whose earlier fight exposed Adam's internal weakness

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH121: in a brutal solo duel Ryan kills Adam the Ogre - shooting a hostage boy free, blinding Adam with depleted-uranium rounds, and finally feeding him his own triggered A-bomb so the blast cooks him from inside. Ryan learns Adam is a fellow Violet who could SENSE his time-stops (giving him only 8-10 seconds of usable freeze that Adam reads), a reminder that even after 17 loops his enemies still surprise him. Wounded (crossbow bolts in waist and leg), he's patched up by the Panda in the infirmary with Livia at his side. The raid is a total success: zero casualties, every Rust Town hostage saved, captive Psychos moved to underwater habitats. He resolves to next break Dynamis, then the Augusti - but Livia tells him to celebrate this hard-won win first.

facts.value: Killed Adam the Ogre; Meta-Gang bunker taken with zero casualties, all hostages saved
Adam could sense his freezes; his usable time-stop is only ~8-10 seconds

ties.rel: at his bedside; steers him to celebrate before the next target

wikiObservations.name: The Perfect Run
wikiObservations.summary: CH121 (first endgame target cleared): Adam the Ogre dies and the Meta-Gang bunker falls with ZERO casualties - every captured Rust Town denizen saved, the goal Ryan chased for 10+ loops. Aftercare: captive Psychos moved to underwater habitats; Psyshock handed (via Livia's ruse to Frank) to Cancel/Greta; Alchemo and the Carnival will occupy the bunker, exploit its resources, and set up Mechron's ghost-tech for final destruction. The Panda lost his Elixir feeding it into the fight, but Livia foresees possibilities where it is extracted alive from Adam's pocket dimension (Elixirs are extra-dimensional and durable). Next legs of the plan: recover, then break Dynamis, then confront the Augusti - but tonight they celebrate.

facts.value: Meta-Gang defeated, all Rust Town hostages saved with zero casualties
Occupy/destroy the bunker, then Dynamis, then the Augusti

wikiObservations.name: The Panda
wikiObservations.summary: CH121: reveals he retains full expertise (a doctorate in medicine, physics, philosophy) with perfect memory even after the mind-transfer, surgically extracting Ryan's crossbow bolt and patching him up in the bunker infirmary - though he 'doesn't learn quickly anymore.' Crucially, it was the Panda's fight with Adam the Ogre in the previous loop that revealed Adam's vulnerability to internal damage, directly giving Ryan the winning A-bomb-down-the-throat tactic. The transfer cost him his own Elixir (no second power this loop), but Livia foresees possibilities where it is recovered from Adam's pocket dimension.

facts.value: Retains medicine/physics/philosophy expertise and perfect memory post-transfer
His prior-loop fight exposed Adam's internal weakness, enabling the kill

ties.rel: his earlier fight revealed the winning weakness
field-medic who patched him after the duel

wikiObservations.name: Enrique Manada
wikiObservations.summary: CH122 (turns / unmasked): confronted with Ryan, Len, and Felix's evidence dossier, Blackthorn fact-checks it by phone (firing staff mid-call) and confirms every charge: Knockoffs are made from Bloodstream slime, Len was cloned at Lab Sixty-Six, and his father Hector conspired with Adam/the Meta-Gang to weaken the Augusti. He unmasks (a lean Antonio-Banderas look) and admits he learned the horror too late (Fait Accompli), kept covering it because Dynamis is 'the last barrier' against Augustus. His brother Alphonse built the Knockoffs to dethrone the god-Genomes and wanted Len as a guinea pig (Enrique vetoed it). Moved by Wyvern and by the offered Psycho/Bloodstream cure, he agrees to analyze the epidemic risk and share the Gravity Gun data - a genuine reformer, Dynamis's own 'Livia.'

facts.value: Confirms the Knockoff/collusion scandal, agrees to help dismantle it and share the Gravity Gun data
Lean Antonio-Banderas look; a sincere reformer who covered up out of fear of Augustus

ties.rel: won over as an ally against Dynamis's rot and Augustus
brother who built the Knockoffs and will retaliate

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: CH122: Len confronts Enrique Manada face-to-face, demanding to know why Dynamis did this to her father. She reveals the doomsday stakes: her own blood carries an agent that strips the safeguards off the Knockoffs - contact would revert every Knockoff-drinker into a Bloodstream clone, killing millions, and the core may soon do it unaided. She refuses Enrique's handshake but accepts his apology; she wants no revenge, only to try the cure on her father Bloodstream and, failing that, to end his suffering and give him peace. Still awkward with strangers (waits in the car during the Jamie visit), she is steadier and braver here, her anger at Dynamis giving her confidence.

facts.value: Her blood is the trigger that turns every Knockoff-drinker into a Bloodstream clone
No revenge - cure her father if possible, else give him a peaceful end

ties.rel: confronts him; accepts his apology, not his hand
her father, whose fate she will decide

wikiObservations.name: Wyvern
wikiObservations.summary: CH122: present at the Dynamis confrontation as Enrique's guard. She reads the evidence dossier in denial, dismissing it as Lab-Sixty-Six conspiracy theory, until Enrique's phone-checks force the truth on her. Devastated - she was Enrique's ex-lover ('Laura'/'Enrique') - she snaps the mahogany desk in half, then resigns on the spot rather than stand by the Knockoff horror, and pleads with Enrique to do the same ('Someone has to try'). Ryan privately urges her to reconcile with Jasmine (Vulcan): all Jasmine wants is an apology and recognition for living in Wyvern's shadow, treated as an equal. Wyvern, shaken, seems willing to try - and to give Enrique another chance.

facts.value: Quits Il Migliore over the Knockoff scandal; urges Enrique to reform too
Enrique's ex-lover ('Laura'); pain and a sliver of hope remain between them

ties.rel: estranged ex-lover she pleads with to do the right thing
Ryan nudges her to reconcile with Jasmine, who wants recognition

wikiObservations.name: Jamie
wikiObservations.summary: CH122: Felix visits his estranged Augusti friends (Jamie, Ki-jung, Lanka) to seek not their return but their neutrality if the Augusti fall. Jamie counters Felix's judgment: he stayed to keep Ki-jung and Lanka alive after Ki-jung stole Bliss and Pluto marked her for death - Felix only escaped because his parents and ex have Augustus's ear. Ki-jung firmly says she WOULD leave (she still fights the Bliss addiction and wants others freed of it), and Jamie, who means to marry her, chooses her: 'I would choose her, wherever that leads.' Lanka stays cynical but promises silence. A conditional alliance secured: they'll step aside when Augustus falls.

facts.value: Stayed with the Augusti to protect Ki-jung (Bliss theft) and Lanka, not from belief
Chooses Ki-jung over the family; will step aside if the Augusti are toppled

ties.rel: girlfriend he means to marry; chooses her over the Augusti
estranged friend who wins his conditional neutrality

wikiObservations.name: The Opis Armor
wikiObservations.summary: CH123: Ryan's secret gift to Livia - a power armor built on the Saturn model but leaner and tailored for her: blood-red plates, a night-black visor, a white spider symbol on the chest, and eight telescopic reinforced-steel tentacles replacing Saturn's ear-antennae. The spider theme suits her precognition: the extra-arm/drone system is unmasterable except by someone who can see the future, and she is 'scheming and sensible like a spider.' Ryan built it in a thin place so her precognition wouldn't spoil the surprise, intending it not for the Bliss Raid (where it would out her powers) but for the fight against Augustus.

facts.value: The Saturn Armor - leaner, female-fit, red/black with a white spider crest
Eight telescopic steel tentacles + a drone system only a precog can pilot

ties.rel: tailor-made for her; Ryan built it in a thin place to hide it from her precognition
the parent model it is derived from

wikiObservations.name: Ghoul
wikiObservations.summary: CH123 (exiled to orbit): the skeletal, sociopathic Meta-Gang Psycho Livia predicted would keep murdering even if cured - the one captive too irredeemable to rehabilitate. Rather than destroy him with Black Flux, Ryan and Livia humanely exile him: they load him (powers heat-suppressed) into 'SpaceZ,' an anti-gravity Red-Flux rocket Vulcan had originally built a year ago as a prison for Wyvern, and launch him into Earth orbit. Being immortal, he'll drift gazing at Earth for decades - a jail, not an execution, kept in orbit in case he's ever needed back.

facts.value: Launched into Earth orbit aboard the 'SpaceZ' anti-grav rocket - immortal, so it is imprisonment not death
Too irredeemable to cure, but Ryan/Livia chose orbit over Black-power destruction

ties.rel: arranged his humane exile via a repurposed Wyvern-prison rocket
built the SpaceZ rocket (originally a prison meant for Wyvern)

wikiObservations.name: Livia Augusti
wikiObservations.summary: CH123: hosts the Dostoevski gathering, plays the Rains of Castamere to needle the suspicious Mathias, and shares her endgame with Ryan. Geist's disappearance has roused Augustus from inaction - he suspects the Meta-Gang, reinforced Ischia, and authorized Vulcan's Rust Town retaking; she'll shield Wyvern if a kill order issues. Her grand plan: once Augustus, Hector, and Alphonse fall and both empires are weakened, she'll merge a reformed Augusti with Enrique's Dynamis into the New European Republic (NER), with Ryan at her side ('the Albert to my Victoria'). She takes the news of Ryan's Black power calmly - it's why they met - and only asks that he spare (imprison, not kill) her father. She gifts him the SpaceZ exile-rocket for Ghoul.

facts.value: Merge a reformed Augusti with Dynamis into the New European Republic after the tyrants fall
Plans to gather the corrupt Olympians (Mercury, Pluto, Mars, Vulcan, Venus, Killer Seven) so the purge can cut the rot at once

ties.rel: receives his Black-power secret with trust; asks only that he spare her father
intended NER merger partner once both empires are reformed

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH123: reviews the Gravity Gun plans with Timmy - a projectile that makes a gravity anomaly to fling Augustus out of the atmosphere ('Kars Augustus') - and insists on miniaturizing it into his own armor and facing Mob Zeus ALONE, since only he can harm the tyrant and survive death via reload. He finally tells Livia the full Black-power secret: he gained it by wishing to die, which is why the Violet Ultimate One now blocks his saves; she reframes it as past-tense, since now he wants to live. He surveys the allies he has gathered/cured (Bianca, Helen, Jerome, Vlad, the Panda, Len) and feels he has something to fight for again. He vows to imprison Augustus, not slay him. Next: Lab Sixty-Six, then the Bliss Factory, then Augustus - the gauntlet.

facts.value: Will fight Augustus alone with a miniaturized Gravity Gun in his armor; can reload if killed
Confesses to Livia he got the power by wishing to die - the reason his saves are now blocked

ties.rel: confides his Black power; vows to imprison, not kill, her father
resolves to face him alone as the final and deadliest foe

wikiObservations.name: Acid Rain
wikiObservations.summary: CH123 (cured, real name Helen): the once-deranged Psycho now restored to a shy, gentle woman named Helen. The cure separated her two rival Elixir powers, leaving her able to swap the positions of items of near-equivalent mass (including herself) - a teleport-by-exchange. Deeply grateful to Ryan for freeing her, she bows and volunteers to take up arms again if it helps, though she's far happier at peace.

facts.value: Helen - restored to a shy, gentle woman by the Psycho cure
Swaps positions of near-equal-mass items (including herself); teleport-by-exchange

ties.rel: grateful to him for the cure; volunteers to help his cause

wikiObservations.name: Mongrel
wikiObservations.summary: CH123 (cured, real name Jerome): with the Knockoff Elixirs out of his system the feral Psycho is healthy and sane again, insisting on the name Jerome and refusing any supervillain nickname. He owes Ryan a life debt and will help improve the cure and even fight if needed, but wants nothing more to do with Elixirs or violence afterward - years as a savage animal left him craving an ordinary nine-to-five life.

facts.value: Jerome - sane again once the Knockoff Elixirs cleared his system
Pays his life-debt to Ryan, then wants out of Elixirs and fighting forever

ties.rel: owes him a life debt; will help then retire to normal life

wikiObservations.name: Frank the Mad
wikiObservations.summary: CH123 (cured, real self Vladimir 'Vlad'): the loyal, funny American-patriot persona was Knockoff brainwashing; his true self is Vladimir, a blunt, humorless Russian Trotskyist giant (Marshal-Zhukov looks) who preaches permanent revolution. Ryan finds him a total killjoy, but Len instantly bonds with him as a fellow communist - they talk political theory for hours. He owes Ryan and is eager to 'burn down the establishment.'

facts.value: Vladimir ('Vlad') - a humorless Russian Trotskyist; 'Agent Frank' was Knockoff brainwashing
Instantly becomes Len's ideological kindred spirit

ties.rel: fellow communist she bonds with over political theory

wikiObservations.name: Bloodstream
wikiObservations.summary: CH124 (death / euthanized): held in a reinforced tank at Lab Sixty-Six, the red alien shoggoth Freddie Sabino became no longer recognizes his daughter Len. She tries the group's Psycho/Bloodstream cure one last time; it fails because he has mutated too far, half-transformed into a denizen of the higher colored dimensions. Accepting he is gone, Len activates Dr. Tyrano's failsafe - without her blood agent shielding him, the sprinkler chemicals grind his cells to formless white goo, a painless euthanasia. Ryan, who long hated him, feels only pity: a father lost to madness and the Alchemist's cruelty, who took two Elixirs to protect his daughter in a hostile world. He now lives only in Len's memory.

facts.value: Euthanized by Len via Tyrano's failsafe after the cure fails - mutated too far to restore
Ryan pities him as a good man lost to madness, not a chosen monster like Adam

ties.rel: his daughter, who chooses to end his suffering herself
whose containment failsafe destroys the mutated creature

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: CH124: insists on facing her father alone at Lab Sixty-Six (Stitch first removed the Bloodstream agent from her blood so she won't transform). She tries the cure on Bloodstream; when it fails she moves from denial through bargaining to acceptance, says 'Goodbye, Father,' and euthanizes him with Tyrano's failsafe - grief, not anger. She asks Ryan to leave her alone with the body a while. Her hardest, most adult moment: choosing to end the suffering of the father she loved rather than cling to a lost hope.

facts.value: Euthanizes her father herself after the cure fails; grieves rather than rages
Stitch removed the Bloodstream agent from her blood so she wouldn't transform near him

ties.rel: her father, whose suffering she chooses to end
stands with her, letting her decide her father's fate

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH124: coordinates the three-pronged Lab Sixty-Six strike from the air in his Saturn armor, comforting Len through her father's euthanasia, then waltzes with Livia over New Rome to seed the sky with the green Cure Flu. His armor is now maxed out with data looted from the Alchemist's lab: five Flux batteries (every color but his own Violet, fueled by his allies) driving Fisty-brothers gauntlets with a Red-Flux shockwave (Bianca's power), a Blue-Flux computer that kills control lag, Orange emergency shielding, Green self-healing, Yellow conceptual defense, White harmony - plus a miniaturized Gravity Gun hidden in his chest as a secret trump against Augustus. He still feels only pity, not joy, at Bloodstream's death. Then Fallout arrives 'riding the atom' from Sicily, and Ryan and Livia stand together to fight him.

facts.value: Five all-color Flux batteries + Fisty/Red-shockwave gauntlets, Blue-lag computer, Green heal, Yellow conceptual defense, White harmony
A miniaturized Gravity Gun built into his chest, kept secret for Augustus

ties.rel: waltzes with her to spread the Cure Flu; teams to face Fallout
confronts him again, this time not alone but with Livia

wikiObservations.name: The Cure Flu
wikiObservations.summary: CH124: a benign, self-spreading airborne virus Ryan's group engineers to erase Dynamis's Knockoff Elixirs from the population. Ryan and Livia release it as green pollen-like dust from their armor backpacks while dancing over New Rome; allies also seed it from high points and the city water system. It scrubs the Bloodstream-derived Knockoff agent from anyone's blood, making would-be Genomes more human again and defusing the Elixir-apocalypse threat - and it spreads with every breath, so within weeks all of Europe would 'catch the Cure Flu.' A cure disguised as a plague, immunizing the continent against Bloodstream's ghost.

facts.value: A benign contagious virus that removes Knockoff Elixirs from the blood, spread breath-to-breath
Released as green dust from Ryan/Livia's armor over New Rome, plus water system and high points

ties.rel: the threat it neutralizes across Europe's population
engineered from the same cure research (Mongrel's power + Psycho work)

wikiObservations.name: Hector Manada
wikiObservations.summary: CH124 (arrested): while tending his roses, Dynamis's chairman is surrounded by Wyvern, Felix, and Il Migliore (Devilry, Reload, Wardrobe) and arrested on his own son Enrique's signed mandate for human experimentation, bioterrorism, funding the Meta-Gang, and more. Shattered that Enrique betrayed him, and abandoned by bodyguards unwilling to die for him, he surrenders 'to call my lawyers' - warning vindictively that his elder son Alphonse will now take over and drown the city in blood: 'After me, the flood.'

facts.value: Taken by Wyvern/Felix/Il Migliore on Enrique's own mandate; surrenders without a fight
'After me, the flood' - Alphonse will retaliate for the lab's closure

ties.rel: the son whose signature authorizes his arrest
the elder son he predicts will bring blood to the streets

wikiObservations.name: Fallout
wikiObservations.summary: CH124 (arrives for battle): Alphonse 'Fallout' Manada is warned the instant Enrique breaches Lab Sixty-Six (moles + a private alarm - the same speed that let him counter Ryan's Meta-Run raid). Rather than fly by plane from Sicily, he 'rides the atom,' appearing as a bright red star above the twilight sun - a titan of black metal propelled on a wave of Red Flux. He killed Ryan's whole team the last time they clashed. Now he descends on Ryan and Livia (in her new Opis armor), who stand together to face him: 'We're invincible.'

facts.value: 'Rides the atom' from Sicily on a Red-Flux wave - a black-metal titan, a bright red star in the sky
Killed Ryan's entire team in a prior loop; now faced by Ryan + Livia together

ties.rel: old nemesis who once wiped out his team; faces him again
confronts them both above New Rome

wikiObservations.name: Fallout
wikiObservations.summary: CH125 (death): battles Ryan and Livia over the Gulf of Naples; their combo (her timeskip makes him intangible/invincible) cracks his suit and drops him into the sea, where he sheds his cyborg armor into a radioactive charred skeleton with fire for flesh and runs along the ocean floor to the ship graveyard. He detonates like a nuke - the blast nearly kills Livia and buckles Ryan's armor. Ryan Black-Fluxes off BOTH his arms (which crumble to harmless red particles), but Fallout refuses Enrique's offered reconciliation ('All for the dream') and moves to self-destruct again. Shroud, invisible, blasts him into space with the full Dynamis Gravity Gun - the weapon Alphonse himself funded to kill Augustus becomes his own executioner. He vanishes beyond the clouds in a trail of fading red explosions.

facts.value: Blasted into space by Shroud with the Gravity Gun he funded, after Ryan severed both his arms
Sheds his suit into a charred radioactive skeleton; a walking meltdown that destroyed a city on his first Elixir

ties.rel: Shroud, who fires the fatal Gravity-Gun shot
brother whose reconciliation he refuses, choosing the dream over family

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH125: fights Fallout with Livia's combo; his upgraded gauntlets (Red shockwaves, Green self-heal, Orange emergency shielding) let him trade blows, but Fallout's nuke-blast burns through, hurts Livia, and forces Ryan to escalate. Enraged for Livia and by Fallout's threat to dissect Len, he wields Black Flux to disintegrate both the corpo's arms ('Give me an inch, I'll take the arm... I destroyed time'), swearing to peel him until he finds his core rather than kill (his vow to Livia). He arms his hidden Gravity Gun but Shroud fires first. He then rushes to the wounded Livia's side - one poison purged from New Rome, but Augustus still waits on Ischia.

facts.value: Uses Black Flux to disintegrate both of Fallout's arms without killing him (per his vow)
Abandons the finishing blow to give first aid to the gravely wounded Livia

ties.rel: cripples him with Black Flux but leaves the kill to Shroud
her near-death drives his fury; he chooses her over finishing Fallout

wikiObservations.name: Livia Augusti
wikiObservations.summary: CH125 (gravely wounded): fights beautifully in her Opis armor - her eight telescopic tentacles rip off Fallout's missile launchers - and her precognition steers Ryan's shockwaves and their combo. When Fallout goes nuclear she could have escaped the blast, but she stayed because she couldn't see Ryan and had to be sure he survived: she takes the explosion, buried in molten glass at the crater's edge. Ryan (and Enrique's roots) dig her out - concussed and dazed but alive, saved by her Genome metabolism and top-notch armor. She'll need real rest to recover. A pointed proof that she loves Ryan more than her own safety.

facts.value: Concussed and buried in molten glass by Fallout's nuke-blast; survives via Genome metabolism + armor
Could have fled but stayed in the blast radius to ensure Ryan survived

ties.rel: risks death to protect him; he gives her first aid over finishing Fallout
cripples his launchers before his self-destruct nearly kills her

wikiObservations.name: Enrique Manada
wikiObservations.summary: CH125 (sets his foot down): arrives with Wyvern after Lab Sixty-Six is blown, excavates Livia with his plant roots, and confronts his brother Alphonse. He confesses his own guilt (never blowing the whistle) but refuses to let the Knockoff madness continue - offering Fallout reconciliation and even pressing a finger to his own forehead, daring his brother to kill him rather than budge ('you will have to step over my corpse'). He genuinely loves Al ('us against the world') and grieves when Shroud is forced to Gravity-Gun him into space - 'It had to be done.' The reformer finally acts, at the cost of his own brother.

facts.value: Dares Alphonse to kill him rather than allow the Knockoffs to resume; loses his brother anyway
Mourns Fallout even as he accepts the Gravity-Gun kill was necessary

ties.rel: brother he tries and fails to redeem, then loses to the Gravity Gun
stands with him; earns her renewed respect

wikiObservations.name: Mr. See-Through
wikiObservations.summary: CH125: Shroud is the one who ends the Fallout fight. Present at the Dynamis raid, he waits invisible with the full Dynamis Gravity Gun rifle (glass-shrouded) and, when the cornered Alphonse begins another self-destruct, fires the fatal shot - a black gravity sphere clamps to Fallout's spine and rockets him into space, forcing Wyvern to hold Enrique back from being pulled along. He calmly drops his invisibility afterward and checks on the wounded Livia, having already called Stitch for reinforcement. The decisive, quiet executioner of the raid.

facts.value: Fires the full Gravity Gun that launches Fallout into space, ending the battle
Waited invisible as the raid's failsafe; also summoned Stitch for Livia

ties.rel: the target he launches into space with the Gravity Gun
wields the full Dynamis rifle to lethal effect

wikiObservations.name: The Gravity Gun
wikiObservations.summary: CH125 (proven lethal): the Dynamis anti-gravity weapon is field-tested for the first time. Shroud fires the full rifle at Fallout; the black gravity sphere clamps to his spine, drags nearby glass shards in, and rockets him up out of the atmosphere to vanish beyond the clouds - so strong it nearly pulls in bystanders (Wyvern must grip Enrique). Confirmed to work exactly as designed: it flings a target into space with no escape. Bitter irony that Alphonse funded it to kill Augustus and became its first victim - and it validates Ryan's own miniaturized chest version as a real trump for the Augustus fight.

facts.value: First live use: launches Fallout out of the atmosphere; works exactly as designed
Alphonse funded it to kill Augustus; it becomes his own executioner

ties.rel: its funder and first fatal target
validates the miniaturized version hidden in his armor for Augustus

wikiObservations.name: Magenta
wikiObservations.summary: CH126 (named): Ryan's sentient Violet Elixir - the emissary he has been bonded to since age sixteen (~800+ years). Via his armor's new Elixir-comms system he finally names it 'Magenta' (over Coos / Color out of Time), and it warms to him like a proud teacher watching a graduating student. It explains that Elixirs are only 'priests' - they ask the Ultimate One for miracles, they don't grant them - so the Ultimate One, not Magenta, blocks Ryan's saves: his Black connection has grown dangerous ('a sword without a hilt' that feeds on deleted timelines and could destroy him), and the Ultimate One may want him to Ascend rather than die. It confirms Augustus is indestructible metal vulnerable only to conceptual powers, so Ryan's Black can beat him - hard, not easy. Deadpan-jealous, it forbids 'Elixir bigamy,' and sends him off with 'Onward.'

facts.value: Ryan's Violet Elixir, bonded since he was 16; a Darkling-parallel companion
Elixirs are 'priests' - the Ultimate One (not Magenta) blocks Ryan's saves; his Black growth is the danger

ties.rel: his ~800-year Elixir companion, now named and speaking with him
parallel sentient Elixir (Black); Magenta is jealous of it

wikiObservations.name: Len
wikiObservations.summary: CH126 (closure): fully at peace after euthanizing her father - grief without guilt, having let go of the childhood belief that his fall was her fault. She sees the world can change (if even Dynamis can), and resolves to join The Architect not just for Rust Town's children but to build cities and help children worldwide, giving them a better childhood than her own. She and Ryan reaffirm their bond ('more powerful than friendship'), and she makes him promise to come back from the Augustus fight. Ryan reflects that Len (unlike Mechron, the Alchemist, Fallout) has the kind heart that makes power matter - 'You will do great.'

facts.value: Grief without guilt; accepts she couldn't have changed her father's fate
Will join The Architect to build cities and help children across the globe

ties.rel: will join her to rebuild devastated countries and aid children worldwide
reaffirms their family bond; makes him promise to return

wikiObservations.name: The Plushie
wikiObservations.summary: CH126 (rejoins as ally): the murderous Killer Rabbit that once slaughtered its way across loops appears in the bunker, briefly solemn and almost sad, before reverting to its cheerful malice ('Let's go to Disneyland!'). It wants payback against Augustus for its previous defeat and, having saved Ryan from Adam, is owed a favor - so Ryan lets it ride in his armor's backpack into the final battle, warning it against multiplication if it wants to keep disemboweling privileges. The nightmare has quietly become Ryan's friend, 'one rampage at a time.'

facts.value: Rides in Ryan's backpack to the Augustus fight, seeking payback for its prior defeat
Now genuinely Ryan's friend; owed a favor for saving him from Adam

ties.rel: joins him for the final battle as a repaid ally
wants revenge for its earlier defeat by him

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH126: after tender farewells with Livia (who begs him to flee if he truly can't survive, since he can't save) and Len, he has his Saturn armor repaired in the bunker and installs an Elixir-comms system to finally talk with and name his Violet Elixir, Magenta. It confirms the Ultimate One blocks his saves because his Black has grown dangerous, hints he may Ascend, and confirms his Black can beat Augustus's conceptual-only-vulnerable metal. He takes the Plushie as an ally, then triggers the bunker self-destruct ('Execute order Sixty-Six') as the Augusti invade Rust Town - collapsing the Junkyard and detonating the Bahamut orbital satellite, erasing Mechron's legacy. He flies to Ischia for his last battle, having promised Livia and Len he'll return.

facts.value: 'Execute order Sixty-Six' collapses the Junkyard bunker and self-destructs the Bahamut satellite
Magenta confirms the Ultimate One won't restore his save; he may Ascend instead

ties.rel: names and consults his Violet Elixir before the final fight
flies to Ischia to face him alone, with no reload safety net

wikiObservations.name: Ascension
wikiObservations.summary: CH126 (deepened by Magenta): the process by which a lesser lifeform becomes a cosmic being of the higher realms - not an end but an open door, unique to each ascendant. Magenta reveals it is conditioned not only by power but by WISDOM: the small-eyed monsters on the Alchemist's ship were denied it, while Ryan (grown wise over centuries) and Leo Hargraves are unusually close. Hargraves is deliberately delaying his own ascension to stay on Earth but will eventually 'become a bright star in the sky' if he chooses. The Ultimate One may intend Ryan to Ascend rather than die - the meaning behind blocking his save and urging him to see 'what lies beyond victory.'

facts.value: Requires wisdom as much as power - why the Alchemist's small-eyed monsters were denied it
Ryan and Leo Hargraves are both close; Hargraves delays his to stay on Earth

ties.rel: the Ultimate One may want him to Ascend instead of dying
the Elixir who explains the wisdom-gated process to Ryan

wikiObservations.name: The Bahamut
wikiObservations.summary: CH126 (destroyed): the Mechron orbital laser satellite - the 'sword of Damocles' hanging over New Rome - is finally erased. When Ryan triggers the bunker self-destruct ('Execute order Sixty-Six'), the Bahamut and its orbital command center self-destruct in tandem, briefly glowing like a dying red star in the sky. With the Junkyard bunker collapsed and the satellite gone, Mechron's dangerous legacy 'would never haunt the world again' - one final loose end closed before the Augustus fight.

facts.value: Self-destructed alongside the bunker via 'order Sixty-Six'; a dying red star in the sky
Too dangerous to keep ('no right hands'); erased with the rest of Mechron's legacy

ties.rel: orders its destruction to close Mechron's last loose end

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH127 (Ischia assault): as King Saturn he leads the counter-invasion of Augustus's Bliss fortress, having pre-arranged rock-paper-scissors power match-ups Livia mapped - Vladimir + Acid Rain neutralize Mars, Shroud + Fortuna tranq Pluto and Cancel, Vulcan's killswitch traps the Augusti in their own armors. He goes inside alone to face the telepath Bacchus (acting as bait so the brainless Sarin can creep up unseen) and the necromancer Mercury, enduring devastating hallucination-assaults (drowning, crucifixion, insanity) that tax but can't physically break his centuries-hardened mind. He unravels Bacchus with the Ascension-wisdom truth, knocks out Mercury, rescues the tortured Narcinia, and demolishes the factory. Then he rises alone into the storm to meet Augustus, who descends as an ivory lightning-god - the final duel begins.

facts.value: Introduces himself to Augustus as 'King Saturn'; Augustus frames the fight as his 'Titanomachy'
Pre-mapped power match-ups (Livia's intel) neutralize Mars, Pluto, Cancel, the Killer Seven, and the Augusti armors

ties.rel: faces him alone in the sky above Ischia to open the final duel
acts as bait for Bacchus so she can ambush the telepath unseen

wikiObservations.name: Augustus
wikiObservations.summary: CH127 (descends for the duel): the Augusti god-emperor finally takes the field, descending from a cumulonimbus as an ivory statue shrouded in crimson electric aura, riding ionized winds, red lightning coursing the skies. He looks down on Ryan with contempt, calls him 'the architect of all of this,' and frames the fight as his own Titanomachy - vowing to nail Ryan to a cross and make him watch his friends die. Indestructible metal vulnerable only to conceptual powers (per Magenta, Ryan's Black can beat him). The final battle opens on his word: 'Let's go.'

facts.value: Ivory lightning-god: crimson electric aura, ionized winds for flight, gaze that burns to look at
Calls the duel his 'Titanomachy'; contemptuous, unafraid, but fists clenched in anger

ties.rel: descends to duel him one-on-one above the ruined fortress

wikiObservations.name: Bacchus
wikiObservations.summary: CH127 (defeated, spared): Andreas Torque, the fallen priest and Augusti telepath, defends the Bliss fortress with devastating hallucination-assaults - drowning Ryan in blood, crucifying him, degrading his sense of reality toward 'insanity' (peeling a mind away like an onion until identity is gone). It is revealed HE broke Giulia Costa/Narcinia's mind this way, torturing her until she forgot herself. Ryan endures as bait; the brainless Sarin, invisible to his telepathy, creeps up and fills his lungs with mist, choking him unconscious mid-rant ('I need to escape! I can't stand this reality!'). Ryan spares him - unlike Augustus, Bacchus didn't choose to become a monster (Eva Fabre wrecked his mind at awakening) and Alchemo may cure him as he cured Helen.

facts.value: Blue-Flux telepathy: broadcasts hallucinations, degrades sanity/identity; can't inflict real physical harm but blinds and delays; briefly dispelled by time-stop
Tortured Giulia Costa's mind until she forgot who she was, remaking her as the 'holy maiden' Narcinia
Sarin's brainless mist (invisible to telepathy) choked him out; sedated and spared for a possible Alchemo cure

ties.rel: ambushed and choked unconscious by her mist while distracted by Ryan
the priest who tortured her mind and caged her

wikiObservations.name: Mercury
wikiObservations.summary: CH127 (defeated, spared): the ancient hunchbacked Olympian necromancer - cashmere suit, bowler hat, wooden cane, tiny fearful eyes - who pilots the Augusti dead from afar (raising drowned corpses, skeletons, and dead test subjects with a yellow glow in their eyes). At Ischia he raised a legion of the dead led by Mars, and cloaked undead thralls in Bacchus's illusions to strike Ryan by surprise. Once Ryan shakes free of the hallucinations, he time-stops, charges, and punches the old man out ('Boo'), breaking his jaw - all his undead collapse at once as the yellow light dies. Sedated and spared alongside Bacchus.

facts.value: Necromancy: infuses corpses with energy and pilots the undead from afar; a yellow glow marks his thralls
Ryan's time-stopped charge and a single jaw-breaking punch; his whole undead legion dropped with him

ties.rel: raised and fielded the undead legion the war-god led at Ischia
knocked out cold by him after the hallucinations broke

wikiObservations.name: Narcinia
wikiObservations.summary: CH127 (rescued): found caged among Bacchus's test subjects in the Bliss production center - fetal, terrified, a red slap-mark on her cheek. It is confirmed that when Geist vanished, Father Torque (Bacchus) confiscated her phone, forbade her to leave or see her father, and tortured her mind - the origin of her fractured 'holy maiden' identity (Giulia Costa remade). Ryan tears open the bars and coaxes her out, recalling how Len once found him in the wreckage. Reunited over the intercom with her sister Fortuna and with Felix ('For you, Narci, I came for you'), she is evacuated by Mr. Wave and folded into a tearful group hug.

facts.value: Caged and mind-tortured by Bacchus after Geist's disappearance; phone confiscated, barred from leaving or seeing her father
Freed by Ryan, reunited with Fortuna and Felix, evacuated by Mr. Wave

ties.rel: her sister, who talks her out of the cage over the intercom
returned to the fight specifically for her

wikiObservations.name: Sarin
wikiObservations.summary: CH127 (the Bacchus-killer play): Bianca, the sentient nerve-gas creature, is the linchpin of Ryan's plan against the telepath Bacchus - because she has no brain, his telepathy can't perceive her. While Ryan draws the priest's full attention with his mind, she creeps through the fortress, seeps into Bacchus's lungs as mist, and chokes him unconscious from within (offering to burst out 'Alien-style,' but Ryan wants him alive for a possible cure). She reforms beside her victim, worried at how harrowed Ryan looks, and later helps Vladimir level the fortress with shockwaves.

facts.value: Brainless, so Bacchus's telepathy can't sense her - the perfect assassin for a mind-reader
Seeped into Bacchus's lungs as mist and choked him out from inside, non-lethally on Ryan's orders

ties.rel: ambushed and subdued the telepath he couldn't sense
his brainless secret weapon; worries over his hallucination-wracked state

wikiObservations.name: Ryan Romano
wikiObservations.summary: CH128 (the Augustus duel): King Saturn duels the lightning-god above New Rome. His Black-Flux punches - fueled by every crime he witnessed - CRACK Augustus's 'invulnerable' ivory body, reversing the fight and drawing real fear. He out-boxes the god with centuries of martial experience, but Augustus refuses melee, harasses him from range with homing lightning that Monaco can't cage (the cursed dimension spits Augustus back out of spite), overloads the Saturn Armor's storage, and finally fries it - Ryan crashes crippled on a French beach, glass in his eye, facing death with no save left. The Plushie sacrifices itself, revealing it was always a living gate between universes and Ryan the key: Ryan grabs the tear it opens, forces it wide, drags Augustus in by the ankle, and both fall into the Purple World.

facts.value: His Black-Flux fists crack Augustus's indestructible ivory flesh - the conceptual power that can finally wound the god
Armor fried and grounded; uses the Plushie's death-gate to drag Augustus into the Purple World
Fights not for the world but to be happy and make others happy; 'my fists carry the weight of centuries and the hopes of thousands'

ties.rel: cracks his invulnerability, is beaten at range, then pulls him into the Purple World
its self-sacrifice as a living gate gives him the exit he needs

wikiObservations.name: Augustus
wikiObservations.summary: CH128 (invulnerability shattered): the lightning-god fights Ryan above New Rome, revealing his Red-Elixir lightning has NO upper limit - he detonates a nuclear-scale crimson supernova in the upper atmosphere (the power that sank Malta; enough to end civilization). But Ryan's Black-Flux punches crack his 'invulnerable' ivory body, glowing red rifts spreading like a damaged statue, and he tastes fear and pain for the first time in twenty years. His over-aggressive, defense-less style (never having needed to dodge) fails against Ryan's centuries of martial skill in melee, so he wins at range instead - homing lightning, overloading the Saturn Armor, immune to Monaco's grasp. Moments from vaporizing the grounded Ryan, he is grabbed by the ankle (his adamantine flesh now soft as butter) and dragged into the Purple World. Creed: 'There can only be one master of the world... they exist to serve us.'

facts.value: Lightning generation has no ceiling; detonates a nuclear-scale crimson supernova, could destroy civilization alone
Ryan's Black-Flux fists split his indestructible ivory body; craters and red rifts spread like a moon-scarred statue
Never learned to defend (20 years untouchable); loses melee to Ryan's experience, so refuses it and fights at range

ties.rel: cracked by his Black, then dragged into the Purple World by the ankle
enraged at Ryan invoking his daughter; the one wound the punches couldn't match

wikiObservations.name: The Plushie
wikiObservations.summary: CH128 (heroic sacrifice - true nature revealed): as Augustus prepares to vaporize the grounded, dying Ryan, the murderous Killer Rabbit crawls from the wrecked backpack with the same sorrowful blue eyes it wore in the bunker. Its pre-recorded 'I will always be your friend' morphs into an alien voice as it leaps between Ryan and the god's city-killing thunderbolt, its mechanical body disintegrating. The lightning focused into it opens a thumb-sized violet tear - a portal. The revelation: the Plushie always existed between two universes; it IS a living gate, and Ryan is the key. Its loops of subtle nudging and 'coincidences' were all to leave that door open at the right moment. Its death gives Ryan his one exit - the tear he forces wide to drag Augustus into the Purple World.

facts.value: A living gate between two universes; its 'random' loop-nudges all engineered to open the portal at this exact moment, with Ryan as the key
Disintegrated taking Augustus's city-killing bolt for Ryan; its death opens the portal to the Purple World

ties.rel: dies shielding him; its death-gate is the key to trapping Augustus
the portal it opens leads there

wikiObservations.name: The Purple World
wikiObservations.summary: CH128 (Ryan and Augustus enter): the Violet realm of the Colored Worlds, reached through the portal the dying Plushie's sacrifice tears open on a French beach. When Ryan forces the thumb-sized rift wide with Violet and Black particles, it consumes his own Black-fed lightning and grows a hungry appetite - sand, seawater, and air pour in, and even the flying Augustus is dragged down as the rift eats the air beneath his feet. Ryan grabs his ankle (the adamantine flesh soft as butter at the threshold) and pulls his nemesis through; the gate closes behind them, swallowing both Genomes into the Purple World for the final reckoning.

facts.value: The Plushie's death-portal on the French coast, forced open by Ryan's Violet+Black particles
Ryan drags Augustus into it by the ankle as the rift devours the surrounding matter

ties.rel: enters it dragging his nemesis for the final confrontation
pulled into the realm against his will as the gate closes

plotObservations.title: The endless delivery loop
plotObservations.beat: Ryan keeps dying delivering a briefcase to Renesco; on the fourth loop he rams the assassin Ghoul with his Plymouth, beats him with a bat, bribes Private Security, and completes the delivery. His only motive: he is bored.

plotObservations.title: Competing recruitment: the branching paths
plotObservations.beat: Wyvern of Il Migliore recruits Ryan and offers to help find Len; then Vulcan of the Augusti counter-recruits him to the Bakuto casino. Ryan realizes multiple faction routes have opened, but his true quest is finding Len.

plotObservations.title: Joining the Augusti to find Len
plotObservations.beat: At the Bakuto, Zanbato recruits Ryan with a favor-for-favor deal: help crush the Meta-Gang and the Augusti will help find Len. Zanbato warns Ghoul has been busted out of Private Security and will hunt Ryan.

plotObservations.title: Harbor ambush and the Len breakthrough
plotObservations.beat: Guarding an Augusti supply run at the old harbor, Ryan sees Len's crimson bathyspheres surface and realizes she is truly in New Rome. Ghoul and Sarin (Blower) ambush the shipment; Ryan fights them off solo, learning the Meta answer to a leader named Adam.

plotObservations.title: Battle won, then killed in the night
plotObservations.beat: With Zanbato's help Ryan defeats Ghoul and Sarin as Private Security fires on everyone; Zanbato reveals his real name is Jamie and promises to ask Vulcan about Len's tech. Back at his hotel, Ryan is killed by a firebomb rigged to his door, forcing a reload.

plotObservations.title: The divergence that breaks the Augusti path
plotObservations.beat: Reloading, Ryan changes his routine (shoots Ghoul, switches hotels, warns Wyvern). The changes cost him: Vulcan never calls, the Augusti path closes, and he meets the mysterious crimson-gowned woman at the Bakuto. He resolves to chase Len's tech through Rust Town's black market instead.

plotObservations.title: Rust Town, Paulie, and the Perfect Run vow
plotObservations.beat: Ryan enters walled Rust Town, finds Paulie who confirms Len operated there as the Underdiver before Private Security caught her and the Augusti broke her out. Paulie begs Ryan to destroy the child-abducting Meta-Gang; Ryan vows to grant it in his Perfect Run, then nukes a Mosquito Psycho for crushing his Plymouth.

plotObservations.title: Past fragment: the Wonderbox and Bloodstream
plotObservations.beat: Flashback to teen Ryan and Len in ruined Venezia finding an Alchemist Wonderbox with three Elixirs and the origin letter. Len's father Bloodstream, a blood-Psycho who calls Ryan 'Cesare,' seizes and drinks the Red Elixir; Ryan secretly pockets the Blue and Violet, resolving they must escape him.

plotObservations.title: Back on the Augusti path and the Made Men's table
plotObservations.beat: Ryan re-runs the loop cleanly, keeps the Augusti path, and detects an invisible flying watcher (possibly Geist). Jamie insists Ryan stay with his Made Men crew, introducing Ki-jung (Chitter) and Lanka, and promises to introduce him to Vulcan to locate Len.

plotObservations.title: Meeting Vulcan and the studio job
plotObservations.beat: At Vulcan's foundry Ryan meets Pluto (Augustus's death-touch sister) hunting the vigilante killing Made Men, and impresses capo Vulcan, a bomb-loving girl Genius who dangles access to Len. She assigns Ryan's crew to trash Star Studios and sabotage 'Wyvern's Flight II'.

plotObservations.title: The studio raid and the assassin's third strike
plotObservations.beat: The crew floods Star Studios with Chitter's rats and flees without a fight. Back home, the invisible glass-controlling assassin detonates the house, killing Ki-jung and Lanka, then beheads Ryan with a storm of glass shards, resetting the loop. Ryan resolves to hunt the killer before Len.

plotObservations.title: Blackthorn's contract and Len's name
plotObservations.beat: Ryan takes Wyvern's referral to Il Migliore and meets Enrique Manada (Blackthorn), who reveals Len's full identity, her Dynamis-linked custody, and offers a five-year contract, clean slate, and reunion in exchange for good behavior and Elixir research, plus a rebrand to 'Timelord'.

plotObservations.title: The corporate seminar and Atom Cat
plotObservations.beat: Ryan endures a soul-crushing Il Migliore internship, plants trackers to hack Dynamis's systems, and befriends Atom Cat, learning Adam's Meta-Gang is now disciplined with lieutenants Psyshock, Acid Rain and Frank the Mad. The two ditch the seminar to hunt the Meta.

plotObservations.title: The orphanage standoff
plotObservations.beat: Ryan and Atom Cat find a Rust Town orphanage-shelter run by children under a hidden 'Mama.' Psyshock, Mosquito and Mongrel arrive to abduct kids small enough for a bunker; Psyshock recognizes Ryan as 'Cesare.' The standoff erupts and Vulcan crashes in to kill Ryan for spurning her.

plotObservations.title: Saving the orphanage and the bunker clue
plotObservations.beat: Ryan kills Psyshock, Atom Cat kills Mongrel, and Wyvern arrives to swat Mosquito and capture Vulcan (revealed as Jasmine; Wyvern is Laura). Dying Mosquito reveals Adam seeks a robot-guarded bunker below the Junkyard needing child-sized entrants. Ryan also detects a rival hacker's backdoor in Dynamis.

plotObservations.title: Vulcan released and the insider theory
plotObservations.beat: At the hospital Enrique reveals Hector orders Vulcan freed to avoid war with Augustus, enraging Wyvern, who reveals Vulcan is Jasmine, her ex-partner turned defector. Atom Cat argues an insider in Dynamis is arming the Meta with knock-off Elixirs; then word comes Sarin massacred Zanbato/Jamie and his crew at the docks.

plotObservations.title: Confronting the Shroud
plotObservations.beat: Ryan tracks the hacker to a hidden server safehouse in the ship graveyard and unmasks the Shroud, a Carnival glass-Genome who killed him twice. Shroud explains he targets the Augusti's Bliss empire and Meta, offers cooperation for a non-lethal path, knows where Len is, and coldly suggests Len never contacted Ryan by choice.

plotObservations.title: Acid Rain and Len's return
plotObservations.beat: A Dynamis DNA tracker leads the Meta to the safehouse: Psyshock (somehow revived) and Acid Rain ambush them under an acid downpour. Acid Rain, sharing Ryan's power source, overpowers him. As he lies dying, Len appears in bronze diver-armor to save him, but Acid Rain's grenade-rain kills them both, ending the loop. Ryan resets to May 8th and sucker-punches Ghoul anew.

plotObservations.title: The pact with the Shroud
plotObservations.beat: In a fresh loop Ryan brings Ghoul's living skull to the Shroud, torturing intel from Ghoul with a Hercules Elixir: the Junkyard bunker is robot-guarded and Adam sees it as 'the future,' and Psyshock secretly runs the Meta's Elixir supply. Shroud reveals Len is the Underdiver in the Vavilov basin, deduces Ryan peeks across timelines, and strikes a pact: no Augusti assassinations for three weeks while Ryan destroys the Ischia Bliss lab.

plotObservations.title: Len's origin under the sea
plotObservations.beat: Flashback: young Len drinks the Blue Elixir to try to cure Bloodstream, gaining water-Genius powers and building a red bathysphere in a fugue. Bloodstream nearly strangles her for taking 'his' power but restrains himself; Ryan kisses her. In the present, Len hides in her deep-sea base, secretly eavesdropping on Ryan via chronoradio, longing for him yet afraid to face him.

plotObservations.title: Pluto's mark and Vulcan's offer
plotObservations.beat: On the Augusti path, Ryan finally beats Luigi's truth-telling by ambushing him with a hockey stick beforehand. He meets Pluto, Augustus's sister, who senses he is 'marked' across loops and threatens death if he disobeys. Vulcan, warmed by Ryan's engineering insight and a gifted A-bomb, offers to arrange a meeting with the Underdiver, and Shroud confirms the orphanage was saved.

plotObservations.title: Pluto's inspection and the brain-car
plotObservations.beat: Pluto surprise-inspects Jamie's crew with Cancel (Greta) and Sparrow. Cancel nullifies Ryan's time-stop, and Pluto's death-sense reads him as 300+ years old. Cornered, Ryan sells a cover lie that he hops parallel universes and fuses with his other selves; his synthetic brain-driven car is exposed but he passes on probation, assigned to Vulcan, who offers a lavish contract and a ride to Len.

plotObservations.title: The reunion with Len
plotObservations.beat: Vulcan flies Ryan to Len's deep-sea commune. Len, gaunt and medicated, admits she avoided him for two years: his looping-warped mind reopens her trauma and she blames him for leading the Carnival to kill Bloodstream. She refuses his offered hand to leave together, choosing to keep building her undersea refuge for orphans. Ryan's main quest ends in heartbreak.

plotObservations.title: Aftermath and the duplicator reveal
plotObservations.beat: Hollowed by the rejection, Ryan is comforted by Jamie, who invites him to a Genome party (warning him off Vamp and Livia). The Shroud ambushes Ryan to report: Psyshock is a duplicator like Bloodstream, and Ryan must reach drug-boss Bacchus (Andreas Torque) to infiltrate the Bliss operation. Ryan recommits to his side quests: clear the Meta and destroy the superlab.

plotObservations.title: Vulcan's assistant and the Killer Seven
plotObservations.beat: Working as Vulcan's weapons-review assistant, Ryan deduces her Genius is narrow 'weapon creation' and hears her bitter history as Wyvern's sidelined 'brain.' He meets the Killer Seven (Mortimer, Sparrow, Greta/Cancel, and Fortuna the lucky), empties his entire arsenal at Fortuna to no effect, then bypasses her luck in frozen time to cut her hair as a trophy. Vulcan tempts him with power-enhancing armor and orders an assault on the Meta-Gang.

plotObservations.title: The Rust Town assault turns into a massacre
plotObservations.beat: Ryan and Fortuna clear the Junkyard's outskirts in a chaotic firefight, but the Meta's true forces spring the trap: the Land collapses all of Rust Town with terrain-fusion geokinesis, a Mechron warmech piloted by Psyshock bombards the district, and Acid Rain counterattacks. The Augusti force is annihilated, Ryan's car destroyed again, and Psyshock corners him. Ryan chooses to reset (loop ~9), now knowing where Len is and that the Meta hold Mechron tech.

plotObservations.title: The crimes of Augustus
plotObservations.beat: A past fragment: Leo the Living Sun bids farewell to the Costa refugee farm as the Carnival heads north on Pythia's counsel. That night Jupiter Augustus, an invulnerable ivory god-warlord, massacres the entire community, killing Bruno Costa to erase the 'paradox' of a blade that can cut anything and butchering Julie in her garden. In the barn's hidden cellar he finds their toddler Giulia, a second-generation Genome, and spares her because her eyes recall his own daughter.

plotObservations.title: The suicide run into the Junkyard
plotObservations.beat: Fed up after the Meta wrecked his car three times and abduct children, Ryan mounts a Rampage-fueled one-man suicide raid: he trucks Ghoul, drives into the Junkyard chained to a facehugger missile that endlessly chases Acid Rain, kills Mosquito and Mongrel, and breaches the Mechron blast door. Inside he discovers the 'bunker' is a Mechron weapons facility, not a shelter.

plotObservations.title: The rampage and the plushie unleashed
plotObservations.beat: Ryan slaughters a room of Meta Psychos, unleashing his uncontrollable killer-rabbit plushie when overwhelmed. Descending deeper he reads the facility map (labs, robot production, orbital comms) and grasps the Meta's plan: seize Mechron's dormant robot army to conquer New Rome. He kills Psyshock, only to learn Psyshock reincarnates into brainwired thralls, then confronts the metal giant Frank the Mad.

plotObservations.title: Bites the Dust and Len's answer
plotObservations.beat: Cornered between Frank and the plushie, Ryan meets Meta leader Adam the Ogre, who reveals his cannibalism and carbon-alloy invulnerability. Adam kills Ryan by dangling a hostage teen Ryan can't abandon; Ryan detonates his belt and resets. In the new loop he confesses everything to Len over the Chronoradio, offering to vanish from her life. She finally answers: 'Meet me at the orphanage.'

plotObservations.title: Knight of Faith: Ryan bares his soul
plotObservations.beat: At the orphanage, Ryan finally explains his power to Len in full: the Purple World, Schrodinger's-cat bilocation, that saving means suicide, that he may be 500-800 years old and has searched for her the whole time. Len, wracked with guilt, weeps for his loneliness but flinches from his touch, still unable to feel safe near him. She asks him to stay the night rather than keep to his old timing.

plotObservations.title: Change of plans and the Meta's true goal
plotObservations.beat: Waking to the cat Eugene-Henry, Ryan reassures a frightened Len about the brain-car and hands over his A-bomb to earn her trust. He learns her origin (jailed by Dynamis for attacking a chemical plant, freed by Vulcan into drug-running) and briefs Shroud on the Mechron bunker. Shroud confirms Mechron is dead, begs him to keep the cache secret from the Augusti, and lets slip Leo is coming, meaning Ryan has ~3 weeks before Leo and Augustus clash.

plotObservations.title: Black Swan: killing Psyshock for good
plotObservations.beat: Ryan finds Len in a medicated near-catatonic state but she suits up to defend the orphans. When Psyshock attacks, Ryan reveals his trump: Cancel, whose negation lets her permanently kill the body-jumper (and Mongrel and Mosquito) before he can transfer. Ryan and Len evacuate the orphans via the sewers; Len hints her Chronoradio navigation insight might finally help his power, and Shroud reveals his search for the teenage Giulia Costa.

plotObservations.title: Hit and Run: the Meta vanish
plotObservations.beat: With Psyshock dead for good (his death freed his brainwashed thralls citywide), Ryan's optimized Augusti loop sails smoothly until the Meta torch the Junkyard and flee north. Ryan alone grasps the trick: they're slipping away by the bunker's hidden sea route to keep the Mechron cache secret. Torn between committing to a Perfect Run (saving hundreds) and preserving his fragile real progress with Len, he's left agonizing over mutually exclusive consequences.

plotObservations.title: Pre-Party: the guests assemble
plotObservations.beat: At Jamie's Genome house party Ryan meets Fortuna's new boyfriend Mathias Martel, whom he recognizes as the Shroud in civilian guise, and her sweet adopted sister Narcinia 'Ceres' Veran, who makes animals from her blood. Ryan and Shroud both realize Narcinia is the lost Giulia Costa, Augustus's stolen hostage; Shroud confirms 'it's her' with murder in his eyes. Talk surfaces Felix's estrangement and the mysterious 'Livia.'

plotObservations.title: Color Rave and the wager
plotObservations.beat: Ryan DJs the rave (brain-in-a-jar, Narcinia's mushrooms, goat fights) as Vulcan reports the Meta escaped by Mechron submarine after Dynamis killstole them. He learns Narcinia works Bacchus's Ischia Bliss op, and meets Livia Augusti/Minerva, Augustus's reality-seeing daughter to whom he is uniquely invisible. On a bet to show her something no timeline predicts, Ryan and Vulcan raid Dynamis HQ, clashing with Enrique on the twentieth floor.

plotObservations.title: The War of the Suit
plotObservations.beat: Vulcan crashes her stealth mech into the twentieth floor of Dynamis HQ so Ryan can steal a purple cashmere suit. Confronted by Enrique/Blackthorn and his squad, Ryan calmly strips and dresses in the suit mid-standoff, short-circuiting Enrique's mind with the sheer stupidity of it. A running gunfight erupts (Enrique revealed as a growth-boosting plant-controller) before the pair escape by sea, winning Livia's bet. Vulcan takes Ryan home as her lover.

plotObservations.title: The Olympians
plotObservations.beat: After a night with Vulcan (real name Jasmine Sharif), who probes the haunted plushie and shares her Red Flux/Red Dimension theory, the pair fly to Mount Augustus. Ryan meets the Augusti high command, the Olympians, and their brutal lightning-emperor leader Augustus/Janus, summoned by Livia. He sees Narcinia among Augustus's family and the priest Bacchus, who claims to have seen God through Bliss.

plotObservations.title: Court of the Lightning King
plotObservations.beat: Augustus's court convenes. Mercury's necromancer exposes Ryan's true name (Cesare Sabino, Bloodstream's 'son'); Livia vouches for him and Pluto keeps her mark on him, sparing his life. Augustus orders the whole Meta-Gang exterminated, promotes Jamie/Zanbato to replace the retiring Mercury, and tasks Vulcan to harden Ischia's Bliss sanctuary. Livia privately admits Ryan is the one blind spot in her reality-sight, and warns him off her own ambitions ('Here be dragons').

plotObservations.title: Mechron's Last Stand
plotObservations.beat: Flashback: at the final battle of Sarajevo, Leo Hargraves rallies 500+ Genomes of the Anti-Mechron Front, networked by Pythia, and drops Mechron's forcefield with a supernova beam. Amid the machine war Mechron launches his twin orbital weapons; the Cossack downs the Kujata but a Mechron-made gravity-controlling Red dragon delays Leo and the Bahamut escapes to orbit. Pythia redirects Leo to the fortress, warning something worse than the satellite waits inside: 'It's all black.'

plotObservations.title: The Darkness Beyond
plotObservations.beat: Inside the fortress-collider Leo confronts a broken, hateful Mechron, who refuses surrender and opens a gate meant for the Blue World / Akashic Records. It instead breaches onto the Darkness Beyond, an eye-like void entity that erases Mechron atom by atom and begins consuming reality. Leo collapses the fortress by going supernova, sealing the gate at the cost of near-death. He wakes days later: the war is won, but Pythia is brain-damaged, the Bahamut lost, and her USB names Bloodstream as humanity's top threat.

plotObservations.title: Progress Made
plotObservations.beat: Back in the present, Ryan cleans up the party wreck and learns Jamie proposed to Ki-jung and will reinvest his new Mercury division into Rust Town charity. Over the Chronoradio, Len (warming toward him, hinting he could visit the orphans) proposes the consciousness-transfer plan to let someone else remember across loops, but it needs Mechron's bunker tech. Ryan refuses to give the Augusti bunker access and accepts this good loop still won't be perfect.

plotObservations.title: The Ghost of Drug Island
plotObservations.beat: Laying low on Vulcan's orders, Ryan spends the weekend with Jasmine designing his power armor and a scheme to trap his own 'Violet Flux' to boost his power. She reveals Dynamis's decade-long mind-uploading immortality project (brain scans into Tyrano's cloned bodies), and Ryan realizes combining it with Len's and Jasmine's tech could let him carry a companion across loops, giving him hope. They fly to the miasma-choked Ischia superlab for Livia's defense inspection, where Livia introduces the ghost Geist as a sentry and warns that many alternate realities now end in her own sudden death. Ryan, planning to blow up the island to settle his debt with Shroud, sizes up how to bring the fortress down.

plotObservations.title: Return of the Corpo
plotObservations.beat: Locked out of the Ischia facility's secrets, Ryan passes the inspection playing knucklebones with Geist and Mortimer, learning Geist's origin, that Ceres is the sole Bliss cook, and that Bliss sterilizes ordinary users. Len calls with alarm, tremors from Rust Town and flying objects inbound on Ischia, then Blackthorn calls to gloat: as retaliation for the HQ raid, Don Hector has finally chosen war. Thirty Dynamis war helicopters and Il Migliore's elite (Wyvern, Windsweep, Devilry) descend on the island, demanding Quicksave and Jasmine surrender. Vulcan refuses, Wyvern transforms into a dragon, and the drug-lab battle erupts, exactly the destruction Ryan owes Shroud, so he sits back to watch.

plotObservations.title: Blood in the Water
plotObservations.beat: The Ischia battle erupts into chaos: Geist swats helicopters, Vulcan grapples the dragon-form Wyvern out to sea, and Ryan duels the newly-arrived Il Migliore pair, Reload and Wardrobe. He steals Reload's violet lightsaber and toys with the self-resurrecting hero, but Wardrobe's shifting costumes escalate until her unstable 'Augustus' guise blasts Ryan with imitation lightning that reaches him even inside stopped time, the exact threat Chitter once warned him about. As she readies a deadly 'Apocalypse Suit,' Len arrives in her underwater armor with skyscraper-sized water arms (mistaken for Neptune) and Augusti reinforcements race in on jet skis. Before Wardrobe can transform, Mortimer phases up and shoots her dead, winning his kill-count bet.

plotObservations.title: While Rome Burns
plotObservations.beat: Ryan reaches the Junkyard, blaming himself for leaving Mechron's bunker for the Meta to seize. He finds the five surviving Psychos (Adam, Frank, Acid Rain, Sarin, and the dirt-formed Land) holding a rock concert beneath the risen orbital-control tower as New Rome burns. Adam gloats that he tracked the sabotage back to Ryan/'Cesare,' reveals he is dying as his Elixir-abused powers go haywire, and that, denied a cure by Psyshock's death, he fired the Bahamut out of pure Jonestown spite, then threatens Len's underwater orphanage. Ryan attacks, unleashing the plushie on Acid Rain, blinding Adam, and killing the Land and Sarin, but is caught between Adam's chain and the Land and nearly force-fed an Elixir, until Vulcan, Lanka and Jamie crash in to rescue him.

plotObservations.title: Bad End
plotObservations.beat: Vulcan (temporarily allied with Wyvern), Jamie and Lanka fight the Meta until Augustus himself descends, moving through Ryan's stopped time. The invulnerable emperor kills Frank, savagely beats and captures Adam (to be crucified alive for killing his family), then destroys Mechron's bunker with a thunderbolt, obliterating the orbital tech, the Chronoradio plans' hardware, and Ryan's last hope of the consciousness-transfer plan. Ryan wakes in a Sorrento hospital to the loop's ruin: Len is dead, his car and the Chronoradio destroyed, and with Hector and Enrique gone the hardliner Alphonse now steers Dynamis toward a new war. Only the cat Schrodinger survived. Deciding he must finally change and stop relying on Len alone, Ryan chooses to trust Vulcan and reveals his secret: 'I can time-travel.'

plotObservations.title: Time and Again
plotObservations.beat: In Vulcan's makeshift lab, Jasmine seals Ryan into the purple power armor for a desperate gambit: using it to open a physical rift to the Purple World so she can time-travel with him rather than be erased by the reset. They share a last kiss and pop-culture banter, and she makes him promise never to replace her or forget her. Ryan activates his power; violet particles multiply uncontrollably and pull him bodily into the Purple World, where he witnesses a vision of the homo-novus founders and their crashed craft, the color-dimension cosmology, a plushie meadow, and a planet-sized god-entity. Then the loop resets to May 8, 2020, in his restored car. Jasmine didn't make it through, but a haunting recording of his rooftop talk with Len plays over the Chronoradio. Ryan vows to keep his promise and complete the Perfect Run.

plotObservations.title: Past Fragment: How to Tame Your Plushie
plotObservations.beat: A flashback to an earlier loop reveals the plushie's origin. A younger Ryan, learning Genius tech from his cyborg roommate Alchemo ('Braindead'), builds a cute rabbit plushie as a probe to send through a mini particle accelerator into the Purple World, hoping to enable his car's dimensional time-travel. The accelerator runs in reverse, frying the hardware and anchoring an alien tentacled entity inside the toy. The possessed plushie kills Alchemo on sight (repeatedly), spares the gynoid Doll/Tea and children, strings up human victims, and multiplies exponentially when happy, overrunning Firenze in one loop. Ryan resets each time and finally tames it by flipping its switch off on reload, keeping it as a last-resort weapon he dares not destroy lest he free what lives inside. It watches over his sleep, pledging eternal friendship.

plotObservations.title: Route Split
plotObservations.beat: A new loop resets everyone's memories, wiping Ryan's progress with Jasmine (Vulcan doesn't remember him). Choosing to avoid an Augusti run so soon after losing her, Ryan takes the Dynamis path instead: he pitches Wyvern to join Il Migliore and warns Shroud that Adam is after the orbital Bahamut. Shroud, shaken that Ryan knows the secret name, believes him and postpones the Carnival's Augusti strikes to prioritize the bunker crisis, urging Ryan to infiltrate Dynamis and report back. Ryan then notices his cat Schrodinger has gained a teleport power from Violet-dimension exposure. Finally Len, who overheard the time-travel recording, radios him live: she now knows he can time-travel, and asks why he didn't just re-run their reconciliation. Ryan explains he wants their bond to be true, not manufactured, and heads to the orphanage where Len agrees to meet him.

plotObservations.title: Chance Meetings
plotObservations.beat: Ryan meets Enrique 'Blackthorn' Manada and lays out his evidence that a Dynamis insider armed the Meta-Gang. Enrique proves clean: he fires the negligent drone-handler, deduces a board-level traitor may be the sponsor, and takes the unstable-but-useful Ryan into Il Migliore's junior division on a six-month supervised trial, granting Ryan's terms (keep his name, never touch the Underdiver). Ryan adopts the hapless hero-hopeful Timmy 'the Panda' as his sidekick, naming their team 'Quicksave the Pandas.' Driving home he learns Dynamis surveils Len's undersea base (likely how Adam found it) and resolves to get her real antidepressant treatment. On Sol Street a chance encounter throws him together with the haughty Fortuna and the intrigued Livia Augusti, whose Purple-World sight cannot perceive Ryan or clearly see his teleporting cat Schrodinger. Ryan rebuffs Fortuna's demand for a ride and drives off, leaving Livia watching him with curiosity.

plotObservations.title: Fashion Disaster
plotObservations.beat: At Wardrobe's Il Migliore atelier, Yukiko designs Ryan's signature costume (dark-purple cashmere suit, clock-symbol scarf, silver-and-black mask) and 'Rambo Panda' for Timmy, while the practical Atom Cat resists a latex cat-suit. Ryan rallies Wardrobe, the Panda, and Atom Cat into an unsanctioned Rust Town patrol to test the costumes. En route Wardrobe explains her power copies the collective *idea* of a persona (not real abilities), that she can become the persona if worn too long, and that her 'Apocalypse Suit' could destroy the world, but she cannot copy the obscure Cancel, spoiling Ryan's plan against Psyshock. Atom Cat is revealed as Livia Augusti's brother and ex who broke with his family. Fortuna, obsessed after Ryan's rejection, spams him with 41 messages. Then a cryptic 'Unknown' texts 'The orange is in the hen house'; Ryan slams the brakes and replies as 'PlushieTamer,' racing back toward the orphanage.

plotObservations.title: A Gambling Man
plotObservations.beat: Ryan brings his patrol team (Wardrobe, Atom Cat, the Panda) plus Len to defend the Rust Town orphanage from Psyshock's raid. Rattled that someone sent him his private power-catchphrase ('the orange is in the hen house'), Ryan suspects Livia may retain loop memories. When Psyshock arrives with reinforcements (Rakshasa and a lizard-man), Ryan runs an audacious poker bluff, posing as Hector Manada's envoy, and extracts the full conspiracy: the Meta approached Don Hector for a knockoff supply, never intended to hit the Augusti, are secretly unearthing Mechron's bunker, and Psyshock's 'second project' is a mind-transfer brain-scan (workable only between closely related brains). Shroud records it all invisibly. His trap sprung, Ryan sucker-punches Psyshock as every window in the area shatters, launching the ambush.

plotObservations.title: The Future Past
